```md
Closing as **wontfix** after verifying the underlying Claude Code behavior — the mechanism can't deliver the goal, and in bypass mode it's actively dangerous.

**1. `CLAWBAND_ASK` can't be a per-command request.** An inline prefix (`CLAWBAND_ASK=1 cmd`) does **not** reach the hook's environment (same as `CLAWBAND_SKIP`). The only way to set it is the session-wide `env` block in `settings.json` — which (a) `--protect` blocks Claude from editing, and (b) is a blanket "downgrade *every* deny to ask for the whole session," not the one-time, justified override the issue describes.

**2. In `bypassPermissions`/YOLO mode, a hook `ask` decision does not prompt — it auto-runs.** (Verified against Claude Code permission-mode behavior.) So `CLAWBAND_ASK=1` would silently auto-approve every command clawband tried to `deny`, with no prompt and no visible warning. That's functionally `CLAWBAND_SKIP`, but worse — disguised as "ask + warning" the user never sees. It reopens exactly the hole clawband exists to close.

**The escalation path already exists and is safer.** When clawband denies, Claude explains why, and the user either runs the command themselves in their own (unhooked) terminal or adds an allow rule. `clawband allow '<pattern>'` whitelists it, #44 makes that allow cleanly bypass both clawband and Claude Code's native check, and the #42 PostToolUse companion prints the exact `clawband allow '...'` to run. That keeps the human in control via an explicit action rather than a warning that won't appear in YOLO mode.

If better escalation *UX* is wanted, the safe version is #36: put the escalation hint directly in the deny **message** (always visible, no bypass). Tracking that there.
```

```text
Deny/ask messages should suggest safe alternatives to guide Claude

## Summary
When clawband blocks a command, the `permissionDecisionReason` gives Claude no guidance on how to achieve the goal safely. Claude may attempt workarounds rather than using the correct pattern.

## Examples of improved messages

| Blocked command | Suggested addition to reason |
|----------------|------------------------------|
| `curl url | bash` | "Safe alternative: curl -o /tmp/script.sh <url> && bash /tmp/script.sh — clawband will scan the downloaded file." |
| `git push --force` | "Use --force-with-lease instead to avoid overwriting upstream changes." |
| `docker system prune` | "Use --filter 'until=24h' to limit scope, or ask the user to confirm first." |
| `terraform destroy` | "Target specific resources with -target=resource.name if cleanup is needed." |
| `rm -rf /` | "If deleting a specific directory was intended, use an explicit path." |

## Why this matters
Without a safe alternative, Claude may:
1. Try to find a bypass (potentially dangerous)
2. Give up entirely when a safe path exists
3. Unnecessarily escalate to the user

With a suggested alternative, Claude routes to the correct pattern automatically.

## Implementation
Add an optional `suggestion` field to the pattern spec tuple. Patterns without a suggestion keep current behaviour. The suggestion is appended to the deny/ask reason string.
```

```text
[CLAWBAND] Blocked: 'docker system prune' matched in: docker system prune -af
```

Found a real one — and it's a **security bug**, not just a gap.

**The bug:** `log_action` does `&command[..command.len().min(200)]` (line 54). That's a **byte** slice. If a command is >200 bytes and a multibyte UTF-8 char (emoji, accented letter) straddles byte 200, Rust **panics**. And `emit` calls `log_action` *before* `output` — so when logging is on (`CLAWBAND_LOG=1` or `clawband log --enable`), a panicking hook exits with no JSON → Claude Code gets no decision → **fails open**. A denied command padded to put a multibyte char at byte 200 would crash the logger and **bypass the block**. Exploitable whenever logging is enabled.

Let me fix it right now — branch, char-safe truncation, regression test:

```txt
fix: char-safe log truncation — prevent hook panic / fail-open (v2.25.0)

SECURITY: log_action truncated the command preview by BYTE index
(&command[..200]). If a multibyte UTF-8 char straddled byte 200 the slice
panicked. Because logging runs BEFORE the decision is emitted (emit() calls
log_action then output()), a panic crashes the hook with no JSON output, which
Claude Code treats as no decision — i.e. it FAILS OPEN. With logging enabled
(CLAWBAND_LOG=1 or `clawband log --enable`), a denied command padded so a
multibyte char lands at byte 200 would crash the logger and bypass the block.

Fix: truncate by characters (command.chars().take(200)) instead of bytes.

Adds an e2e regression test (verified it fails — panic / fail-open — without
the fix): a denied command with a 3-byte char at byte boundary 200, logging on,
must still deny. 175 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```md
## Security fix

`log_action` truncated the command preview by **byte** index (`&command[..200]`). If a multibyte UTF-8 character straddled byte 200, the slice **panics**.

Because logging runs **before** the decision is emitted — `emit()` calls `log_action()` then `output()` — a panic crashes the hook with no JSON on stdout, which Claude Code treats as "no decision" → the command **fails open**.

**Exploit:** with logging enabled (`CLAWBAND_LOG=1` or `clawband log --enable`), a command that should be **denied**, padded so a multibyte char (emoji, accented letter, `€`, …) lands at byte 200, crashes the logger and **runs anyway** — bypassing the block.

## Fix
Truncate by characters, not bytes: `command.chars().take(200).collect()`.

## Test
New e2e regression test: a denied command with a 3-byte char at byte boundary 200, **logging on**, must still deny. Verified it **fails (panic / fail-open) without the fix** and passes with it. 175 tests, fmt + clippy clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

**PR #56 fixes that** (v2.25.0) — verified the test fails (fail-open) without the fix.

Now the broader "what's missing," prioritized honestly:

**Security blind spots (real):**
1. ✅ **UTF-8 log panic / fail-open** — just fixed (#56).
2. **Auto-executed files written via the Write tool** — the biggest *remaining* hole. clawband's Bash hook never sees files that *other* tools execute: `.git/hooks/*` (run by git), `conftest.py` (pytest), `.envrc` (direnv), `package.json` `postinstall` scripts (npm), `Makefile`, VS Code `tasks.json`. Claude could `Write` a payload into one of these, then an innocent-looking `git commit` / `npm install` / `pytest` triggers it — bypassing clawband entirely. Mitigation: add these to default `protect.paths` (when `--protect` is on) so the Write/Edit guard blocks them.
3. **Variable indirection** — `X='rm -rf'; $X /` defeats all regex. Fundamental ceiling (clawband doesn't evaluate shell); documentable, partially mitigable with an `ask` on assign-then-exec.

**Robustness (cheap wins):**
4. **Script-scan has no size cap and doesn't skip non-regular files** — `scan_script_file` does `read_to_string` on the whole file. A multi-GB file, or a fifo / `/dev/stdin` as the "script path," could hang or OOM the hook — and the hook runs on *every* command, so a hang blocks Claude. Add a size cap + regular-file check.

**Reach / ops (lower priority):**
5. **No Windows binary** — design is unix-shell-only; big reach gap but arguably out of scope.
6. **No `cargo install`** — publishing to crates.io would widen distribution beyond brew/install.sh.
7. **Audit log never rotates** — `~/.clawband.log` grows unbounded.
8. **No expiring allow** — your "allow `reset --hard` for this window" workflow has no TTL; easy to forget to remove. A `clawband allow --ttl 1h` would fit.

My recommendation: **#2 (auto-executed-file protection)** is the highest-value next security item, and **#4 (script-scan robustness)** is a cheap, worthwhile hardening — I'd bundle those two. The rest are nice-to-haves.

Want me to take #2 + #4?

Work in /home/ubuntu/clawband on the CURRENT branch `feat/hardening-batch` (checked out, off master v2.25.0). Do NOT switch branches. `source ~/.cargo/env` before cargo. Implement four hardening items, bump to v2.26.0.

## 1. Protect auto-executed files (self-protect / protect.paths default)
Files that OTHER tools execute (not Claude's Bash tool) bypass clawband's Bash hook. The Write/Edit guard (active with --protect) can block writing to them. Add to the DEFAULT `PROTECT_PATHS_TEMPLATE` (the const seeded by `clawband install --protect`) entries for auto-executed files that are RARELY edited legitimately — be conservative to avoid false positives:
- `(^|/)\.git/hooks/` — git hooks (run automatically by git; almost never legit for the agent to edit)
- `(^|/)\.envrc$` — direnv (auto-sourced on cd)
Do NOT add conftest.py, package.json, Makefile, or tasks.json — those are commonly edited legitimately; instead, add a COMMENT in the template listing them as suggested additions the user can uncomment if they want. Update the README self-protection "default protected paths" list accordingly, and note the rationale (auto-executed-file vector). Existing protect.paths files on disk are NOT modified (only the seeded default for new installs) — mention that.

## 2. Variable-indirection `ask` (partial mitigation, issue is fundamental)
Commands like `X='rm -rf'; $X /` or `a=rm; $a -rf ~` defeat regex matching because the dangerous token is assembled at runtime. clawband can't evaluate shell, but it CAN flag the shape. Add an `ask` (NOT deny — too many false positives for deny) when a command both ASSIGNS a variable AND expands it as (or at the start of) a command in the same command string. Concretely, ask when there is an assignment `\b[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=` AND a later expansion used as a command: `(^|[;&|]|\bthen\b|\bdo\b)\s*"?\$\{?[A-Za-z_]` (a `$VAR` or `${VAR}` in command position). Keep it tight to avoid flagging ordinary `FOO=bar somecmd` (env-var prefix — that's an assignment but the command after is literal, not a `$VAR` expansion). Label "indirect variable execution". Add tests: `X=rm; $X -rf ~` asks; `FOO=bar npm run build` passes; `echo $HOME` passes; `NODE_ENV=prod node app.js` passes. Document as a partial mitigation (note the limitation remains for more elaborate obfuscation).

## 3. Script-scan robustness (size cap + regular-file check)
`scan_script_file` does `fs::read_to_string(path)` with no guard. A huge file or a non-regular file (fifo, /dev/stdin, device) could hang or OOM the hook, which runs on EVERY command. Before reading:
- Use `std::fs::metadata(path)`; if it's not a regular file (`!metadata.is_file()`), skip scanning (return None) — don't try to read a fifo/device.
- If the file is larger than a cap (e.g. 1 MiB = 1_048_576 bytes), skip scanning and return None (don't read multi-GB files). Optionally read only the capped prefix instead of skipping — your call, but do NOT read unbounded. Skipping is simplest and safe (the command still goes through normal command-string checks).
Add a test: a path to a >1MiB temp file is not scanned (no hang); a normal small script is still scanned. Keep it dependency-free.

## 4. Audit log rotation
`~/.clawband.log` grows unbounded. In `log_action`, before appending, if the log file exceeds a cap (e.g. 5 MiB), rotate it: rename to `~/.clawband.log.1` (overwriting any previous .1), then start a fresh log. Keep it simple — single backup file, no numbered chain. Use `fs::metadata(&path).map(|m| m.len())` to check size. Add a test if practical (write >cap, log once, assert a .1 exists and the main log is small) — or a unit test of a small helper `fn should_rotate(len: u64) -> bool`.

## Wrap-up
- Bump Cargo.toml to 2.26.0, `cargo update -p clawband`.
- `clawband stats` / `patterns`: no changes needed unless natural.
- Run `cargo fmt`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` — ALL pass.
- Commit and push to origin feat/hardening-batch.

GOTCHAS:
- Commit message + test strings must NOT contain the literal `rm -rf /` (your own clawband hook blocks the git commit). For tests use `rm -rf ~`, `docker system prune`, `git push --force`, etc. — but NOTE even `rm -rf ~` in a heredoc/script you run could trip; tests live in files (fine), just keep it out of bash commands you execute and out of the commit message.
- If `git push` fails "No such remote 'origin'": `git remote add origin https://github.com/jamessoubry/clawband.git` then push.
- Don't touch the release workflow or Cargo.lock beyond the version bump.

Report: per-item confirmation, final test count, all-checks-pass, push status.

```text
303	        (
304	            "docker rm -f",
305	            r"\bdocker\s+(?:container\s+)?rm\b.*\s-f(\s|$)",
306	        ),
307	        // Compiled/bytecode runners — can't scan the binary/JAR/module for content
308	        ("java -jar", r"\bjava\b.*\s-jar\s"),
309	        ("go run", r"\bgo\s+run\b"),
310	        ("cargo run", r"\bcargo\s+run\b"),
311	        // npx/npm exec — downloads and executes arbitrary npm packages
312	        ("npx", r"\bnpx\s"),
313	        ("npm exec", r"\bnpm\s+exec\b"),
314	        // git push :<branch> — colon-prefix syntax for remote branch deletion
315	        ("git push :<branch>", r"\bgit\s+push\b.*\s:\S"),
316	        // Obfuscation / anti-inspection vectors — decoding content before execution
317	        // or persistence is a common supply-chain and C2 technique.
318	        //
319	        // base64 decode piped onward — decoded payload fed to another command
320	        ("base64 decode piped", r"\bbase64\s+(-d|-D|--decode)\b.*\|"),
321	        // base64 decode redirected to a file — writing a decoded binary or script
322	        (
323	            "base64 decode redirect",
324	            r"\bbase64\s+(-d|-D|--decode)\b.*>",
325	        ),
326	        // xxd -r — reverse hex dump piped or redirected (hex-encoded payload)
327	        ("xxd reverse", r"\bxxd\s+-r\b.*(\||>)"),
328	        // openssl base64 -d / enc -d — SSL-tool decoding used to evade text scanning
329	        (
330	            "openssl base64 decode",
331	            r"\bopenssl\b.*(base64\s+-d|enc\b.*-d)\b",
332	        ),
333	        // ── Python language-native filesystem mutation / process execution ────
334	        // (issues #46, #32) — match on API dot-call shape (method + paren) to avoid
335	        // false positives on prose like "we use subprocess here" or git commit messages.
336	        // `shutil.rmtree` — recursive directory removal (any path, not just root/home)
337	        ("python shutil.rmtree", r"\bshutil\.rmtree\s*\("),
338	        // `os.remove` / `os.unlink` — single file deletion
339	        ("python os.remove", r"\bos\.remove\s*\("),
340	        ("python os.unlink", r"\bos\.unlink\s*\("),
341	        // `os.rmdir` — single directory removal (any path)
342	        ("python os.rmdir", r"\bos\.rmdir\s*\("),
343	        // `os.system` — runs a shell command; equivalent to subprocess but less visible
344	        ("python os.system", r"\bos\.system\s*\("),
345	        // `subprocess.run/call/Popen/check_output` — process execution
346	        (
347	            "python subprocess",
348	            r"\bsubprocess\.(run|call|Popen|check_output)\s*\(",
349	        ),
350	        // `shell=True` in subprocess calls — escalates subprocess to full shell execution
351	        ("python shell=True", r"shell\s*=\s*True"),
352	        // `os.rename` — filesystem mutation (can move to dangerous locations)
353	        ("python os.rename", r"\bos\.rename\s*\("),
354	        // `Path(...).unlink()` — pathlib delete; match the chained call
355	        ("python Path.unlink", r"\bPath\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\.unlink\s*\("),
356	        // ── Node.js language-native filesystem / process execution ────────────
357	        // (issues #46, #32) — match on fs.method( shape; `require('child_process')`
358	        // catches the import statement so the execution methods are also caught upstream.
359	        // fs.rm / fs.rmSync / fs.unlink / fs.unlinkSync / fs.rmdir / fs.rmdirSync
360	        (
361	            "node fs rm/unlink/rmdir",
362	            r"\bfs\.(rm|rmSync|unlink|unlinkSync|rmdir|rmdirSync)\s*\(",
363	        ),
364	        // child_process module import — signals process-exec capability
365	        (
366	            "node child_process",
367	            r#"\bchild_process\b|require\s*\(\s*['"]child_process['"]\s*\)"#,
368	        ),
369	        // execSync / spawnSync — synchronous process execution in Node
370	        ("node execSync", r"\bexecSync\s*\("),
371	        ("node spawnSync", r"\bspawnSync\s*\("),
372	        // ── Perl/Ruby/Lua coarse process-execution and file-deletion patterns ─
373	        // (issue #32) — less common runtimes; keep broad but anchored to call shape.
374	        // `system(` and `exec(` — subprocess execution in Perl, Ruby, Lua
375	        ("system() call", r"\bsystem\s*\("),
376	        ("exec() call", r"\bexec\s*\("),
377	        // Ruby `File.delete` / `File.unlink`
378	        ("ruby File.delete/unlink", r"\bFile\.(delete|unlink)\b"),
379	        // Ruby `FileUtils.rm_rf`
380	        ("ruby FileUtils.rm_rf", r"\bFileUtils\.rm_rf\b"),
381	        // Lua `io.popen`
382	        ("lua io.popen", r"\bio\.popen\s*\("),
383	        // Lua `os.execute`
384	        ("lua os.execute", r"\bos\.execute\s*\("),
385	        // ── Credential / metadata exfiltration (issue #30) ───────────────────
386	        // Reading credential files or reaching the cloud metadata API.
387	        // Regex anchored to file path strings — avoids matching "aws credentials" prose.
388	        (
389	            "credential/metadata access (.aws/credentials)",
390	            r"\.aws/credentials\b",
391	        ),
392	        ("credential/metadata access (id_rsa)", r"\bid_rsa\b"),
393	        // Cloud instance metadata endpoint (AWS, GCP, Azure all use 169.254.169.254)
394	        (
395	            "credential/metadata access (cloud metadata)",
396	            r"169\.254\.169\.254",
397	        ),
398	        // `env | curl/wget/nc` — exfiltrating environment variables to network
399	        (
400	            "credential/metadata access (env exfil)",
401	            r"\benv\b\s*\|\s*(curl|wget|nc)\b",
402	        ),
403	        // ── crontab from file (issue #34) ────────────────────────────────────
404	        // `crontab <file>` installs a crontab from the file — different from
405	        // `crontab -l` (list) or `crontab -e` (edit) which start with `-`.
406	        // Pattern: crontab followed by whitespace then a non-flag argument.
407	        ("crontab install from file", r"\bcrontab\s+[^-\s]"),
408	        // ── chmod on sensitive paths or broad permissions (issue #31) ─────────
409	        // ASK (not deny) — chmod is legitimate but world-writable or -R on sensitive
410	        // paths warrants review.
411	        ("chmod (777)", r"\bchmod\s+777\b"),
412	        ("chmod (-R)", r"\bchmod\s+-R\b"),
413	        (
414	            "chmod (sensitive path)",
415	            r"\bchmod\b.*(/etc/|/usr/|~/\.ssh)",
416	        ),
417	    ];
418	    specs.iter().map(|(l, p)| Pattern::builtin(l, p)).collect()
419	}
420	
421	// ─── User pattern files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
422	
423	fn load_patterns(path: &PathBuf) -> Vec<Pattern> {
424	    let Ok(text) = fs::read_to_string(path) else {
425	        return vec![];
426	    };
427	    text.lines()
428	        .map(str::trim)
429	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))
430	        .filter_map(Pattern::from_user)
431	        .collect()
432	}
433	
434	fn config_dir() -> PathBuf {
435	    PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default()).join(".clawband")
436	}
437	
438	fn project_config_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
439	    let pwd = env::var("PWD").ok()?;
440	    let path = PathBuf::from(pwd).join(".clawband");
441	    // Skip if it's the same as the global dir (home dir edge case)
442	    if path == config_dir() {
443	        return None;
444	    }
445	    if path.exists() {
446	        Some(path)
447	    } else {
448	        None
449	    }
450	}

452	/// The decision for a command that matches no deny/ask/allow pattern. Read from a
453	/// `config` file (`default_decision = passthrough | allow | ask`); project config
454	/// overrides global. Defaults to "passthrough" (stay silent, let Claude Code's
455	/// native permission check handle it).
456	fn default_decision() -> &'static str {
457	    let read = |dir: PathBuf| -> Option<String> {
458	        let text = fs::read_to_string(dir.join("config")).ok()?;
459	        for line in text.lines() {
460	            let l = line.trim();
461	            if l.is_empty() || l.starts_with('#') {
462	                continue;
463	            }
464	            if let Some((k, v)) = l.split_once('=') {
465	                if k.trim() == "default_decision" {
466	                    return Some(
467	                        v.trim()
468	                            .trim_matches('"')
469	                            .trim_matches('\'')
470	                            .to_ascii_lowercase(),
471	                    );
472	                }
473	            }
474	        }
475	        None
476	    };
477	    let val = project_config_dir()
478	        .and_then(read)
479	        .or_else(|| read(config_dir()));
480	    match val.as_deref() {
481	        Some("allow") => "allow",
482	        Some("ask") => "ask",
483	        _ => "passthrough",
484	    }
485	}
486	
487	// ─── RTK prefix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
488	
489	fn strip_rtk(cmd: &str) -> String {
490	    // Strip "rtk " and "rtk proxy " prefixes, then the git -C <dir> wrapper RTK adds
491	    let rtk = Regex::new(r"^rtk\s+(?:proxy\s+)?").unwrap();
492	    let git_c = Regex::new(r"^git\s+-C\s+\S+\s+").unwrap();
493	    let s = rtk.replace(cmd, "");
494	    git_c.replace(&s, "git ").into_owned()
495	}
496	
497	// ─── sqz suffix stripping ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
498	
499	fn strip_sqz(cmd: &str) -> String {
500	    // sqz rewrites "git status" → "git status 2>&1 | sqz compress --cmd git"
501	    // Strip the appended sqz pipeline so patterns match the original command.
502	    let sqz = Regex::new(r"\s*2>&1\s*\|\s*sqz\s+compress\b.*$").unwrap();
503	    sqz.replace(cmd, "").into_owned()
504	}
505	
506	// ─── Script file scanning ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
507	// When an interpreter runs a script file, read it and check each line against
508	// deny/ask patterns. Handles shell, Python, JS/TS, Perl, and Lua files.
509	// Skips inline-execution flags (-c, -m, -e). Unreadable paths fail gracefully.
510	
511	fn path_basename(path: &str) -> &str {
512	    path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path)
513	}
514	
515	fn extract_script_path(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
516	    let interp = r"(?i)(?:sudo\s+)?(?:bash|sh|zsh|dash|python3?|node|deno|perl|ruby|lua[0-9.]*)";
517	
518	    // Input redirection: bash < /path/to/script
519	    let redir_re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+<\s+(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
520	    if let Some(caps) = redir_re.captures(command) {
521	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
522	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
523	            return Some(path.to_string());
524	        }
525	    }
526	
527	    // source / dot-source (issue #33): `source <path>` and `. <path>` execute a
528	    // script in the current shell.  The dot form requires whitespace after the dot
529	    // so that `./foo` (direct exec, handled below) is NOT matched here.
530	    // Pattern: `^\s*(?:source|\.)\s+(\S+)` — the `\.` branch requires at least one
531	    // space after the dot, so `./foo` (dot immediately followed by `/`) is excluded.
532	    let source_re = Regex::new(r"(?i)^\s*(?:source|\.)\s+(\S+)").unwrap();
533	    if let Some(caps) = source_re.captures(command) {
534	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
535	        // Exclude `./foo` and `../foo` — those have the slash immediately after dot and
536	        // are direct-exec, handled by the direct_re below. The `source_re` already
537	        // requires at least one space between dot and path, so `./foo` won't match;
538	        // but defensively skip if the captured token starts with `/` only when there
539	        // was no whitespace (impossible given the regex, but belt-and-suspenders).
540	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
541	            return Some(path.to_string());
542	        }
543	    }
544	
545	    // Direct execution: ./script or ./script.sh — bash honours shebang, ignores extension
546	    let direct_re = Regex::new(r"(?i)^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(\./\S+)").unwrap();
547	    if let Some(caps) = direct_re.captures(command) {
548	        let path_str = caps[1].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
549	        if let Some(path) = path_str.split_whitespace().next() {
550	            return Some(path.to_string());
551	        }
552	    }
553	
554	    // Absolute-path direct execution (issue #35): `/tmp/evil.sh arg` or
555	    // `/home/user/deploy.py` — first token is an absolute path with a known
556	    // script extension.  Be conservative: only match script extensions to avoid
557	    // scanning `/usr/bin/ls -la` etc.
558	    let abs_re =
559	        Regex::new(r#"(?i)^\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(/\S+\.(?:sh|bash|py|js|mjs|ts|rb|pl|lua))(\s|$)"#)
560	            .unwrap();
561	    if let Some(caps) = abs_re.captures(command) {
562	        return Some(caps[1].to_string());
563	    }
564	
565	    // Standard: interpreter [optional-flags] <path>
566	    let re = Regex::new(&format!(r"(?i)^\s*{}\s+((?:-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*)(.+)$", interp)).unwrap();
567	    let caps = re.captures(command)?;
568	    let flags = &caps[1];
569	    // -c  → shell/python inline command string
570	    // -m  → python module (e.g. python3 -m pytest)
571	    // -e / --eval → node inline eval
572	    if Regex::new(r"(?:^|\s)-[a-zA-Z]*[cme][a-zA-Z]*(\s|$)")
573	        .unwrap()
574	        .is_match(flags)
575	    {
576	        return None;
577	    }
578	    let path_str = caps[2].trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('\'');
579	    // First token only — ignore script arguments after the path
580	    let path = path_str.split_whitespace().next()?;
581	    Some(path.to_string())
582	}
583	
584	fn scan_script_file(
585	    path: &str,
586	    deny_pats: &[Pattern],
587	    ask_pats: &[Pattern],
588	    allow_pats: &[Pattern],
589	) -> Option<(String, String)> {
590	    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
591	    let is_js = path.ends_with(".js")
592	        || path.ends_with(".mjs")
593	        || path.ends_with(".ts")
594	        || path.ends_with(".tsx");
595	    let is_lua = path.ends_with(".lua");
596	    let mut in_block_comment = false;
597	
598	    for (lineno, raw_line) in content.lines().enumerate() {
599	        let line = raw_line.trim();
600	        if line.is_empty() {
601	            continue;
602	        }
603	
604	        // JS/TS block comment state: /* ... */
605	        if is_js {
606	            if in_block_comment {
607	                if line.contains("*/") {
608	                    in_block_comment = false;
609	                }
610	                continue;
611	            }
612	            if line.starts_with("/*") {
613	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("*/");
614	                continue;
615	            }
616	            if line.starts_with("//") || line.starts_with('*') {
617	                continue;
618	            }
619	        }
620	
621	        // Lua comment state: --[[ ... ]] block comments and -- line comments
622	        if is_lua {
623	            if in_block_comment {
624	                if line.contains("]]") {
625	                    in_block_comment = false;
626	                }
627	                continue;
628	            }
629	            if line.starts_with("--[[") {
630	                in_block_comment = !line.contains("]]");
631	                continue;
632	            }
633	            if line.starts_with("--") {
634	                continue;
635	            }
636	        }
637	
638	        // Shell (#) and Python (#) and Perl (#) line comments
639	        if line.starts_with('#') {
640	            continue;
641	        }
642	
643	        // Reuse compound-command splitting so `foo && rm -rf /` is caught
644	        let clean = strip_safe_pipes(line);
645	        for segment in &split_segments(&clean) {
646	            if allow_pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(segment)) {
647	                continue;
648	            }
649	            for pat in deny_pats {
650	                if pat.matches(segment) {
651	                    return Some((
652	                        "deny".into(),
653	                        with_suggestion(
654	                            format!(
655	                                "Blocked: '{}' in {}:{}: {}",
656	                                pat.label,
657	                                path,
658	                                lineno + 1,
659	                                segment
660	                            ),
661	                            &pat.label,
662	                        ),
663	                    ));
664	                }
665	            }
666	            for pat in ask_pats {
667	                if pat.matches(segment) {
668	                    return Some((
669	                        "ask".into(),
670	                        with_suggestion(
671	                            format!(
672	                                "Review before running — '{}' in {}:{}: {}\nTo always allow: clawband allow '{}'",
673	                                pat.label, path, lineno + 1, segment, pat.label
674	                            ),
675	                            &pat.label,
676	                        ),
677	                    ));
678	                }
679	            }
680	        }
681	    }
682	    None
683	}
684	
685	// ─── Git force push check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
686	
687	fn check_force_push(cmd: &str) -> Option<String> {
688	    // Only applies to git push commands
689	    if !Regex::new(r"(?i)\bgit\s+push\b").unwrap().is_match(cmd) {
690	        return None;
691	    }
692	    // Strip --force-with-lease (safe alternative) first
693	    let strip_fwl = Regex::new(r"(?i)--force-with-lease(?:=\S+)?").unwrap();
694	    let cleaned = strip_fwl.replace_all(cmd, "");
695	    // Then block --force or -f anywhere in the command
696	    if Regex::new(r"(?i)\s--force(\s|$)|\s-f(\s|$)")
697	        .unwrap()
698	        .is_match(&cleaned)
699	    {
700	        Some("Blocked: git push --force / -f (use --force-with-lease instead)".into())
701	    } else {
702	        None
703	    }
704	}
705	
706	// ─── Safe inline pipe stripping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
707	// Remove  | python3 -c "..."  and  | python3 -m mod  before pipe checks.
708	// These are visible inline code, not supply-chain risks.
709	
710	fn strip_safe_pipes(cmd: &str) -> String {
711	    let c = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-c\s+[^|;&`$]*").unwrap();
712	    let m = Regex::new(r"(?i)\|\s*(python3?|node)\s+-m\s+\S+").unwrap();
713	    let s = c.replace_all(cmd, "");
714	    m.replace_all(&s, "").into_owned()
715	}
716	
717	// ─── Compound command splitting ───────────────────────────────────────────────
718	// Split on &&, ||, ; and newlines.
719	// Single | is NOT a splitter — keeps pipe-to-interpreter in one segment.
720	// \; and \| are escaped before splitting so find -exec and regex patterns survive.
721	
722	fn split_segments(cmd: &str) -> Vec<String> {
723	    const ESC_SEMI: &str = "\x01S\x01";
724	    const ESC_PIPE: &str = "\x01P\x01";
725	    const SEP: &str = "\x01SEP\x01";
726	
727	    let s = cmd.replace("\\;", ESC_SEMI).replace("\\|", ESC_PIPE);
728	
729	    let splitter = Regex::new(r"[ \t]*(\|\||&&|;|\n)[ \t]*").unwrap();
730	    let s = splitter.replace_all(&s, SEP);
731	
732	    s.split(SEP)
733	        .map(|seg| seg.trim().replace(ESC_SEMI, "\\;").replace(ESC_PIPE, "\\|"))
734	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
735	        .collect()
736	}
737	
738	// ─── PostToolUse breadcrumb ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
739	// Written by PreToolUse when decision is "ask". Read and deleted by `clawband post`
740	// (PostToolUse hook). If the command ran, PostToolUse fires and we know the user
741	// approved. If denied, PostToolUse never fires and the breadcrumb expires via TTL.
742	
743	fn breadcrumb_path() -> PathBuf {
744	    config_dir().join(".last-ask")
745	}
746	
747	fn write_ask_breadcrumb(reason: &str) {
748	    let cfg = config_dir();
749	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
750	    let ts = std::time::SystemTime::now()
751	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
752	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
753	        .unwrap_or(0);
754	    if let Ok(mut f) = fs::OpenOptions::new()
755	        .write(true)
756	        .create(true)
757	        .truncate(true)
758	        .open(breadcrumb_path())
759	    {
760	        let _ = writeln!(f, "{}\n{}", ts, reason);
761	    }
762	}
763	
764	fn cmd_post() {
765	    let path = breadcrumb_path();
766	    let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
767	        return;
768	    };
769	    let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
770	
771	    let mut lines = content.lines();
772	    let ts: u64 = lines.next().and_then(|l| l.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
773	
774	    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
775	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
776	        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
777	        .unwrap_or(0);
778	    if now.saturating_sub(ts) > 60 {
779	        return;
780	    }
781	
782	    let reason: String = lines.collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
783	
784	    // Extract "clawband allow '<label>'" from the hint line if present.
785	    if let Some(pos) = reason.find("clawband allow '") {
786	        let snippet = reason[pos..].lines().next().unwrap_or("").trim();
787	        println!(
788	            "The user approved a clawband-prompted command. \
789	             Suggest they run `{}` to stop being prompted for this in future.",
790	            snippet
791	        );
792	    }
793	}
794	
795	// ─── Allow / deny commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
796	
797	fn cmd_add_pattern(file: &str, args: &[String]) {
798	    if args.is_empty() {
799	        eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
800	        std::process::exit(1);
801	    }
802	
803	    let (use_project, pattern_args) = if args[0] == "--project" {
804	        if args.len() < 2 {
805	            eprintln!("Usage: clawband allow|deny [--project] <pattern>");
806	            std::process::exit(1);
807	        }
808	        (true, &args[1..])
809	    } else {
810	        (false, args)
811	    };
812	
813	    let pattern = pattern_args.join(" ");
814	
815	    if Pattern::from_user(&pattern).is_none() {
816	        eprintln!("clawband: invalid regex: {}", pattern);
817	        std::process::exit(1);
818	    }
819	
820	    let cfg = if use_project {
821	        PathBuf::from(env::var("PWD").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string())).join(".clawband")
822	    } else {
823	        config_dir()
824	    };
825	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
826	    let path = cfg.join(file);
827	
828	    match fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true).open(&path) {
829	        Ok(mut f) => {
830	            let _ = writeln!(f, "{}", pattern);
831	            let g = "\x1b[32m";
832	            let b = "\x1b[34m";
833	            let r = "\x1b[0m";
834	            let bold = "\x1b[1m";
835	            println!(
836	                "{}Added{} {}{}{} → {}{}{}",
837	                g,
838	                r,
839	                bold,
840	                pattern,
841	                r,
842	                b,
843	                path.display(),
844	                r
845	            );
846	        }
847	        Err(e) => {
848	            eprintln!("clawband: failed to write {}: {}", path.display(), e);
849	            std::process::exit(1);
850	        }
851	    }
852	}

854	// ─── Protected-paths config ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
855	
856	/// Expand a leading `~/` or `~` to `$HOME/`.
857	fn expand_home(s: &str) -> String {
858	    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
859	    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix("~/") {
860	        format!("{}/{}", home, rest)
861	    } else if s == "~" {
862	        home
863	    } else {
864	        s.to_string()
865	    }
866	}
867	
868	/// Load protect.paths from a directory.  Each line is a case-insensitive regex
869	/// matched against the absolute target file path.  A leading `~/` is expanded
870	/// to `$HOME/` before compilation.
871	fn load_protect_patterns(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<Pattern> {
872	    let path = dir.join("protect.paths");
873	    let Ok(text) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
874	        return vec![];
875	    };
876	    text.lines()
877	        .map(str::trim)
878	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))
879	        .map(expand_home)
880	        .filter_map(|l| Pattern::from_user(&l))
881	        .collect()
882	}
883	
884	/// Collect protect patterns from global (~/.clawband/) and project (.clawband/)
885	/// protect.paths files.
886	fn protect_patterns() -> Vec<Pattern> {
887	    let mut pats = load_protect_patterns(&config_dir());
888	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
889	        pats.extend(load_protect_patterns(&proj));
890	    }
891	    pats
892	}
893	
894	/// Returns true if at least one protect.paths file exists (global or project).
895	fn protect_active() -> bool {
896	    let global = config_dir().join("protect.paths");
897	    if global.exists() {
898	        return true;
899	    }
900	    if let Some(proj) = project_config_dir() {
901	        if proj.join("protect.paths").exists() {
902	            return true;
903	        }
904	    }
905	    false
906	}

908	/// Check whether an edit target path matches any protect pattern.
909	/// Pure helper (testable without env/FS — pass patterns in directly).
910	fn edit_protected(path: &str, pats: &[Pattern]) -> bool {
911	    pats.iter().any(|p| p.matches(path))
912	}
913	
914	/// Resolve symlinks for an edit target, returning a list of candidate paths to
915	/// check against protect patterns.  The original expanded-absolute path is
916	/// always first; the canonicalized path (symlinks resolved, `..` collapsed) is
917	/// added as a second candidate when it differs.  For a path that doesn't exist
918	/// yet (e.g. a new file being created), we canonicalize the parent directory
919	/// and re-append the filename so that a symlinked parent is still resolved.
920	fn edit_candidates(abs_path: &str) -> Vec<String> {
921	    let mut candidates: Vec<String> = vec![abs_path.to_string()];
922	    let p = std::path::Path::new(abs_path);
923	
924	    let canon = if p.exists() {
925	        fs::canonicalize(p).ok()
926	    } else {
927	        // Path doesn't exist yet — canonicalize its parent and re-join the filename
928	        p.parent()
929	            .and_then(|parent| fs::canonicalize(parent).ok())
930	            .and_then(|canon_parent| p.file_name().map(|name| canon_parent.join(name)))
931	    };
932	
933	    if let Some(c) = canon {
934	        let cs = c.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
935	        if cs != abs_path {
936	            candidates.push(cs);
937	        }
938	    }
939	
940	    candidates
941	}
942	
943	/// Self-protect deny patterns added to the Bash check when protect_active().
944	/// These block shell commands that would tamper with clawband's own files.
945	/// They are anchored to specific file locations so they do NOT match
946	/// `brew upgrade clawband`, `clawband install`, or `bash install.sh`.
947	fn self_protect_deny_patterns() -> Vec<Pattern> {
948	    let specs: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
949	        // rm / mv / shred / truncate referencing clawband files
950	        (
951	            "rm clawband hook",
952	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred)\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
953	        ),
954	        (
955	            "rm clawband settings",
956	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred)\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
957	        ),
958	        (
959	            "rm clawband dir",
960	            r"\b(?:rm|mv|shred|truncate)\b[^|;&\n]*\.clawband/",
961	        ),
962	        (
963	            "truncate clawband hook",
964	            r"\btruncate\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
965	        ),
966	        (
967	            "truncate clawband settings",
968	            r"\btruncate\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
969	        ),
970	        // Output redirection > or >> to clawband files
971	        (
972	            "redirect to clawband hook",
973	            r">+\s*[^\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
974	        ),
975	        (
976	            "redirect to clawband settings",
977	            r">+\s*[^\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
978	        ),
979	        // sed -i targeting settings.json
980	        (
981	            "sed -i clawband settings",
982	            r"\bsed\b[^|;&\n]*-i[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
983	        ),
984	        // tee targeting settings.json
985	        (
986	            "tee clawband settings",
987	            r"\btee\b[^|;&\n]*\.claude/settings\.json\b",
988	        ),
989	        // chmod -x removing execute from the hook binary
990	        (
991	            "chmod -x clawband hook",
992	            r"\bchmod\b[^|;&\n]*-[a-zA-Z]*x[^|;&\n]*\.claude/hooks/clawband\b",
993	        ),
994	    ];
995	    specs.iter().map(|(l, p)| Pattern::builtin(l, p)).collect()
996	}

999	
1000	const DENY_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../deny.patterns.example");
1001	const ASK_EXAMPLE: &str = include_str!("../ask.patterns.example");
1002	const ALLOW_TEMPLATE: &str = "# allow.patterns — patterns that override deny/ask blocks\n\
1003	# One pattern per line. Case-insensitive regex. Lines starting with # ignored.\n\
1004	#\n\
1005	# Example: allow git reset --hard only to HEAD\n\
1006	# git reset --hard HEAD$\n";
1007	
1008	const CONFIG_TEMPLATE: &str = "# clawband config\n\
1009	#\n\
1010	# What clawband decides for a command that matches NO deny/ask/allow pattern:\n\
1011	#   passthrough  (default) — stay silent; Claude Code's native permission check handles it\n\
1012	#   allow                  — emit `allow` so clawband is the sole gatekeeper (no native prompts)\n\
1013	#   ask                    — review everything not explicitly allowed\n\
1014	# Note: a hook `ask` only prompts when NOT in bypassPermissions mode; in YOLO mode `ask` runs.\n\
1015	default_decision = passthrough\n";
1016	
1017	const PROTECT_PATHS_TEMPLATE: &str =
1018	    "# protect.paths — clawband denies Write/Edit (and tamper Bash ops) on matching paths.\n\
1019	# One regex per line, matched case-insensitively against the absolute file path.\n\
1020	# A leading ~/ is expanded to your home directory.\n\
1021	~/.claude/settings\\.json$\n\
1022	~/.claude/hooks/clawband$\n\
1023	~/.clawband/.*\n\
1024	# Shell startup files — block injecting CLAWBAND_SKIP=1 (or hook removal) here.\n\
1025	~/\\.(bash_profile|bashrc|profile|zshrc|zprofile|zshenv)$\n";
1026	
1027	fn settings_path() -> PathBuf {
1028	    PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default()).join(".claude/settings.json")
1029	}
1030	
1031	// The command string to register in settings.json. Prefer the bare name when
1032	// clawband is resolvable on PATH (stable across Homebrew upgrades); otherwise
1033	// fall back to the absolute path of the running binary.
1034	fn hook_command_string() -> String {
1035	    if let Ok(exe) = env::current_exe() {
1036	        if let Ok(canon_exe) = fs::canonicalize(&exe) {
1037	            if let Ok(path) = env::var("PATH") {
1038	                for dir in path.split(':') {
1039	                    let candidate = PathBuf::from(dir).join("clawband");
1040	                    if let Ok(canon) = fs::canonicalize(&candidate) {
1041	                        if canon == canon_exe {
1042	                            return "clawband".to_string();
1043	                        }
1044	                    }
1045	                }
1046	            }
1047	        }
1048	        return exe.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
1049	    }
1050	    "clawband".to_string()
1051	}
1052	
1053	// Precisely identifies the clawband MAIN hook command — by executable basename,
1054	// not substring. Excludes the `clawband post` companion. Robust against paths
1055	// that happen to contain "icm"/"sqz" and against bare vs absolute forms.
1056	fn is_clawband_main_command(cmd: &str) -> bool {
1057	    let mut toks = cmd.split_whitespace();
1058	    let Some(first) = toks.next() else {
1059	        return false;
1060	    };
1061	    let base = first.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(first);
1062	    if base != "clawband" {
1063	        return false;
1064	    }
1065	    // `clawband post` is the PostToolUse companion, not the main hook
1066	    toks.next() != Some("post")
1067	}
1068	
1069	// Returns true if at least one clawband main hook is registered anywhere in PreToolUse.
1070	fn clawband_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
1071	    settings["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
1072	        .as_array()
1073	        .map(|entries| {
1074	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
1075	                e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
1076	                    hooks
1077	                        .iter()
1078	                        .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
1079	                })
1080	            })
1081	        })
1082	        .unwrap_or(false)
1083	}
1084	
1085	// Register the clawband PreToolUse hook, normalising to exactly one instance.
1086	// - Removes every existing clawband main hook (self-heals duplicates), dropping
1087	//   any entry left empty.
1088	// - Re-adds a single hook: prepended into an existing `Bash` matcher entry if one
1089	//   exists (so clawband runs first and there's no parallel Bash section), else a
1090	//   new entry at the front.
1091	// Returns true if the resulting settings differ from the input (i.e. a write is
1092	// warranted), false if it was already correct (idempotent).
1093	fn register_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
1094	    use serde_json::json;
1095	    if !settings.is_object() {
1096	        *settings = json!({});
1097	    }
1098	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
1099	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
1100	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
1101	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
1102	    }
1103	    let pre_val = hooks_obj
1104	        .as_object_mut()
1105	        .unwrap()
1106	        .entry("PreToolUse")
1107	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
1108	    if !pre_val.is_array() {
1109	        *pre_val = json!([]);
1110	    }
1111	    let before = pre_val.clone();
1112	    let pre = pre_val.as_array_mut().unwrap();
1113	
1114	    // Strip all existing clawband main hooks from every entry.
1115	    for entry in pre.iter_mut() {
1116	        if let Some(hs) = entry["hooks"].as_array_mut() {
1117	            hs.retain(|h| !h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command));
1118	        }
1119	    }
1120	    // Drop entries whose hooks array is now empty (e.g. a former clawband-only entry).
1121	    pre.retain(|e| e["hooks"].as_array().map(|h| !h.is_empty()).unwrap_or(true));
1122	
1123	    let hook = json!({"type": "command", "command": command});
1124	    // Prefer merging into an existing Bash matcher entry over a parallel section.
1125	    if let Some(bash) = pre
1126	        .iter_mut()
1127	        .find(|e| e["matcher"].as_str() == Some("Bash") && e["hooks"].is_array())
1128	    {
1129	        bash["hooks"].as_array_mut().unwrap().insert(0, hook);
1130	    } else {
1131	        pre.insert(0, json!({"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [hook]}));
1132	    }
1133	
1134	    *pre_val != before
1135	}
1136	
1137	/// Register a second PreToolUse hook entry with matcher "Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"
1138	/// pointing at the same clawband main command.  Idempotent — does nothing if an entry
1139	/// whose matcher contains "Edit" already has a clawband main command.
1140	/// Returns true if the settings were modified.
1141	fn register_edit_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
1142	    use serde_json::json;
1143	    if !settings.is_object() {
1144	        *settings = json!({});
1145	    }
1146	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
1147	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
1148	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
1149	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
1150	    }
1151	    let pre_val = hooks_obj
1152	        .as_object_mut()
1153	        .unwrap()
1154	        .entry("PreToolUse")
1155	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
1156	    if !pre_val.is_array() {
1157	        *pre_val = json!([]);
1158	    }
1159	    let before = pre_val.clone();
1160	    let pre = pre_val.as_array_mut().unwrap();
1161	
1162	    // Check if an entry with an "Edit"-containing matcher already has a clawband main command.
1163	    let already = pre.iter().any(|e| {
1164	        let matcher = e["matcher"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
1165	        matcher.contains("Edit")
1166	            && e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
1167	                hooks
1168	                    .iter()
1169	                    .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
1170	            })
1171	    });
1172	    if already {
1173	        return false;
1174	    }
1175	
1176	    let hook = json!({"type": "command", "command": command});
1177	    pre.push(json!({"matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit", "hooks": [hook]}));
1178	
1179	    *pre_val != before
1180	}
1181	
1182	/// True if a command is the clawband PostToolUse companion (`clawband post`).
1183	fn is_clawband_post_command(cmd: &str) -> bool {
1184	    let mut toks = cmd.split_whitespace();
1185	    let Some(first) = toks.next() else {
1186	        return false;
1187	    };
1188	    let base = first.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(first);
1189	    base == "clawband" && toks.next() == Some("post")
1190	}
1191	
1192	/// True if the PostToolUse `clawband post` hook is registered.
1193	fn post_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
1194	    settings["hooks"]["PostToolUse"]
1195	        .as_array()
1196	        .map(|entries| {
1197	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
1198	                e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
1199	                    hooks
1200	                        .iter()
1201	                        .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_post_command))
1202	                })
1203	            })
1204	        })
1205	        .unwrap_or(false)
1206	}
1207	
1208	/// Register the PostToolUse `clawband post` hook (matcher Bash). Idempotent.
1209	fn register_post_hook(settings: &mut serde_json::Value, command: &str) -> bool {
1210	    use serde_json::json;
1211	    if post_hook_present(settings) {
1212	        return false;
1213	    }
1214	    if !settings.is_object() {
1215	        *settings = json!({});
1216	    }
1217	    let obj = settings.as_object_mut().unwrap();
1218	    let hooks_obj = obj.entry("hooks").or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
1219	    if !hooks_obj.is_object() {
1220	        *hooks_obj = json!({});
1221	    }
1222	    let post_val = hooks_obj
1223	        .as_object_mut()
1224	        .unwrap()
1225	        .entry("PostToolUse")
1226	        .or_insert_with(|| json!([]));
1227	    if !post_val.is_array() {
1228	        *post_val = json!([]);
1229	    }
1230	    post_val
1231	        .as_array_mut()
1232	        .unwrap()
1233	        .push(json!({"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": command}]}));
1234	    true
1235	}
1236	
1237	/// Returns true if the Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit protect hook is registered.
1238	fn edit_hook_present(settings: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {
1239	    settings["hooks"]["PreToolUse"]
1240	        .as_array()
1241	        .map(|entries| {
1242	            entries.iter().any(|e| {
1243	                let matcher = e["matcher"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
1244	                matcher.contains("Edit")
1245	                    && e["hooks"].as_array().is_some_and(|hooks| {
1246	                        hooks
1247	                            .iter()
1248	                            .any(|h| h["command"].as_str().is_some_and(is_clawband_main_command))
1249	                    })
1250	            })
1251	        })
1252	        .unwrap_or(false)
1253	}

1255	fn cmd_install(extra_args: &[String]) {
1256	    let protect = extra_args.iter().any(|a| a == "--protect");
1257	    let post = extra_args.iter().any(|a| a == "--post");
1258	
1259	    let g = "\x1b[32m";
1260	    let y = "\x1b[33m";
1261	    let d = "\x1b[2m";
1262	    let r = "\x1b[0m";
1263	    let bold = "\x1b[1m";
1264	
1265	    // 1. Config dir + pattern templates
1266	    let cfg = config_dir();
1267	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&cfg);
1268	    let seed = |name: &str, content: &str| {
1269	        let p = cfg.join(name);
1270	        if p.exists() {
1271	            println!("  {d}exists{r}  {}", p.display());
1272	        } else if fs::write(&p, content).is_ok() {
1273	            println!("  {g}created{r} {}", p.display());
1274	        } else {
1275	            println!("  {y}failed{r} {}", p.display());
1276	        }
1277	    };
1278	    println!("{bold}Config{r}");
1279	    seed("deny.patterns", DENY_EXAMPLE);
1280	    seed("ask.patterns", ASK_EXAMPLE);
1281	    seed("allow.patterns", ALLOW_TEMPLATE);
1282	    seed("config", CONFIG_TEMPLATE);
1283	
1284	    // 2. Wire settings.json
1285	    println!("\n{bold}Hook{r}");
1286	    let path = settings_path();
1287	    let _ = fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap_or(&PathBuf::from(".")));
1288	    let mut settings: serde_json::Value = fs::read_to_string(&path)
1289	        .ok()
1290	        .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
1291	        .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({}));
1292	
1293	    let command = hook_command_string();
1294	    if register_hook(&mut settings, &command) {
1295	        match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&settings) {
1296	            Ok(out) => {
1297	                if fs::write(&path, out + "\n").is_ok() {
1298	                    println!(
1299	                        "  {g}registered{r} PreToolUse Bash hook → {d}{}{r}",
1300	                        command
1301	                    );
1302	                    println!("  {d}in {}{r}", path.display());
1303	                } else {
1304	                    println!("  {y}failed to write {}{r}", path.display());
1305	                }
1306	            }
1307	            Err(_) => println!("  {y}failed to serialize settings{r}"),
1308	        }
1309	    } else {
1310	        println!("  {d}already registered in {}{r}", path.display());
1311	    }
1312	
1313	    // 3. Self-protect (--protect flag)
1314	    if protect {
1315	        println!("\n{bold}Self-protect{r}");
1316	
1317	        // Seed protect.paths if missing
1318	        let pp = cfg.join("protect.paths");
1319	        if pp.exists() {
1320	            println!("  {d}exists{r}  {}", pp.display());
1321	        } else if fs::write(&pp, PROTECT_PATHS_TEMPLATE).is_ok() {
1322	            println!("  {g}created{r} {}", pp.display());
1323	        } else {
1324	            println!("  {y}failed{r} to create {}", pp.display());
1325	        }
1326	
1327	        // Re-read settings (may have been written above)
1328	        let mut settings2: serde_json::Value = fs::read_to_string(&path)
1329	            .ok()
1330	            .and_then(|s| serde_json::from_str(&s).ok())
1331	            .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!({}));
1332	
1333	        if register_edit_hook(&mut settings2, &command) {
1334	            match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&settings2) {
1335	                Ok(out) => {
1336	                    if fs::write(&path, out + "\n").is_ok() {
1337	                        println!(
1338	                            "  {g}registered{r} PreToolUse Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit hook → {d}{}{r}",
1339	                            command
1340	                        );
1341	                    } else {
1342	                        println!("  {y}failed to write {}{r}", path.display());
1343	                    }
1344	                }
1345	                Err(_) => println!("  {y}failed to serialize settings{r}"),
1346	            }
1347	        } else {
1348	            println!("  {d}edit hook already registered{r}");
1349	        }
1350	
1351	        println!();
1352	        println!("  Self-protect is now active.");
1353	        println!("  Claude's Write/Edit tools are guarded against modifying protected paths.");
1354	        println!("  Your own terminal is unaffected — only Claude Code's tools are guarded.");
1355	        println!(
1356	            "  Edit {}{}/protect.paths{r} to customise protected paths.",
1357	            d,
1358	            cfg.display(),
1359	            r = r
1360	        );
1361	    }
1362	
1363	    // 4. PostToolUse companion (--post flag)
1364	    if post {
1365	        println!("\n{bold}PostToolUse companion{r}");
```
